paragraphs.ca: Diré que, per a la major part de la població, aprenem a un ritme força semblant. Tanmateix, hi ha factors que difereixen entre les persones i que afecten el ritme de progrés: com ens concentrem en una tasca, les preguntes que ens fem mentre aprenem, la quantitat de temps que dediquem a una tasca, la mentalitat amb què afrontem una tasca, el nostre entorn quan aprenem.

paragraphs.en: Do you think Steve Vai picks four notes, then neurotically worries that he did it wrong and spends three hours googling the right way to do it?
paragraphs.ca: Creus que Steve Vai agafa quatre notes i després es preocupa neuròticament per si ho ha fet malament i passa tres hores buscant a Google la manera correcta de fer-ho?

paragraphs.en: Or do you think he just gets on with it? While I can't say for sure, I'm guessing it's the latter. Did Ingui Malmsteen play the guitar for ten minutes a day?
paragraphs.ca: O creus que simplement tira endavant? No puc assegurar-ho, però diria que és el segon cas. Yngwie Malmsteen tocava la guitarra deu minuts al dia?

paragraphs.en: Or did he practice relentlessly, skipping school and falling asleep with his guitar? These areas are all areas that we can actively improve to learn guitar faster and reach higher levels of playing. When it comes down to it, we all learn at pretty much the same rate. By improving the above areas, we accelerate our rate of progress.
paragraphs.ca: O practicava sense descans, saltant-se l'escola i adormint-se amb la guitarra a les mans? Tots aquests són aspectes que podem millorar activament per aprendre guitarra més de pressa i arribar a nivells de tocada més alts. Al capdavall, tots aprenem més o menys al mateix ritme. Millorant els aspectes anteriors, accelerem el nostre ritme de progrés.

paragraphs.en: I get what you're saying, but what if I do learn slowly? There is one response and two solutions to this problem. The first is you have to look at this like a mathematical equation.
paragraphs.ca: Entenc què vols dir, però i si jo aprenc lentament? Hi ha una resposta i dues solucions per a aquest problema. La primera és que ho has de mirar com una equació matemàtica.

paragraphs.en: If you learn slowly, then you can still achieve high levels of playing by putting in more practice time, which is high-quality practice.
paragraphs.ca: Si aprens lentament, encara pots arribar a nivells alts de tocada dedicant-hi més temps de pràctica, i que aquesta sigui pràctica de qualitat.

paragraphs.en: Therefore, plan out ways to increase your practice time on guitar, and you can still achieve high levels of playing. So what if you learn slowly? It doesn't matter.
paragraphs.ca: Per tant, planifica maneres d'augmentar el teu temps de pràctica de guitarra i encara podràs assolir nivells alts de tocada. I què passa si aprens lentament? No importa.

paragraphs.en: The second way is to find a great teacher to help you. You might have to sift through a few different teachers to find one that works well for you.
paragraphs.ca: La segona manera és trobar un bon professor que t'ajudi. Potser hauràs de provar uns quants professors diferents fins a trobar-ne un que et vagi bé.

paragraphs.en: Having someone give you advice and feedback, answer your questions, and help make sure that you correctly understand and practice various topics and have a plan for doing so, is a great way to accelerate your progress on the guitar.
paragraphs.ca: Tenir algú que et doni consells i retroalimentació, que respongui les teves preguntes i que t'ajudi a assegurar-te que entens i practiques correctament diversos temes i que tens un pla per fer-ho és una manera excel·lent d'accelerar el teu progrés amb la guitarra.

paragraphs.en: But the truth of the matter is, you don't learn slowly. Every second you spend considering that thought is one you could have spent practicing and improving.
paragraphs.ca: Però la veritat és que no aprens lentament. Cada segon que passes donant voltes a aquest pensament és un segon que podries haver passat practicant i millorant.

paragraphs.en: Ironically, worrying that you are a slow learner will slow down your learning. Next time you catch yourself worrying about whether or not you are a slow learner, pinch yourself, literally, and just get back to practicing the guitar.
paragraphs.ca: Irònicament, preocupar-te pel fet de ser un aprenent lent alentirà el teu aprenentatge. La propera vegada que et trobis preocupat per si ets o no un aprenent lent, fes-te una pessigada, literalment, i torna a practicar la guitarra.

paragraphs.en: Talent myth 3. Expert amnesia Sometimes talented people themselves spread the myth of talent. Have you ever watched instructional DVDs of great guitar players?
paragraphs.ca: Mite del talent 3. L'amnèsia de l'expert. De vegades són les mateixes persones amb talent qui escampen el mite del talent. Has mirat mai DVD didàctics de grans guitarristes?

paragraphs.en: I know I have. Sometimes these DVDs really suck. Let me clarify. These DVDs have awesome licks and great ideas to work on, but they rarely explain how to play those awesome ideas.
paragraphs.ca: Jo sí que n'he mirat. De vegades aquests DVD són realment dolents. Deixa'm que ho aclareixi. Aquests DVD tenen licks fantàstics i grans idees per treballar, però poques vegades expliquen com tocar aquestes idees fantàstiques.

paragraphs.en: When some guitar players are asked how to play XYZ lick, they say, just do it. When they are asked how they learned, they say they just did it.
paragraphs.ca: Quan es pregunta a alguns guitarristes com tocar tal o tal lick, diuen: «doncs fes-ho». Quan se'ls pregunta com ho van aprendre, diuen que simplement ho van fer.

paragraphs.en: And boom, the myth of natural talent has new life. However, this is not quite true. This is an effect referred to as expert amnesia.
paragraphs.ca: I bum, el mite del talent natural té vida nova. Tanmateix, això no és del tot cert. És un efecte que s'anomena amnèsia de l'expert.

paragraphs.en: This is when someone has reached an incredibly high level of ability and cannot remember what it is like to be at a lower level. This is why sometimes high-level guitar players struggle to effectively teach beginner guitar players because it is incredibly difficult for them to understand things from the beginner's perspective. You may have experienced this yourself when taking lessons.
paragraphs.ca: Es dóna quan algú ha arribat a un nivell de capacitat increïblement alt i no pot recordar com era estar en un nivell inferior. Per això de vegades els guitarristes de nivell alt tenen dificultats per ensenyar eficaçment a guitarristes principiants: perquè els resulta increïblement difícil entendre les coses des de la perspectiva del principiant. Potser ho has viscut tu mateix quan has fet classes.

paragraphs.en: A teacher may give you something and tell you to play it, you struggle, and then they get frustrated with you. I have one student who had a previous teacher tell her that she probably wouldn't be able to play the guitar. She now writes her own music, can freely improvise across a variety of scales, and is studying counterpoint. The problem wasn't her natural ability to play the guitar, it was that things were not sufficiently explained to her. The effect of expert amnesia occurs
paragraphs.ca: Un professor et pot donar una cosa i dir-te que la toquis, tu hi vas amb dificultats i llavors ell s'impacienta amb tu. Tinc una alumna a qui un professor anterior li va dir que probablement no seria capaç de tocar la guitarra. Ara escriu la seva pròpia música, improvisa lliurement amb diverses escales i estudia contrapunt. El problema no era la seva capacitat natural per tocar la guitarra, sinó que no se li van explicar prou bé les coses. L'efecte de l'amnèsia de l'expert es produeix

paragraphs.en: partially due to the nature of how our minds work and how we learn. Additionally, this is not to say that all high-level guitar players are bad teachers. Expert amnesia, epistemology, and tying your shoelaces. Let's talk briefly about how we learn. We learn by taking simple ideas and integrating them into concepts. Then we learn more advanced ideas and skills by integrating concepts. For example, we learn to identify the color brown, to identify the texture of wood and how to
paragraphs.ca: en part per la naturalesa de com funciona la nostra ment i de com aprenem. A més, això no vol dir que tots els guitarristes de nivell alt siguin mals professors. L'amnèsia de l'expert, l'epistemologia i cordar-se les sabates. Parlem breument de com aprenem. Aprenem agafant idees simples i integrant-les en conceptes. Després aprenem idees i habilitats més avançades integrant conceptes. Per exemple, aprenem a identificar el color marró, a identificar la textura de la fusta i a

paragraphs.en: distinguish shapes together. When we see a certain arrangement of this sensory data and we create the mental concept of a chair, we learn what a chair is, what a table is and what a bench is, and we integrate these low-level concepts to form a slightly higher-level concept of furniture.
paragraphs.ca: distingir formes alhora. Quan veiem una determinada disposició d'aquestes dades sensorials i creem el concepte mental de cadira, aprenem què és una cadira, què és una taula i què és un banc, i integrem aquests conceptes de nivell baix per formar un concepte una mica més elevat: el moble.

paragraphs.en: Learning guitar works the same way, but we have the added complexity of performing a physical action in addition to building mental concepts.
paragraphs.ca: Aprendre guitarra funciona de la mateixa manera, però hi ha la complexitat afegida d'executar una acció física a més de construir conceptes mentals.

paragraphs.en: There is a mechanical and a conceptual side to learning guitar, and they have to be worked on simultaneously. As a guitar example, to pick through a three-note-per-string scale, we have to train three separate skills.
paragraphs.ca: Hi ha una cara mecànica i una cara conceptual en aprendre guitarra, i s'han de treballar simultàniament. Com a exemple guitarristic, per fer pua en una escala de tres notes per corda hem d'entrenar tres habilitats separades.

paragraphs.en: 1. Picking notes on a single string. 2. Controlling how the pick travels between strings. 3. Visualizing the scale position on the guitar neck and then combine them to effectively pick through a scale Now, imagine it took you several months to master the two basic motions of picking on a single string controlling the movement of the pick between strings and visualizing guitar scales in different keys Then, you relentlessly shred scales for 20 years
paragraphs.ca: 1. Fer pua en notes d'una sola corda. 2. Controlar com viatja la pua entre les cordes. 3. Visualitzar la posició de l'escala al mànec de la guitarra, i després combinar-les per fer pua eficaçment en una escala. Ara imagina que vas trigar diversos mesos a dominar els dos moviments bàsics de fer pua en una sola corda, controlar el moviment de la pua entre les cordes i visualitzar escales de guitarra en tonalitats diferents. Llavors, durant 20 anys vas tocar escales a tota velocitat sense parar

paragraphs.en: It's easy to imagine that you might have forgotten what it was like to work on the fundamental building blocks of your technique.
paragraphs.ca: És fàcil imaginar que potser has oblidat com era treballar els elements fonamentals de la teva tècnica.

paragraphs.en: Another possibility is that the guitar player in question did not consciously distinguish between each element of picking through a scale.
paragraphs.ca: Una altra possibilitat és que el guitarrista en qüestió no distingís conscientment cada element de fer pua en una escala.

paragraphs.en: They just did it a million times until something clicked, and they found they were able to shred their scales. The advice someone in this situation would give, based on their experience, is that you just need to do it a million times.
paragraphs.ca: Simplement ho va fer un milió de vegades fins que alguna cosa va fer clic, i va descobrir que era capaç de tocar les seves escales a tota velocitat. El consell que donaria algú en aquesta situació, basant-se en la seva experiència, és que només cal fer-ho un milió de vegades.

paragraphs.en: And while there is certainly a strong element of repetition needed to develop a skill, consciously identifying the components of that skill and working on them individually, then integrating them will help you learn a lot, lot faster.
paragraphs.ca: I tot i que sens dubte cal un fort component de repetició per desenvolupar una habilitat, identificar conscientment els components d'aquesta habilitat i treballar-los individualment, i després integrar-los, t'ajudarà a aprendre molt, molt més de pressa.

paragraphs.en: You have expert amnesia, too. Take something you do every day, such as tying your shoelaces or brushing your teeth. Now, write out a list of instructions on how to do that action.
paragraphs.ca: Tu també tens amnèsia de l'expert. Agafa una cosa que facis cada dia, com cordar-te les sabates o raspallar-te les dents. Ara escriu una llista d'instruccions sobre com fer aquesta acció.

paragraphs.en: Finally, follow your instructions exactly. Would someone who had never performed that task before be able to follow your instructions and accomplish the task?
paragraphs.ca: Finalment, segueix les teves instruccions exactament. Algú que no hagués fet mai aquesta tasca seria capaç de seguir les teves instruccions i completar la tasca?

paragraphs.en: If you wrote something like, just do it, then the answer is no, and you have expert amnesia. If you take 10, 15 minutes, sat and thought, you could probably work out an effective list of instructions.
paragraphs.ca: Si has escrit una cosa com «doncs fes-ho», la resposta és no, i tens amnèsia de l'expert. Si dediques 10 o 15 minuts a seure i pensar-hi, probablement podries elaborar una llista d'instruccions efectiva.

paragraphs.en: You will probably find that your instructions need some testing to help you fully document the process of brushing your teeth.
paragraphs.ca: Probablement descobriràs que les teves instruccions necessiten una mica de prova per acabar de documentar del tot el procés de raspallar-te les dents.

paragraphs.en: Why do we get expert amnesia? A fundamental part of what our brains do, and what learning is, is automating. We consciously train a skill and over time, and with enough repetitions, we eventually automate that skill, forgetting the fundamental components of the skill and retaining the higher-level outlook.
paragraphs.ca: Per què tenim amnèsia de l'expert? Una part fonamental del que fan els nostres cervells, i del que és aprendre, és automatitzar. Entrenem conscientment una habilitat i, amb el temps i prou repeticions, finalment l'automatitzem, oblidant els components fonamentals de l'habilitat i conservant la visió de nivell superior.

paragraphs.en: As an example, we go from having to visualize the scale, move the pick between the strings, and carefully fret the notes to just playing a major scale. This is a natural and incredible feature of how our minds work, which allows us to work on higher level concepts and more advanced skills. Ideas and execution. This is quite a general idea we are going to look at. Someone can explain an idea to you, and that idea may take two minutes to explain. It could take two months
paragraphs.ca: Per exemple, passem d'haver de visualitzar l'escala, moure la pua entre les cordes i prémer amb cura les notes a simplement tocar una escala major. Aquesta és una característica natural i increïble de com funciona la nostra ment, que ens permet treballar conceptes de nivell superior i habilitats més avançades. Idees i execució. Aquesta és una idea força general que veurem. Algú et pot explicar una idea, i explicar-la et pot trigar dos minuts. Posar-la en pràctica i executar-la et pot trigar dos mesos

paragraphs.en: or two years to execute and put into practice. For example, I can explain the fundamentals of sweep picking to you in about 15 minutes, covering all the vital aspects of the technique.
paragraphs.ca: o dos anys. Per exemple, et puc explicar els fonaments del sweep picking en uns 15 minuts, cobrint tots els aspectes vitals de la tècnica.

paragraphs.en: Properly learning that technique will usually take six to nine months. Why is that? When we are learning a technique, we are forcing neural pathways in our brain to grow and reinforce.
paragraphs.ca: Aprendre bé aquesta tècnica normalment triga de sis a nou mesos. Per què? Quan aprenem una tècnica, forcem vies neuronals del nostre cervell a créixer i reforçar-se.

paragraphs.en: This is a physical process in our brain, and it takes time to happen. This may seem like a simple concept, but it's important because often people think that because they understand an idea but can't execute the idea on the spot, they cannot execute the idea at all. This is completely wrong.
paragraphs.ca: Aquest és un procés físic al nostre cervell, i triga temps a produir-se. Pot semblar un concepte simple, però és important, perquè sovint la gent pensa que, com que entén una idea però no la pot executar de seguida, no la pot executar de cap manera. Això és completament fals.

paragraphs.en: Understand that your ability to understand an idea and perform the idea, while related, exist on completely different timescales. If you can grasp this, you will save yourself a lot of frustration. Perfection as a guide, one step farther as the goal. This is a concept that we will revisit, possibly more than once, but I want to cover it here, as it is another big mindset idea. Often when it comes to learning guitar, I see students try to get things perfect. Now,
paragraphs.ca: Entén que la teva capacitat d'entendre una idea i de dur-la a terme, tot i estar relacionades, existeixen en escales de temps completament diferents. Si ho aconsegueixes assimilar, t'estalviaràs moltes frustracions. La perfecció com a guia, un pas més enllà com a objectiu. Aquest és un concepte que revisarem, possiblement més d'una vegada, però el vull tractar aquí, perquè és una altra gran idea de mentalitat. Sovint, quan es tracta d'aprendre guitarra, veig estudiants que intenten que les coses surtin perfectes. Ara,

paragraphs.en: I'm not saying don't try to get something perfect, but you have to understand that knowledge and ability are not linear. We previously looked at this with the spiral theory of knowledge.
paragraphs.ca: no dic que no intentis que una cosa surti perfecta, però has d'entendre que el coneixement i la capacitat no són lineals. Abans hem vist això amb la teoria espiral del coneixement.

paragraphs.en: Perfection is a curse that can affect you in your practice and your composition. Let's look at both.
paragraphs.ca: La perfecció és una maledicció que et pot afectar en la pràctica i en la composició. Mirem les dues coses.

paragraphs.en: Perfection in your practice. Often, a student will want to be able to play an exercise perfectly before moving on to the next exercise or next lesson. When you work this way, the 80-20 rule starts to work against you. The 80-20 rule states that 80% of the results come from 20% of the work, or in reverse, the top 20% of results take 80% of the work. In plain English, this means that getting an exercise to 80% takes 20% of the work, and getting that last 20% takes 80% of the work.
paragraphs.ca: La perfecció en la teva pràctica. Sovint, un estudiant voldrà ser capaç de tocar un exercici perfectament abans de passar al següent exercici o a la lliçó següent. Quan treballes així, la regla 80-20 comença a jugar en contra teva. La regla 80-20 diu que el 80% dels resultats provenen del 20% de la feina o, a l'inrevés, que el 20% dels resultats més alts requereixen el 80% de la feina. En paraules planeres, això vol dir que portar un exercici al 80% requereix el 20% de la feina, i aconseguir aquest últim 20% requereix el 80% de la feina.

paragraphs.en: That is, the last little bit of exercise to reach perfection takes four times as much work. In general, I find that getting an exercise to around 80% to 90% and then moving on to the next helps students progress much faster than if they spend all their time on getting one exercise to 100%. I also find that if a student is to practice this way for several weeks, they will find that when they revisit an older exercise, they had at 80%. They can usually get it to 100% with relative
paragraphs.ca: És a dir, l'últim petit tros d'exercici per arribar a la perfecció requereix quatre vegades més feina. En general, trobo que portar un exercici al voltant del 80% o el 90% i després passar al següent ajuda els estudiants a progressar molt més de pressa que si es passen tot el temps portant un sol exercici al 100%. També trobo que si un estudiant practica així durant diverses setmanes, descobrirà que, quan torna a un exercici antic que tenia al 80%, normalment el pot portar al 100% amb relativa

paragraphs.en: ease. As counterintuitive as this sounds, it is very effective. Perfection in your songwriting. Songwriting is a very personal experience, and releasing a song can be incredibly stressful.
paragraphs.ca: facilitat. Per contra-intuïtiu que soni, és molt efectiu. La perfecció en la teva composició. Escriure cançons és una experiència molt personal, i publicar una cançó pot ser increïblement estressant.

paragraphs.en: You're taking something you've worked on and putting it out to the world. This can be even worse in the modern-day setting of the internet and social media, with trolls and haters lurking in the void, waiting for the chance to tear down what you've put your work into. I've experienced this myself. Before releasing my album Impetuous Desire, I listened to it every night before going to sleep for a month, wondering if it was good enough and if I should just delete it. Fortunately,
paragraphs.ca: Agafes una cosa en què has treballat i la mostres al món. Això pot ser encara pitjor en l'entorn actual d'internet i les xarxes socials, amb trols i haters amagats al buit, esperant l'oportunitat de destruir allò on has posat la teva feina. Ho he viscut jo mateix. Abans de publicar el meu àlbum Impetuous Desire, el vaig escoltar cada nit abans d'anar a dormir durant un mes, preguntant-me si era prou bo i si l'hauria d'esborrar directament. Afortunadament,

paragraphs.en: I saw the light and released it. I know that students have felt anxiety about releasing music they have composed. Maybe you can relate to how they feel. Where does this anxiety come from?
paragraphs.ca: vaig veure la llum i el vaig publicar. Sé que els estudiants han sentit ansietat per publicar música que han compost. Potser t'hi pots identificar, amb com se senten. D'on ve aquesta ansietat?

paragraphs.en: It can come from, one, comparing what we have composed and recorded to our favorite songs, then concluding that our song falls short.
paragraphs.ca: Pot venir, primer, de comparar el que hem compost i enregistrat amb les nostres cançons preferides i després concloure que la nostra cançó es queda curta.

paragraphs.en: Two, wondering who we are to go and release a song. Three, identifying any minute errors in the song that no one else will ever hear or be able to hear.
paragraphs.ca: Segon, de preguntar-nos qui som nosaltres per anar a publicar una cançó. Tercer, d'identificar qualsevol error minúscul a la cançó que ningú més no sentirà mai ni serà capaç de sentir.

paragraphs.en: So when it comes to composing and releasing your music, what should the standard be? We do want to seek perfection, but in our effort, not the product of our effort.
paragraphs.ca: Així doncs, a l'hora de compondre i publicar la teva música, quin hauria de ser el criteri? Volem buscar la perfecció, però en el nostre esforç, no en el producte del nostre esforç.

paragraphs.en: We can't guarantee that we will write a great song, but we can guarantee that we will put 100% into it, that we will apply ourselves in a focused way and throw everything we have at it.
paragraphs.ca: No podem garantir que escriurem una gran cançó, però sí que podem garantir que hi posarem el 100%, que ens hi aplicarem d'una manera concentrada i que hi llançarem tot el que tenim.

paragraphs.en: That is the standard of perfection that we should adhere to. Our job as composers is not to judge the output of our work, that is for the public to do.
paragraphs.ca: Aquest és el criteri de perfecció al qual ens hauríem d'atenir. La nostra feina com a compositors no és jutjar el resultat de la nostra feina; això és cosa del públic.

paragraphs.en: Our job is to judge the standard of the effort we put into our work Additionally, consider this If you try, you can probably write a song that is at least half decent Is there one person in the world who will enjoy listening to that song?
paragraphs.ca: La nostra feina és jutjar el nivell d'esforç que posem a la nostra feina. A més, considera això: si ho intentes, probablement pots escriure una cançó que sigui com a mínim mig decent. Hi ha una persona al món a qui li agradarà escoltar aquesta cançó?

paragraphs.en: Is there one person in the world who for a few minutes You could make their life better by listening to your song? Probably Given the population of the world and how tragically awful most modern music is This is almost certainly true If you try and judge your music as good or bad, you will psychologically paralyze yourself.
paragraphs.ca: Hi ha una persona al món a qui, durant uns minuts, podries millorar-li la vida escoltant la teva cançó? Probablement. Tenint en compte la població del món i com de tràgicament dolenta és la majoria de la música moderna, això és gairebé segur que és cert. Si ho intentes i jutges la teva música com a bona o dolenta, et paralitzaràs psicològicament.

paragraphs.en: So don't do it. The speed you can work at increases with time. When you are at the start of your journey, the time it takes to complete projects can seem daunting.
paragraphs.ca: Així que no ho facis. La velocitat a què pots treballar augmenta amb el temps. Quan ets a l'inici del teu camí, el temps que cal per completar projectes et pot semblar aclaparador.

paragraphs.en: Your first instrumental song may take you months to complete. You do some simple maths and extrapolate that it will take you three years to complete a short album.
paragraphs.ca: La teva primera cançó instrumental et pot trigar mesos a completar. Fas uns càlculs senzills i extrapoles que trigaràs tres anys a completar un àlbum curt.

paragraphs.en: That can be quite daunting. At this point, it's easy to feel that the mountain ahead of you is insurmountable. However, the above calculation fails to take into account how you will improve with time.
paragraphs.ca: Això pot ser força aclaparador. En aquest punt, és fàcil sentir que la muntanya que tens al davant és insuperable. Tanmateix, el càlcul anterior no té en compte com milloraràs amb el temps.

paragraphs.en: Sure, your first few songs will take you a few months to compose, but after that experience, you'll be able to compose a bit faster. You'll learn workflow hacks that you can use to use your software faster.
paragraphs.ca: És clar, les teves primeres cançons et trigaran uns quants mesos a compondre, però després d'aquesta experiència podràs compondre una mica més de pressa. Aprendràs trucs de flux de treball que et permetran fer servir el teu programari més de pressa.

paragraphs.en: You'll learn more efficient ways to record. You'll learn more efficient ways to learn your compositions. If you keep studying, you will learn faster ways of composing.
paragraphs.ca: Aprendràs maneres més eficients d'enregistrar. Aprendràs maneres més eficients d'aprendre les teves composicions. Si continues estudiant, aprendràs maneres més ràpides de compondre.

paragraphs.en: You'll become more solid with your understanding of the fundamentals that go into composing, speeding up the rate at which you can compose.
paragraphs.ca: Tindràs una comprensió més sòlida dels fonaments que intervenen en la composició, cosa que accelerarà el ritme amb què pots compondre.

paragraphs.en: Your playing and performance skills will improve, meaning that you no longer need 1,021 takes to get a good recording of that difficult lick.
paragraphs.ca: La teva manera de tocar i les teves habilitats d'interpretació milloraran, cosa que vol dir que ja no necessitaràs 1.021 preses per aconseguir un bon enregistrament d'aquell lick difícil.

paragraphs.en: If you just keep working at it consistently, you will slowly and consistently improve over time. As we mentioned earlier, if you stick to the process for a few years, you will find your ability to compose and record increases consistently, allowing you to work faster at a higher quality than before.
paragraphs.ca: Si hi continues treballant de manera constant, milloraràs lenta i constantment amb el temps. Com hem dit abans, si mantens el procés durant uns quants anys, descobriràs que la teva capacitat de compondre i enregistrar augmenta de manera constant, cosa que et permetrà treballar més de pressa i amb més qualitat que abans.

paragraphs.en: The myth and danger of going all in. You don't have to look far in the creative world to find the advice of going all in.
paragraphs.ca: El mite i el perill de llançar-s'hi de ple. No cal buscar gaire en el món creatiu per trobar el consell de llançar-s'hi de ple.

paragraphs.en: The gurus and experts peddle this, as well as their lackeys. Why is this a myth, and why do people keep pushing this idea?
paragraphs.ca: Els gurus i els experts ho vengen, així com els seus sequaços. Per què és un mite, i per què la gent continua empenyent aquesta idea?

paragraphs.en: The myth. Succeeding in any creative venture takes time and a bit of luck. You can be a great composer, but there might not be an audience for what you create, or if there is an audience, developing that audience may take time.
paragraphs.ca: El mite. Triomfar en qualsevol aventura creativa requereix temps i una mica de sort. Pots ser un gran compositor, però potser no hi ha públic per a allò que crees o, si hi ha públic, potser desenvolupar aquest públic triga temps.

paragraphs.en: There is one inescapable truth. You're going to need money to live. You need a roof over your head and food on your table.
paragraphs.ca: Hi ha una veritat ineludible. Necessitaràs diners per viure. Necessites un sostre sobre el cap i menjar a taula.

paragraphs.en: Other people create these things and you need to make money so that you can trade for them. If you go all in, you find yourself with a lot of time, which is great for creating, but without an income, which is not so great for living.
paragraphs.ca: Altres persones creen aquestes coses i tu necessites guanyar diners per poder intercanviar-los per elles. Si t'hi llances de ple, et trobaràs amb molt de temps, cosa que és fantàstica per crear, però sense ingressos, cosa que no és tan fantàstica per viure.

paragraphs.en: A more effective approach is to keep a day job so that you can pay for your life and work on your composing as a side project until it takes off, if that's what you want.
paragraphs.ca: Una estratègia més efectiva és mantenir una feina diürna per poder pagar la teva vida i treballar en la teva composició com a projecte paral·lel fins que s'enlairi, si és això el que vols.

paragraphs.en: Why does this myth keep going? This myth is often perpetuated by the marketing gurus as a way to guilt you into being serious about your music and buying into their programs.
paragraphs.ca: Per què continua el mite? Aquest mite sovint el perpetuen els gurus del màrqueting com una manera de fer-te sentir culpable perquè et prenguis seriosament la teva música i compris els seus programes.

paragraphs.en: They'll roll out the story of the commander who ordered his troops to burn their ships to force them to win the battle. Unfortunately, all that you get from this is losing a big chunk of change and putting yourself in a financially precarious position.
paragraphs.ca: T'expliquen la història del comandant que va ordenar a les seves tropes cremar els vaixells per forçar-los a guanyar la batalla. Malauradament, l'únic que n'obtens és perdre una bona pila de diners i posar-te en una situació financera precària.

paragraphs.en: Section 2. Guitar Practice
paragraphs.ca: Secció 2. Pràctica de la guitarra

segments.text: Section 2. Guitar Practice
In this section, we're going to take an in-depth look at guitar practice.
We're going to break down how to approach and organize your practice,
and what it is we are trying to achieve with practice.
Implementing all the ideas in this section will take time.
The most effective way to use this section of the book is to read through it
and pick one idea that you think will help you the most.
Take a week to implement that idea into your practice.
Then, the following week, pick another idea and then incorporate that into your practice.
Muscle memory.
What is it we are trying to achieve when we practice the guitar?
Most of the time, we are working on training what is known as muscle memory,
which is our ability to play something accurately, with little effort and without having to think about it.
There are four levels to mastering any physical skill.
1. Conscious incompetence. 2. Conscious competence. 3. Subconscious incompetence.
4. Subconscious competence. Level 1. Conscious incompetence.
At level 1, we are carefully thinking through the movements we are trying to execute,
and our body is not doing what we want. We are trying to make the chord change,
and our fingers are flying everywhere. We are trying to pick through a scale,
and our pick hand is hitting all sorts of strings it shouldn't be.
This is the level that we all start at when working on a skill.
It is vital to practice slowly.
You must practice slowly enough that you give yourself enough time
to think through what you are doing.
You may find it helpful to talk yourself through what you are trying to do out loud
to force yourself to slow down to the speed at which you can think.
It is common for students at this level to try to practice too quickly.
By playing too quickly, their mind can't consciously think through what they are trying to do,
forcing their mind to rely on their subconscious skill, which has not yet been trained,
and predictably, nonsense comes out of their hands.
Progression to level two requires slowing things down, way down,
so you can think through what you are doing.
Play things slow enough to get them right.
If you are consistently making mistakes, you are playing too quickly and not learning anything.
Level 2 Conscious Competence
At this level, we are still carefully thinking through what we are doing,
but we are now executing movements accurately, and the music is starting to sound right.
You will probably find that you can think things through a bit faster than when you were at level 1.
Here it is tempting to start speeding things up, but resist the urge to move too quickly.
Now that you can consciously play the exercise accurately, start to think about muscle tension and technique.
Are you playing things as efficiently as you could be, or are you waving your hands around?
Are you relaxed when you play, or is your body tense like you're about to fight a bear?
Working on your technique and muscle tension will help you progress to the next level.
It is also important to play the exercise at the same tempo, accurately, the same way, every single time.
At this level, we are trying to program our muscle memory.
You can think of programming muscle memory like this.
You have to play something ten times in a row correctly,
exactly the same way to increase your muscle memory by one.
During those ten repetitions, if you make a mistake or play something a different way,
for example, using a different finger, you reset your repetitions and have to start again.
A common mistake is to play an exercise slightly differently each time the exercise is repeated.
This forces your muscle memory to have to learn three, four, five different ways of playing the exercise,
which makes programming the muscle memory infinitely harder.
Level 3. Subconscious incompetence
This level is usually a sign that we have rushed level 2.
Now, there is a fine line that has to be drawn here, which I'll attempt to explain.
At some point, we have to push the tempos of what we are working on and push ourselves to the next level.
We also have to ensure that we can play something correctly before doing so.
When pushing ourselves appropriately, it can take a few repetitions to get the hang of what we are doing.
After all, our body is doing something new by increasing the tempo.
so it is unreasonable to expect to play the exercise perfectly the first time we increase
the tempo. However, if we are unable to play at a higher tempo, we need to come back down a bit.
When increasing tempos, I usually find 15 to 20 repetitions will give me a good idea of if I need
to turn the metronome back down or soldier on. If, after 15 to 20 repetitions, you see no improvement,
you need to slow things back down. If you see a lot of improvement, you probably want to continue
pushing to get it right. If you see a little improvement, maybe find a tempo between where
you were and where you are. Level 4. Subconscious Competence
At this level, we can truly say that the skill has been learned, and we can move on to something
else, creating a variation of it, pushing the tempos even harder, or trying it out in different
contexts. At this level, we can see big improvements in the speeds we can reach,
while still playing accurately. I usually find this level takes two to three weeks to reach,
practicing an exercise six days out of seven. Side note on pushing tempos. It is worth pushing
your ability beyond what you can do. If you find you are struggling at, say, 100 bpm, then having
a go at 110 bpm for 5 to 10 minutes, where you try and force your body to play faster,
can be beneficial. When you roll the tempo back down to 100 bpm, you may well find that
it is now a bit easier. However, if you spend all your practice time at 110 bpm, you will
be wasting time. If you play electric guitar, a great training trick is to warm up with
the exercise on an acoustic guitar. Acoustic guitar strings are much bigger and heavier than
electric guitar strings, making the exercise much harder. Take your exercise and play it on acoustic
guitar for five minutes, then go back to electric guitar. Your fingers will feel like they are
playing faster than ever. Preparing for practice. Often, we don't think of what it takes to prepare
for practicing and want to dive straight into rushing through the practice as fast as possible.
This is a huge mistake, and while rushing in like this gives you a feeling of being busy and getting things done,
what you'll find is that you frustrate yourself, learn inefficiently with the wrong expectation, and make very little progress.
That's why this section of the book deals with some of the ideas behind why we practice,
what we are trying to achieve when we practice, and how to set ourselves up to learn effectively, long-term,
continuously making progress with our playing. The importance of long-term learning. When it
comes to learning guitar or anything else in life, we often overestimate how quickly we can learn.
Tony Robbins has a fantastic quote on this. We overestimate what we can accomplish in a year
and underestimate what we can accomplish in 10, and learning guitar is a great example of the
power of this concept. I cannot count how many times I have seen a student say something along
the lines of, this is simple, I should be able to just play it. Simple by what standard? Just
because you understand what your fingers should be able to do does not mean that they will do it.
Every single motion you want to make on a guitar must be trained. And to demonstrate the other
side of the spectrum, I have students who, when at their initial lesson, thought that writing their
own guitar song would be impossible, seven years later, are composing their own orchestral works
and performing their own arrangements of jazz standards. Most people give up early and don't
truly apply themselves to learning something long-term. They might dip into it from time to
time and play a few chords, but they don't truly stick to learning long-term. The truth is, if they
did, and if you stick to learning long-term, you would not be able to imagine the progress you
would make across 5, 10, 15 years. This is important to understand. Anyone who sticks
to something long-term and takes their learning seriously is going to make incredible progress.
Someone studying in academia will spend seven years going from undergraduate to acquiring a
PhD in their chosen field. Sticking to aggressively learning and practicing for seven years,
10 years, 15 years is like acquiring your own PhD in guitar and composition.
Sure, it's not exactly the same, but given some of the subjects people seem to gain a doctorate in,
it's a better use of your time. Why do people quit learning guitar?
So when it comes to dedicating ourselves to something long-term, even if it's something
we enjoy, or at least think we will enjoy, why do people quit before giving themselves a chance?
There are a few reasons. 1. Not budgeting their time. 2. Not understanding what learning feels
like. 3. The difference between practicing and playing. 4. Not understanding how to learn.
5. Setting the wrong standard for evaluating their progress. Not budgeting their time.
Elsewhere in this book, we're going to talk about how important budgeting our time is.
by controlling our time, we can control the person we become. But for now, we'll look at
the basic idea. If you want to improve at something, you have to put time into practicing it.
It doesn't matter if it's learning guitar, learning mathematics, becoming a better father,
or becoming a carpenter. Improvement requires practice, which requires time.
If you have a schedule that has no available time for practice, and you enroll in lessons,
you are not going to improve. In fact, you will probably create more stress for yourself,
which you do not need. If you want to improve, you first have to create the conditions for success,
which in this case means finding a way to budget some time every day so that you can practice.
Sit down with your calendar and budget some time to practice every day, and then stick to it.
Not understanding what learning feels like. Learning will often feel frustrating. Or is it?
When we are learning something new, we are trying to find a way to do something that we have never
done before. To understand this on a slightly deeper level, we need to understand what doing
something means on a neurological level. Whenever we make an action with our body,
a series of neurons in our brain fire in a specific sequence, which creates the electrical
signal that makes our muscles move in a certain way. When we are experts at something, such as
tying our shoelaces or putting on a jacket, our brain has an established network of neurons to
fire for that specific task. As a task is practiced over and over, the network involved
becomes reinforced and the electrical signal can travel faster through it. If we have never done
that particular task before, that network does not exist and needs to be made. This is what we
are doing when we practice. We are forcing our brain to physically build new connections between
neurons. We are trying to force electrical signals around our brains in ways that are new to us.
This is difficult.

We feel a mental resistance that takes focus to overcome. This resistance is often misidentified as frustration. That resistance is normal and should be expected. We should embrace it, because when you feel that resistance, it means you are right at the edge of your ability, which is the right place to be when learning something new.
But a lot of people interpret this feeling as something negative and put a negative value judgment on themselves from it
This feeling you experience when working on something new, such as a new chord progression
Isn't a sign that you are stupid, that you have no talent or that you can't play the guitar
It's a sign that you're doing exactly what you need to be doing to improve
Changing how you emotionally react to this resistance is key to being able to push your ability long term.
Sure, it can be frustrating, but if it gets too much, walk away for five minutes, make a cup of tea and get back on it.
Don't give up because you are experiencing what it feels like to learn.
Practice doesn't always have to be fun.
When approaching something like learning an instrument, we learn it because we want to get an emotional reward of some sort.
For most people, that's having fun.
However, reaching the stage where we can have fun takes effort,
and that process usually isn't fun, at least, there are times when it isn't fun.
I know that sometimes I just don't want to pick up my guitar at all.
Admittedly, this is rare, but sometimes I really have to make myself do it.
When I'm feeling like that, I don't usually have fun playing the guitar,
but I know I need to at least do something, so I do something.
I also know that when I sit down and work on something, the next day I am much better at it
Other times, I can easily pick up the guitar
But there are things I need to practice that aren't very fun for me to do so
But I know will benefit me if I do
And a lot of times I really enjoy practicing
The point is, practice isn't always fun
Most of the time it should be a sort of rewarding concentration
Sometimes practice puts us in an almost trance-like state
But it isn't always fun, and that's okay.
It is important to anticipate that it won't always be fun,
so that when this happens to you, rather than getting carried away in the emotion,
you understand it and do some practice anyway.
The difference between practicing and playing.
This is a progress killer.
A lot of the time when people pick up their guitars thinking they're practicing,
they're actually playing.
Playing guitar is when you are repeating a set of motions that you have previously learned.
Practicing is when you are training your body on a new set of motions.
These could be variations on something previously learned or something new.
If you look at how much time you are practicing, you will probably find you are playing and not doing much practice at all.
If you are not practicing, you are not improving.

Now, I'm not saying that you should spend all your time practicing, and don't spend any time playing your favorite songs, but if you want to continuously improve your playing, you need to ensure that there is a proportion of your time devoted to practicing, and generally speaking, the more time practicing, the faster you will improve.
Not understanding how to learn
This is a critical piece of the puzzle that we will cover in detail later in the book.
If you do not understand how to learn or what the purpose of learning is,
then you will not progress and you will not have fun.
It's as simple as that.
Unfortunately, we are never taught how to learn effectively.
In school, we are taught that the process of learning is the memorization of almost random facts.
This is simply not true.
Memorization is a part of learning, but learning also requires integration and application.
It requires understanding the context of the facts that you are studying and identifying the essentials behind each idea.
And without these critical parts, your learning will be ineffective.
Setting the wrong standard for progress
This one is killer.
When we set the wrong standard for being able to feel good about our playing,
we are setting ourselves up to feel miserable about our playing for life.
It doesn't take too much imagination to picture that someone who feels miserable about playing an instrument
will not want to play it for very long.
When it comes to learning an instrument,
99% of students will compare themselves to their favourite player.
They are continuously judging their ability against someone who is a master of their craft,
Unsurprisingly, they continuously come up short.
Let's make a comparison.
Let's say it's your first day at university
and your lecturer was giving you a brief overview of a complex topic
that you will be studying later in the year.
It's obvious your lecturer is an expert in this field.
Would you feel like a failure because you don't know what your professor does?
Of course not.
That would be ridiculous.
As soon as you think about this for one second,
it's obvious that to feel bad because you don't know as much as the expert makes no sense whatsoever
because you haven't put in the time like they have, which is why you're there in the first place.
Yet, when it comes to learning guitar, we do this all the time. And because we do this,
we make ourselves feel miserable. So the question is, how should we judge our progress?
Should we judge our progress at all? We need to find some metric to evaluate our progress.
Otherwise, we risk never improving.
The correct metric that we should use is how we were doing last week.
And the correct goal is to be a tiny bit better than we were last week.
Maybe just 1%.
That could be 1% faster with our tempo, or playing 1% more consistently, or 1% less tension.
You get the idea.
We just want to be 1% better.
Along as you are practicing regularly, this is an achievable goal.
In fact, most weeks you will improve more than 1%.
So, if you can retrain the criteria for what it takes to feel good about your playing from
can I play like my favourite player to did I improve 1% compared to last week,
then you are going to feel good about your playing.
The impact of this is that if you feel good about your playing,
you will keep practising and keep improving a few percent each week over a period of several years.
And all those small improvements will compound into improvements so large that it's difficult for you to imagine at this point in time.
If you just keep going, improving a little week by week, you will become a monster guitar player.
Setting the correct expectations of ourselves.
