paragraphs.en: Muscle memory. What is it we are trying to achieve when we practice the guitar? Most of the time, we are working on training what is known as muscle memory, which is our ability to play something accurately, with little effort and without having to think about it.
paragraphs.ca: Memòria muscular. Què és el que intentem aconseguir quan practiquem la guitarra? La major part del temps treballem entrenant el que es coneix com a memòria muscular, que és la nostra capacitat de tocar una cosa amb precisió, amb poc esforç i sense haver-hi de pensar.

paragraphs.en: There are four levels to mastering any physical skill. 1. Conscious incompetence. 2. Conscious competence. 3. Subconscious incompetence.
paragraphs.ca: Hi ha quatre nivells per dominar qualsevol habilitat física. 1. Incompetència conscient. 2. Competència conscient. 3. Incompetència subconscient.

paragraphs.en: 4. Subconscious competence. Level 1. Conscious incompetence. At level 1, we are carefully thinking through the movements we are trying to execute, and our body is not doing what we want. We are trying to make the chord change, and our fingers are flying everywhere. We are trying to pick through a scale, and our pick hand is hitting all sorts of strings it shouldn't be.
paragraphs.ca: 4. Competència subconscient. Nivell 1. Incompetència conscient. Al nivell 1, pensem acuradament els moviments que intentem executar, i el nostre cos no fa el que volem. Intentem fer el canvi d'acord i els dits se'ns escampen pertot arreu. Intentem tocar una escala amb la pua i la mà de la pua colpeja tota mena de cordes que no hauria de tocar.

paragraphs.en: This is the level that we all start at when working on a skill. It is vital to practice slowly. You must practice slowly enough that you give yourself enough time to think through what you are doing.
paragraphs.ca: Aquest és el nivell en què tots comencem quan treballem una habilitat. És vital practicar a poc a poc. Has de practicar prou lentament per donar-te temps suficient per pensar què estàs fent.

paragraphs.en: You may find it helpful to talk yourself through what you are trying to do out loud to force yourself to slow down to the speed at which you can think.
paragraphs.ca: Potser et resultarà útil parlar-te en veu alta sobre el que intentes fer, per obligar-te a alentir-te fins a la velocitat a la qual pots pensar.

paragraphs.en: It is common for students at this level to try to practice too quickly. By playing too quickly, their mind can't consciously think through what they are trying to do, forcing their mind to rely on their subconscious skill, which has not yet been trained, and predictably, nonsense comes out of their hands.
paragraphs.ca: És habitual que els estudiants d'aquest nivell intentin practicar massa de pressa. En tocar massa de pressa, la seva ment no pot pensar conscientment què intenten fer, cosa que l'obliga a confiar en la seva habilitat subconscient, que encara no s'ha entrenat i, com era previsible, de les seves mans en surten disbarats.

paragraphs.en: Progression to level two requires slowing things down, way down, so you can think through what you are doing. Play things slow enough to get them right.
paragraphs.ca: Per passar al nivell dos cal alentir les coses, molt, per poder pensar què estàs fent. Toca les coses prou lentament per fer-les bé.

paragraphs.en: If you are consistently making mistakes, you are playing too quickly and not learning anything.
paragraphs.ca: Si fas errors de manera constant, toques massa de pressa i no aprens res.

paragraphs.en: Level 2 Conscious Competence At this level, we are still carefully thinking through what we are doing, but we are now executing movements accurately, and the music is starting to sound right.
paragraphs.ca: Nivell 2. Competència conscient. En aquest nivell encara pensem acuradament què fem, però ara executem els moviments amb precisió i la música comença a sonar bé.

paragraphs.en: You will probably find that you can think things through a bit faster than when you were at level 1. Here it is tempting to start speeding things up, but resist the urge to move too quickly.
paragraphs.ca: Probablement veuràs que pots pensar les coses una mica més de pressa que quan eres al nivell 1. Aquí és temptador començar a accelerar les coses, però resisteix la temptació d'anar massa de pressa.

paragraphs.en: Now that you can consciously play the exercise accurately, start to think about muscle tension and technique. Are you playing things as efficiently as you could be, or are you waving your hands around?
paragraphs.ca: Ara que pots tocar l'exercici amb precisió de manera conscient, comença a pensar en la tensió muscular i la tècnica. Toques les coses tan eficientment com podries, o vas movent les mans d'una banda a l'altra?

paragraphs.en: Are you relaxed when you play, or is your body tense like you're about to fight a bear? Working on your technique and muscle tension will help you progress to the next level.
paragraphs.ca: Estàs relaxat quan toques, o el teu cos està tens com si estiguessis a punt de barallar-te amb un ós? Treballar la tècnica i la tensió muscular t'ajudarà a passar al nivell següent.

paragraphs.en: It is also important to play the exercise at the same tempo, accurately, the same way, every single time. At this level, we are trying to program our muscle memory.
paragraphs.ca: També és important tocar l'exercici al mateix tempo, amb precisió, de la mateixa manera, cada vegada. En aquest nivell intentem programar la nostra memòria muscular.

paragraphs.en: You can think of programming muscle memory like this. You have to play something ten times in a row correctly, exactly the same way to increase your muscle memory by one.
paragraphs.ca: Pots imaginar la programació de la memòria muscular així: has de tocar una cosa deu vegades seguides correctament, exactament de la mateixa manera, per augmentar la teva memòria muscular en un punt.

paragraphs.en: During those ten repetitions, if you make a mistake or play something a different way, for example, using a different finger, you reset your repetitions and have to start again.
paragraphs.ca: Durant aquestes deu repeticions, si fas un error o toques una cosa d'una manera diferent, per exemple amb un dit diferent, reinicies les repeticions i has de tornar a començar.

paragraphs.en: A common mistake is to play an exercise slightly differently each time the exercise is repeated. This forces your muscle memory to have to learn three, four, five different ways of playing the exercise, which makes programming the muscle memory infinitely harder.
paragraphs.ca: Un error habitual és tocar un exercici una mica diferent cada vegada que es repeteix. Això obliga la teva memòria muscular a aprendre tres, quatre o cinc maneres diferents de tocar l'exercici, cosa que fa que programar-la sigui infinitament més difícil.

paragraphs.en: Level 3. Subconscious incompetence This level is usually a sign that we have rushed level 2. Now, there is a fine line that has to be drawn here, which I'll attempt to explain.
paragraphs.ca: Nivell 3. Incompetència subconscient. Aquest nivell sol ser un senyal que hem precipitat el nivell 2. Ara bé, aquí hi ha una línia molt fina que cal traçar i que intentaré explicar.

paragraphs.en: At some point, we have to push the tempos of what we are working on and push ourselves to the next level. We also have to ensure that we can play something correctly before doing so.
paragraphs.ca: En algun moment hem d'apujar els tempos del que estem treballant i empènyer-nos cap al nivell següent. També hem d'assegurar-nos que sabem tocar una cosa correctament abans de fer-ho.

paragraphs.en: When pushing ourselves appropriately, it can take a few repetitions to get the hang of what we are doing. After all, our body is doing something new by increasing the tempo.
paragraphs.ca: Quan ens exigim de manera adequada, pot caldre unes quantes repeticions per agafar el truc al que estem fent. Al capdavall, el nostre cos està fent una cosa nova en augmentar el tempo,

paragraphs.en: so it is unreasonable to expect to play the exercise perfectly the first time we increase the tempo. However, if we are unable to play at a higher tempo, we need to come back down a bit.
paragraphs.ca: així que no és raonable esperar tocar l'exercici perfectament la primera vegada que apugem el tempo. Tanmateix, si no som capaços de tocar a un tempo més alt, hem de tornar a baixar una mica.

paragraphs.en: When increasing tempos, I usually find 15 to 20 repetitions will give me a good idea of if I need to turn the metronome back down or soldier on. If, after 15 to 20 repetitions, you see no improvement, you need to slow things back down. If you see a lot of improvement, you probably want to continue pushing to get it right. If you see a little improvement, maybe find a tempo between where you were and where you are. Level 4. Subconscious Competence
paragraphs.ca: Quan apujo tempos, normalment trobo que 15 o 20 repeticions em donen una bona idea de si he de tornar a baixar el metrònom o seguir endavant. Si, després de 15 o 20 repeticions, no veus cap millora, has de tornar a alentir les coses. Si veus una millora important, segurament voldràs continuar insistint per fer-ho bé. Si veus una millora petita, potser troba un tempo entre on eres i on ets ara. Nivell 4. Competència subconscient.

paragraphs.en: At this level, we can truly say that the skill has been learned, and we can move on to something else, creating a variation of it, pushing the tempos even harder, or trying it out in different contexts. At this level, we can see big improvements in the speeds we can reach, while still playing accurately. I usually find this level takes two to three weeks to reach, practicing an exercise six days out of seven. Side note on pushing tempos. It is worth pushing
paragraphs.ca: En aquest nivell podem dir de debò que l'habilitat s'ha après, i podem passar a una altra cosa: crear-ne una variació, apujar encara més els tempos o provar-la en contextos diferents. En aquest nivell podem veure millores grans en les velocitats que assolim, tot i tocar amb precisió. Normalment trobo que aquest nivell triga dues o tres setmanes a assolir-se, practicant un exercici sis dies de cada set. Nota al marge sobre apujar tempos. Val la pena empènyer

paragraphs.en: your ability beyond what you can do. If you find you are struggling at, say, 100 bpm, then having a go at 110 bpm for 5 to 10 minutes, where you try and force your body to play faster, can be beneficial. When you roll the tempo back down to 100 bpm, you may well find that it is now a bit easier. However, if you spend all your practice time at 110 bpm, you will be wasting time. If you play electric guitar, a great training trick is to warm up with
paragraphs.ca: la teva capacitat més enllà del que ets capaç de fer. Si veus que vas amb dificultat, posem per cas a 100 bpm, provar-ho a 110 bpm durant 5 o 10 minuts, intentant forçar el cos a tocar més de pressa, pot ser beneficiós. Quan tornis a baixar el tempo a 100 bpm, és molt possible que ara et resulti una mica més fàcil. Ara bé, si passes tot el temps de pràctica a 110 bpm, estaràs perdent el temps. Si toques guitarra elèctrica, un bon truc d'entrenament és escalfar amb

paragraphs.en: the exercise on an acoustic guitar. Acoustic guitar strings are much bigger and heavier than electric guitar strings, making the exercise much harder. Take your exercise and play it on acoustic guitar for five minutes, then go back to electric guitar. Your fingers will feel like they are playing faster than ever. Preparing for practice. Often, we don't think of what it takes to prepare for practicing and want to dive straight into rushing through the practice as fast as possible.
paragraphs.ca: l'exercici en una guitarra acústica. Les cordes de la guitarra acústica són molt més grans i més gruixudes que les de la guitarra elèctrica, cosa que fa l'exercici molt més difícil. Agafa el teu exercici i toca'l amb la guitarra acústica durant cinc minuts, i després torna a la guitarra elèctrica. Els dits et semblaran anar més de pressa que mai. Preparar la pràctica. Sovint no pensem en què cal per preparar la pràctica i volem llançar-nos directament a passar per la pràctica tan de pressa com sigui possible.

paragraphs.en: This is a huge mistake, and while rushing in like this gives you a feeling of being busy and getting things done, what you'll find is that you frustrate yourself, learn inefficiently with the wrong expectation, and make very little progress.
paragraphs.ca: Això és un error enorme i, tot i que llançar-se així et dona la sensació d'estar ocupat i de fer coses, el que trobaràs és que t'irrites, aprens de manera ineficient amb expectatives equivocades i avances molt poc.

paragraphs.en: That's why this section of the book deals with some of the ideas behind why we practice, what we are trying to achieve when we practice, and how to set ourselves up to learn effectively, long-term, continuously making progress with our playing. The importance of long-term learning. When it comes to learning guitar or anything else in life, we often overestimate how quickly we can learn.
paragraphs.ca: Per això aquesta secció del llibre tracta algunes de les idees que hi ha darrere del perquè practiquem, què intentem aconseguir quan practiquem i com preparar-nos per aprendre eficaçment, a llarg termini, progressant contínuament amb el nostre instrument. La importància de l'aprenentatge a llarg termini. Quan es tracta d'aprendre guitarra o qualsevol altra cosa a la vida, sovint sobreestimem la rapidesa amb què podem aprendre.

paragraphs.en: Tony Robbins has a fantastic quote on this. We overestimate what we can accomplish in a year and underestimate what we can accomplish in 10, and learning guitar is a great example of the power of this concept. I cannot count how many times I have seen a student say something along the lines of, this is simple, I should be able to just play it. Simple by what standard? Just because you understand what your fingers should be able to do does not mean that they will do it.
paragraphs.ca: Tony Robbins té una cita fantàstica sobre això: sobreestimem el que podem aconseguir en un any i subestimem el que podem aconseguir en 10, i aprendre guitarra és un gran exemple del poder d'aquest concepte. No puc comptar les vegades que he vist un alumne dir una cosa com: això és senzill, hauria de poder tocar-ho i prou. Senzill segons quin criteri? Que entenguis què haurien de fer els teus dits no vol dir que ho facin.

paragraphs.en: Every single motion you want to make on a guitar must be trained. And to demonstrate the other side of the spectrum, I have students who, when at their initial lesson, thought that writing their own guitar song would be impossible, seven years later, are composing their own orchestral works and performing their own arrangements of jazz standards. Most people give up early and don't truly apply themselves to learning something long-term. They might dip into it from time to
paragraphs.ca: Cada moviment que vulguis fer amb una guitarra s'ha d'entrenar. I, per mostrar l'altre extrem de l'espectre, tinc alumnes que, a la seva primera classe, pensaven que escriure la seva pròpia cançó de guitarra seria impossible i que, set anys després, componen obres orquestrals pròpies i interpreten els seus propis arranjaments d'estàndards de jazz. La majoria de la gent es rendeix aviat i no s'aplica de debò a aprendre una cosa a llarg termini. Potser hi toquen de tant en tant

paragraphs.en: time and play a few chords, but they don't truly stick to learning long-term. The truth is, if they did, and if you stick to learning long-term, you would not be able to imagine the progress you would make across 5, 10, 15 years. This is important to understand. Anyone who sticks to something long-term and takes their learning seriously is going to make incredible progress.
paragraphs.ca: i toquen uns quants acords, però no es mantenen de debò en l'aprenentatge a llarg termini. La veritat és que, si ho fessin, i si tu et mantens en l'aprenentatge a llarg termini, no series capaç d'imaginar el progrés que faries al llarg de 5, 10 o 15 anys. Això és important d'entendre. Qualsevol que es mantingui en una cosa a llarg termini i es prengui seriosament el seu aprenentatge farà un progrés increïble.

paragraphs.en: Someone studying in academia will spend seven years going from undergraduate to acquiring a PhD in their chosen field. Sticking to aggressively learning and practicing for seven years, 10 years, 15 years is like acquiring your own PhD in guitar and composition.
paragraphs.ca: Algú que estudia a la universitat passarà set anys des del grau fins a obtenir un doctorat en el seu camp. Mantenir-se aprenent i practicant de manera agressiva durant set, deu o quinze anys és com obtenir el teu propi doctorat en guitarra i composició.

paragraphs.en: Sure, it's not exactly the same, but given some of the subjects people seem to gain a doctorate in, it's a better use of your time. Why do people quit learning guitar?
paragraphs.ca: És clar que no és exactament el mateix, però, vistos alguns dels temes pels quals la gent sembla obtenir un doctorat, és una millor manera de fer servir el teu temps. Per què la gent deixa d'aprendre guitarra?

paragraphs.en: So when it comes to dedicating ourselves to something long-term, even if it's something we enjoy, or at least think we will enjoy, why do people quit before giving themselves a chance?
paragraphs.ca: Així, quan es tracta de dedicar-nos a una cosa a llarg termini, encara que sigui una cosa que gaudim, o que almenys pensem que gaudirem, per què la gent ho deixa abans de donar-se una oportunitat?

paragraphs.en: There are a few reasons. 1. Not budgeting their time. 2. Not understanding what learning feels like. 3. The difference between practicing and playing. 4. Not understanding how to learn.
paragraphs.ca: Hi ha unes quantes raons. 1. No pressupostar el seu temps. 2. No entendre com se sent aprendre. 3. La diferència entre practicar i tocar. 4. No saber com aprendre.

paragraphs.en: 5. Setting the wrong standard for evaluating their progress. Not budgeting their time. Elsewhere in this book, we're going to talk about how important budgeting our time is.
paragraphs.ca: 5. Fixar un criteri equivocat per avaluar el seu progrés. No pressupostar el seu temps. En un altre lloc d'aquest llibre parlarem de com n'és d'important pressupostar el nostre temps.

paragraphs.en: by controlling our time, we can control the person we become. But for now, we'll look at the basic idea. If you want to improve at something, you have to put time into practicing it.
paragraphs.ca: controlant el nostre temps podem controlar la persona en què ens convertim. Però de moment veurem la idea bàsica. Si vols millorar en una cosa, hi has de dedicar temps de pràctica.

paragraphs.en: It doesn't matter if it's learning guitar, learning mathematics, becoming a better father, or becoming a carpenter. Improvement requires practice, which requires time.
paragraphs.ca: Tant és si es tracta d'aprendre guitarra, aprendre matemàtiques, ser un millor pare o convertir-te en fuster. La millora requereix pràctica, i la pràctica requereix temps.

paragraphs.en: If you have a schedule that has no available time for practice, and you enroll in lessons, you are not going to improve. In fact, you will probably create more stress for yourself, which you do not need. If you want to improve, you first have to create the conditions for success, which in this case means finding a way to budget some time every day so that you can practice.
paragraphs.ca: Si tens una agenda sense temps disponible per practicar i t'apuntes a classes, no milloraràs. De fet, probablement et crearàs més estrès, que no necessites. Si vols millorar, primer has de crear les condicions per a l'èxit, que en aquest cas vol dir trobar la manera de reservar una mica de temps cada dia per poder practicar.

paragraphs.en: Sit down with your calendar and budget some time to practice every day, and then stick to it.
paragraphs.ca: Seu amb el teu calendari, reserva una mica de temps per practicar cada dia i després compleix-ho.

paragraphs.en: Not understanding what learning feels like. Learning will often feel frustrating. Or is it? When we are learning something new, we are trying to find a way to do something that we have never done before. To understand this on a slightly deeper level, we need to understand what doing something means on a neurological level. Whenever we make an action with our body, a series of neurons in our brain fire in a specific sequence, which creates the electrical
paragraphs.ca: No entendre com se sent aprendre. Aprendre sovint se sent frustrant. O no? Quan aprenem una cosa nova, intentem trobar la manera de fer una cosa que mai no hem fet abans. Per entendre-ho una mica més a fons, hem d'entendre què vol dir fer una cosa a nivell neurològic. Cada vegada que fem una acció amb el cos, una sèrie de neurones del nostre cervell s'activen en una seqüència específica, cosa que crea el senyal elèctric

paragraphs.en: signal that makes our muscles move in a certain way. When we are experts at something, such as tying our shoelaces or putting on a jacket, our brain has an established network of neurons to fire for that specific task. As a task is practiced over and over, the network involved becomes reinforced and the electrical signal can travel faster through it. If we have never done that particular task before, that network does not exist and needs to be made. This is what we
paragraphs.ca: que fa que els nostres músculs es moguin d'una manera determinada. Quan som experts en una cosa, com cordar-se les sabates o posar-se una jaqueta, el nostre cervell té una xarxa de neurones establerta que s'activa per a aquella tasca concreta. A mesura que una tasca es practica una vegada i una altra, la xarxa implicada es reforça i el senyal elèctric hi pot viatjar més de pressa. Si mai no hem fet aquella tasca concreta, aquella xarxa no existeix i cal crear-la. Això és el que

paragraphs.en: are doing when we practice. We are forcing our brain to physically build new connections between neurons. We are trying to force electrical signals around our brains in ways that are new to us.
paragraphs.ca: fem quan practiquem. Forcem el nostre cervell a construir físicament noves connexions entre neurones. Intentem forçar senyals elèctrics pel cervell de maneres que ens són noves.

paragraphs.en: This is difficult. We feel a mental resistance that takes focus to overcome. This resistance is often misidentified as frustration. That resistance is normal and should be expected. We should embrace it, because when you feel that resistance, it means you are right at the edge of your ability, which is the right place to be when learning something new.
paragraphs.ca: Això és difícil. Sentim una resistència mental que cal concentració per superar. Aquesta resistència sovint s'identifica malament com a frustració. Aquesta resistència és normal i cal esperar-la. L'hem d'acceptar, perquè quan sents aquesta resistència vol dir que ets just al límit de la teva capacitat, que és el lloc on has de ser quan aprens una cosa nova.

paragraphs.en: But a lot of people interpret this feeling as something negative and put a negative value judgment on themselves from it This feeling you experience when working on something new, such as a new chord progression Isn't a sign that you are stupid, that you have no talent or that you can't play the guitar It's a sign that you're doing exactly what you need to be doing to improve Changing how you emotionally react to this resistance is key to being able to push your ability long term.
paragraphs.ca: Però molta gent interpreta aquesta sensació com una cosa negativa i se'n fa un judici de valor negatiu. Aquesta sensació que experimentes quan treballes una cosa nova, com una progressió d'acords nova, no és un senyal que siguis estúpid, que no tinguis talent o que no sàpigues tocar la guitarra. És un senyal que estàs fent exactament el que has de fer per millorar. Canviar com reacciones emocionalment a aquesta resistència és clau per poder empènyer la teva capacitat a llarg termini.

paragraphs.en: Sure, it can be frustrating, but if it gets too much, walk away for five minutes, make a cup of tea and get back on it. Don't give up because you are experiencing what it feels like to learn.
paragraphs.ca: És clar que pot ser frustrant, però si es fa massa gros, aparta't cinc minuts, fes-te una tassa de te i torna-hi. No ho deixis perquè estàs experimentant com se sent aprendre.

paragraphs.en: Practice doesn't always have to be fun. When approaching something like learning an instrument, we learn it because we want to get an emotional reward of some sort.
paragraphs.ca: La pràctica no sempre ha de ser divertida. Quan ens acostem a una cosa com aprendre un instrument, ho aprenem perquè volem obtenir alguna mena de recompensa emocional.

paragraphs.en: For most people, that's having fun. However, reaching the stage where we can have fun takes effort, and that process usually isn't fun, at least, there are times when it isn't fun.
paragraphs.ca: Per a la majoria de la gent, això és divertir-se. Tanmateix, arribar a l'etapa en què podem divertir-nos requereix esforç, i aquest procés normalment no és divertit; almenys, hi ha moments en què no ho és.

paragraphs.en: I know that sometimes I just don't want to pick up my guitar at all. Admittedly, this is rare, but sometimes I really have to make myself do it.
paragraphs.ca: Sé que de vegades no em ve gens de gust agafar la guitarra. La veritat és que és estrany, però de vegades m'he d'obligar de debò a fer-ho.

paragraphs.en: When I'm feeling like that, I don't usually have fun playing the guitar, but I know I need to at least do something, so I do something.
paragraphs.ca: Quan em sento així, normalment no em diverteixo tocant la guitarra, però sé que com a mínim he de fer alguna cosa, així que en faig alguna.

paragraphs.en: I also know that when I sit down and work on something, the next day I am much better at it Other times, I can easily pick up the guitar But there are things I need to practice that aren't very fun for me to do so But I know will benefit me if I do And a lot of times I really enjoy practicing The point is, practice isn't always fun Most of the time it should be a sort of rewarding concentration Sometimes practice puts us in an almost trance-like state
paragraphs.ca: També sé que quan m'assec i treballo una cosa, l'endemà me'n surto molt millor. Altres vegades agafo la guitarra amb facilitat. Però hi ha coses que he de practicar que no em resulten gaire divertides de fer, i tot i així sé que em beneficiaran si les faig. I moltes vegades gaudeixo de debò practicant. El cas és que la pràctica no sempre és divertida. La majoria del temps hauria de ser una mena de concentració gratificant. De vegades la pràctica ens posa en un estat quasi de trànsit

paragraphs.en: But it isn't always fun, and that's okay. It is important to anticipate that it won't always be fun, so that when this happens to you, rather than getting carried away in the emotion, you understand it and do some practice anyway.
paragraphs.ca: Però no sempre és divertida, i no passa res. És important preveure que no sempre serà divertida, perquè quan et passi, en lloc de deixar-te endur per l'emoció, ho entenguis i practiquis una mica igualment.

paragraphs.en: The difference between practicing and playing. This is a progress killer. A lot of the time when people pick up their guitars thinking they're practicing, they're actually playing.
paragraphs.ca: La diferència entre practicar i tocar. Això mata el progrés. Moltes vegades, quan la gent agafa la guitarra pensant que practica, en realitat està tocant.

paragraphs.en: Playing guitar is when you are repeating a set of motions that you have previously learned. Practicing is when you are training your body on a new set of motions.
paragraphs.ca: Tocar la guitarra és quan repeteixes un conjunt de moviments que ja has après abans. Practicar és quan entrenes el cos amb un conjunt de moviments nous.

paragraphs.en: These could be variations on something previously learned or something new. If you look at how much time you are practicing, you will probably find you are playing and not doing much practice at all.
paragraphs.ca: Aquests poden ser variacions d'alguna cosa apresa abans o una cosa nova. Si mires quant de temps passes practicant, probablement veuràs que estàs tocant i que no practiques gairebé gens.

paragraphs.en: If you are not practicing, you are not improving. Now, I'm not saying that you should spend all your time practicing, and don't spend any time playing your favorite songs, but if you want to continuously improve your playing, you need to ensure that there is a proportion of your time devoted to practicing, and generally speaking, the more time practicing, the faster you will improve.
paragraphs.ca: Si no practiques, no millores. Ara bé, no dic que hagis de passar tot el temps practicant i no dedicar mai temps a tocar les teves cançons preferides, però si vols millorar contínuament la teva manera de tocar, has d'assegurar-te que hi ha una part del teu temps dedicada a practicar i, en general, com més temps practiquis, més de pressa milloraràs.

paragraphs.en: Not understanding how to learn This is a critical piece of the puzzle that we will cover in detail later in the book. If you do not understand how to learn or what the purpose of learning is, then you will not progress and you will not have fun.
paragraphs.ca: No saber com aprendre. Aquesta és una peça crítica del trencaclosques que tractarem amb detall més endavant al llibre. Si no entens com aprendre ni quina és la finalitat d'aprendre, no progressaràs i no et divertiràs.

paragraphs.en: It's as simple as that.
paragraphs.ca: Així de simple.

paragraphs.en: Unfortunately, we are never taught how to learn effectively. In school, we are taught that the process of learning is the memorization of almost random facts.
paragraphs.ca: Malauradament, mai no ens ensenyen a aprendre eficaçment. A l'escola ens ensenyen que el procés d'aprendre és la memorització de fets gairebé aleatoris.

paragraphs.en: This is simply not true. Memorization is a part of learning, but learning also requires integration and application. It requires understanding the context of the facts that you are studying and identifying the essentials behind each idea.
paragraphs.ca: Això simplement no és veritat. La memorització és una part de l'aprenentatge, però aprendre també requereix integració i aplicació. Requereix entendre el context dels fets que estudies i identificar l'essencial que hi ha darrere de cada idea.

paragraphs.en: And without these critical parts, your learning will be ineffective. Setting the wrong standard for progress This one is killer.
paragraphs.ca: I sense aquestes parts crítiques, el teu aprenentatge serà ineficaç. Fixar un criteri equivocat per al progrés. Aquest és letal.

paragraphs.en: When we set the wrong standard for being able to feel good about our playing, we are setting ourselves up to feel miserable about our playing for life.
paragraphs.ca: Quan fixem el criteri equivocat per poder sentir-nos bé amb la nostra manera de tocar, ens predisposem a sentir-nos desgraciats amb la nostra manera de tocar tota la vida.

paragraphs.en: It doesn't take too much imagination to picture that someone who feels miserable about playing an instrument will not want to play it for very long.
paragraphs.ca: No cal gaire imaginació per figurar-se que algú que se sent desgraciat tocant un instrument no voldrà tocar-lo durant gaire temps.

paragraphs.en: When it comes to learning an instrument, 99% of students will compare themselves to their favourite player. They are continuously judging their ability against someone who is a master of their craft, Unsurprisingly, they continuously come up short.
paragraphs.ca: Quan es tracta d'aprendre un instrument, el 99% dels estudiants es comparen amb el seu intèrpret preferit. Judiquen contínuament la seva capacitat contra algú que és un mestre del seu ofici i, com era d'esperar, sempre queden curts.

paragraphs.en: Let's make a comparison. Let's say it's your first day at university and your lecturer was giving you a brief overview of a complex topic that you will be studying later in the year.
paragraphs.ca: Fem una comparació. Posem que és el teu primer dia a la universitat i el teu professor et fa una visió general breu d'un tema complex que estudiaràs més endavant durant el curs.

paragraphs.en: It's obvious your lecturer is an expert in this field. Would you feel like a failure because you don't know what your professor does?
paragraphs.ca: És evident que el teu professor és un expert en aquest camp. Et sentiries un fracàs perquè no saps el que sap el teu professor?

paragraphs.en: Of course not. That would be ridiculous. As soon as you think about this for one second, it's obvious that to feel bad because you don't know as much as the expert makes no sense whatsoever because you haven't put in the time like they have, which is why you're there in the first place.
paragraphs.ca: És clar que no. Seria ridícul. Tan bon punt hi penses un segon, és evident que sentir-te malament perquè no saps tant com l'expert no té cap mena de sentit, perquè tu no hi has dedicat el temps que hi ha dedicat ell, que és precisament per això que ets allà.

paragraphs.en: Yet, when it comes to learning guitar, we do this all the time. And because we do this, we make ourselves feel miserable. So the question is, how should we judge our progress?
paragraphs.ca: I tot i així, quan es tracta d'aprendre guitarra, ho fem constantment. I pel fet de fer-ho, ens fem sentir desgraciats. Així que la pregunta és: com hauríem de jutjar el nostre progrés?

paragraphs.en: Should we judge our progress at all? We need to find some metric to evaluate our progress. Otherwise, we risk never improving.
paragraphs.ca: Hauríem de jutjar el nostre progrés, de fet? Hem de trobar alguna mètrica per avaluar el nostre progrés. Si no, correm el risc de no millorar mai.

paragraphs.en: The correct metric that we should use is how we were doing last week. And the correct goal is to be a tiny bit better than we were last week.
paragraphs.ca: La mètrica correcta que hauríem de fer servir és com anàvem la setmana passada. I l'objectiu correcte és ser una mica millor del que érem la setmana passada.

paragraphs.en: Maybe just 1%. That could be 1% faster with our tempo, or playing 1% more consistently, or 1% less tension. You get the idea.
paragraphs.ca: Potser només un 1%. Això pot ser un 1% més ràpid amb el nostre tempo, o tocar un 1% més constantment, o un 1% menys de tensió. Ja m'entens.

paragraphs.en: We just want to be 1% better. Along as you are practicing regularly, this is an achievable goal. In fact, most weeks you will improve more than 1%.
paragraphs.ca: Només volem ser un 1% millors. Sempre que practiquis regularment, aquest és un objectiu assolible. De fet, la majoria de setmanes milloraràs més d'un 1%.

paragraphs.en: So, if you can retrain the criteria for what it takes to feel good about your playing from can I play like my favourite player to did I improve 1% compared to last week, then you are going to feel good about your playing.
paragraphs.ca: Així que, si pots reeducar el criteri sobre què cal per sentir-te bé amb la teva manera de tocar, passant de «puc tocar com el meu intèrpret preferit?» a «he millorat un 1% respecte de la setmana passada?», llavors et sentiràs bé amb la teva manera de tocar.

paragraphs.en: The impact of this is that if you feel good about your playing, you will keep practising and keep improving a few percent each week over a period of several years.
paragraphs.ca: L'impacte d'això és que, si et sents bé amb la teva manera de tocar, continuaràs practicant i millorant uns quants punts percentuals cada setmana durant un període de diversos anys.

paragraphs.en: And all those small improvements will compound into improvements so large that it's difficult for you to imagine at this point in time.
paragraphs.ca: I totes aquestes petites millores es combinaran en millores tan grans que et serà difícil imaginar-les en aquest moment.

paragraphs.en: If you just keep going, improving a little week by week, you will become a monster guitar player.
paragraphs.ca: Si continues endavant, millorant una mica setmana rere setmana, esdevindràs un guitarrista monstruós.

chapters.title: Setting the right expectations for ourselves

segments.text: Setting the correct expectations of ourselves.
One question students often ask is, how long does it take to learn guitar?
That's a bit like asking, how long is a piece of string?
It depends on many factors, all of which we will cover throughout the course of this book.
In general, if you are serious about your guitar playing, learning the guitar is a lifelong
endeavor.
It will take a lifetime to study and learn the various aspects of playing the guitar.
You can't control how fast you learn, but you can control.
The amount of time you put into practice.
Your focus during practice.
what you practice. And generally speaking, when you maximize those things, you learn faster.
If you set yourself a goal of, I want to learn 20 chords in the next five weeks,
you may be disappointed when you don't reach that goal. You can't control how quickly you
learn how to play chords. Saying that, we will look at a few exercises later in the book that
always work for speeding up how quickly you can learn chords. If you set yourself the goal of,
I will spend 45 minutes a day at 8am working on my cords, that is a goal that you can achieve.
And by doing that, you should be able to improve a little bit on where you were last week,
hitting that 1% weekly improvement goal we talked about in the previous section.
When it comes to general practice and technique, that is the method I would use for deciding how
successful my practice has been. My goal is the time spent practicing and the quality of the
practice, not reaching a particular milestone. However, if I am failing to improve, then that
tells me I need to change what I'm practicing. Every now and then, certain events will happen
where you have to perform. You'll have a gig, recording deadline, studio time booked, something
like that. In those situations, you want to ramp up your practice so that the weeks before the event
you are practicing like mad. The night before and the day of the event do light warm-ups,
but focus on relaxing rather than intensity. Save the intensity for when it's time to perform.
To revisit the original question of how long does it take to learn guitar,
while we can't say how long it takes to learn guitar, we can look at how long some pieces take
to learn. Sometime around 2016, I was working on learning Bach's first and second cello suites.
I booked a weekend of lessons with the artist known as the Commander-in-Chief. She's an
electric guitarist who plays virtuoso violin pieces on guitar. While talking in general about music,
I was staggered to learn that classical violinists will spend a year studying a single piece of music
that won't be the only thing they will learn, but they will spend a year working on it.
Before that, I had never considered that I should spend so long learning a piece of music,
or that it was normal to spend so long learning a piece of music. That's probably why these
violinists are so good, if you work at anything for a year, you will find that you start to get
pretty good at it. This is a long way of saying, when it comes to working on something, don't feel
down if it takes you a long time to learn it. It's not taking you a long time, it's taking you a
normal amount of time to learn. Why do we judge ourselves so harshly? Have you ever found yourself
thinking, this is simple. Why is it taking me so long to learn it? I bet you have. Every guitarist
has thought that. I still battle fighting this thought. I find many students suffer from this
idea, and it's quite insidious. It leads to us feeling incompetent as guitar players,
and feeling incompetent is not a good way to feel inspired to focus and practice.
So where does this idea come from, and how can we fight it? I think there are two possible causes.
1. Conflating understanding an idea and performing an idea
2. Not understanding what learning feels like
When looking at two chords on a page, we can usually conceptually understand what we have to do quite quickly, usually within a few seconds
We can read the tab or chord diagram and understand where to place our fingers and how to strum in order to play the two chords
But making our body do that smoothly and in time is another matter
It takes time to train muscle memory and iron out any weird bugs in how we are moving between the two cords
If we assume that the speed at which we can understand how to move our fingers
Should be the same as the amount of time it will take to train the movement of our two fingers
We will continuously be disappointed with ourselves
Additionally, where does this assumption come from?
Why should learning to move our fingers take the same amount of time as being able to read a tab?
I have no idea about the source of this assumption, but by identifying it,
hopefully, you can gain some serenity with your practice.
Another problem that adult students tend to face is that they have forgotten what learning feels like.
We've already talked about this, so we won't cover it again.
But to briefly mention, if you're not used to learning, you can mistake the feeling of learning for the feeling of frustration or failure.
We constantly judge ourselves for not being able to play like XYZ guitarist.
Sure, we might not be able to play a song as our favourite player does now, but that doesn't mean that we can never play the song like them, we just need to practice a bit more.
As a final thought on this topic, any time we learn something new, even if it is composed of
things we already know, we have to mentally treat it like learning from scratch. If you know the
chords E minor, G and D, it may be tempting to think that you should be able to play them in
any order at any time. Let's say you've been playing those chords for years, but never played
them in the following order, G, D, E minor. You try that, struggle to get it as good as you want,
and feel miserable because you think you should be able to do it. If you instead treated it as
something new, you wouldn't be feeling miserable, and you'll practice it and eventually crack it.
Additionally, by what standard should you be able to learn it quickly? If you think about it,
there are no facts supporting why you should just be able to do XYZ quickly. Have you
scientifically measured how fast you can learn something new on guitar? Does learning one thing
mean learning another should be any easier? The thought of this should be easy is a complete
fantasy with no basis in reality. It is ridiculous. Next time you feel that way, realize how ridiculous
the idea is and throw it in the trash where it belongs and instead focus on your practice.
Organizing your practice. There are five levels at which your practice can be organized
and to get the most out of your practice time, you need to consider all five levels.
One, what is the big picture goal for whom you want to be as a guitar player?
Two, how can you structure what you need to learn to achieve that goal, deciding on a learning path?
3. How are you going to plan out your practice time every week?
4. What are you going to work on for the specific practice session you are about to have?
5. Feedback and improvement.
But before we do that, it is important to understand the difference between linear and non-linear practice.
This is a direct reflection of the linear and spiral theories of knowledge that we looked at towards the start of the book.
Linear practice.
This is something that people into lead and shred guitar often fall victim to.

And I know that I certainly fell prey to this trap. Linear practice is when you practice one thing before moving on to the next. For example, you may want to practice rhythm guitar before learning lead guitar. In my case, I always wanted to play as fast as possible, so I put years and years into developing my speed with scale sequences and sweep picking, completely neglecting my ornamentation, such as bends, slides, and vibrato.
I ended up being able to play over 16 notes a second, but my lead playing in general sucked
because I had no ornamentation skills. Fortunately, I since fixed that. Linear practice often leads to
a guitarist being very skilled in a very limited number of areas. Unfortunately, as playing the
guitar in real situations, for example, playing a song from start to finish or playing a nice guitar
solo involves combining a range of skills. The limited range of highly developed skills the
guitar player can do are effectively worthless. Non-linear practice. This is a fancy way of saying
practice several things at once. There is a balance to be struck. If you practice too many different
things, then you end up in the reverse problem of the guitar player who practices linearly,
where you practice so many different things that you are not skilled at any of them.
I usually find that when guitar players are wanting to work on their technique,
having three to seven different items to work on is the right balance.
If there is something in particular that you do want to be highly skilled at, for example speed,
then you could split your practice time between focusing on your speed and the rest of your time on a range of skills.
Setting your big picture goal
It's important to take a moment to think about exactly who you want to be as a guitarist.
Someone who wants to learn to write and play funk music is going to have a different learning path
than someone who wants to compose neoclassical guitar instrumentals for an orchestra.
Someone that wants to learn to play rock songs is going to have a different learning path
than someone who wants to play jazz music.
Now, when starting, it can be difficult to visualize where you want to go with your guitar playing.
Part of the problem is that there are a lot of areas of guitar playing that you might not know about.
There might be genres you haven't heard of, techniques you don't know about, and you might have some misunderstandings about what's involved in certain aspects of playing.
But there will be something that takes your interest.
You'll have music that you enjoy listening to, and maybe guitar players that you admire, so you can start there.
Take something that holds your interest, and move in that direction.
You can always change direction as you learn more about guitar and music, but to get started,
pick something, even if it's to learn three of your favorite songs.
When setting your goal, it should be something positive and concrete.
For example, I don't want to be a bad guitarist is not positive or concrete.
I want to be a good guitarist is positive, but it is not concrete.
Being good doesn't mean anything.
I want to be able to play five Iron Maiden songs is positive and concrete.
This is a goal that we can break down into steps and work towards.
Deciding on your learning path
Now that you know where you want to go with your playing, you have to decide how to get there.
This has a bit of a catch-22 attached to it.
You don't know how to get somewhere you have never been.
So you'll have to find someone who can offer you advice.
You can use forums and Facebook groups.
You might have some friends who play at a level that you want to play
at whom you can ask for advice.
The most effective thing is to find a great teacher
who can put together a plan for you.
You don't necessarily have to take lessons with a teacher,
although I would recommend that,
but you could contact two, three teachers,
tell them your big-picture goal,
and then pay them to put together a plan for you.
Planning your weekly practice time
This is a big secret to effective practice.
Plan your practice time.
Create a schedule for your practice in advance that you will stick to.
I would go as far as writing down your schedule in your calendar, on paper, or however you organize your life.
If you say to yourself, I'm going to practice this week, and leave it at that, chances are you are not going to practice very much.
When planning your practice time, you want to aim to have frequent practice sessions, ideally every day, even if it is just for a few minutes.
Practicing for 15 minutes every day, 105 minutes a week, will be more effective than practicing for 3 hours once a week,
even though practicing for 3 hours once a week is more time in total than 15 minutes once a day.
This is due to several neurophysiological effects of how practice affects our brain
that we will look at later in the book.
When planning your practice time, you always want to consider the time of day
and what else is happening in your life.
For example, if you practice after work, you're going to be tired, hungry, distracted and a little stressed.
If you practice before work, you're going to have your brain at maximum focus
and you will be able to concentrate on what you are going.
Knowing that, one of the most effective things you can do to improve your practice
is to change your daily routine, go to bed a bit earlier in the evening
and wake up earlier so that you can practice before work.
I know that is not possible for everyone, but if it is possible for you,
then seriously consider it.
If you are wanting to make serious progress with your playing,
you want to aim for a minimum of two hours of practice a day,
six days a week. Make sure that if you do aim for this or more, you slowly build up to this
much practice over several weeks. Do not go from playing zero minutes a day to playing two hours a
day overnight. How to wake up. Some people have a hard time waking up in the morning.
I understand it used to take me almost an hour to properly get my brain in gear in the mornings.
I found the following things to help get my brain going as fast as possible.
When you wake up, don't look at your phone.
A lot of people will waste 20, 30, 60 minutes in the morning mindlessly on their phones.
Leave it in a different room overnight, or at least away from the bed,
so you have to physically get out of bed before you can get to your phone.
Get outside and take a 10-minute walk, no matter what the weather is.
The sunlight, fresh air and light exercise will wake you up.
Drink water.
Don't drink anything with caffeine for 60 to 90 minutes after waking up.
Or at least have a pint of water before your coffee.
Consider quitting caffeine altogether, or at least switching to decaf.
You'll probably sleep better after getting past the two-week detox hump.
Do intermittent fasting.
This is great because then you don't need to eat breakfast at all.
Massive time saver.
or at the very least cut out the sugary cereals and carbs at breakfast and eat real food.

paragraphs.en: 5. Feedback and improvement. But before we do that, it is important to understand the difference between linear and non-linear practice.
paragraphs.ca: 5. Retroalimentació i millora. Però abans de fer això, és important entendre la diferència entre la pràctica lineal i la pràctica no lineal.

paragraphs.en: This is a direct reflection of the linear and spiral theories of knowledge that we looked at towards the start of the book.
paragraphs.ca: Això és un reflex directe de les teories lineal i en espiral del coneixement que vam veure a l'inici del llibre.

paragraphs.en: Linear practice. This is something that people into lead and shred guitar often fall victim to. And I know that I certainly fell prey to this trap. Linear practice is when you practice one thing before moving on to the next. For example, you may want to practice rhythm guitar before learning lead guitar. In my case, I always wanted to play as fast as possible, so I put years and years into developing my speed with scale sequences and sweep picking, completely neglecting my ornamentation, such as bends, slides, and vibrato.
paragraphs.ca: Pràctica lineal. És una cosa en què sovint cauen els qui s'interessen per la guitarra solista i el shred. I sé que jo mateix vaig caure en aquest parany. La pràctica lineal és quan practiques una cosa abans de passar a la següent. Per exemple, potser vols practicar la guitarra rítmica abans d'aprendre la solista. En el meu cas, sempre volia tocar tan de pressa com fos possible, així que vaig dedicar anys i anys a desenvolupar la meva velocitat amb seqüències d'escales i sweep picking, descuidant completament l'ornamentació, com els bends, els slides i el vibrato.

paragraphs.en: I ended up being able to play over 16 notes a second, but my lead playing in general sucked because I had no ornamentation skills. Fortunately, I since fixed that. Linear practice often leads to a guitarist being very skilled in a very limited number of areas. Unfortunately, as playing the guitar in real situations, for example, playing a song from start to finish or playing a nice guitar solo involves combining a range of skills. The limited range of highly developed skills the
paragraphs.ca: Vaig acabar podent tocar més de 16 notes per segon, però la meva manera de tocar solista en general feia pena, perquè no tenia cap habilitat d'ornamentació. Afortunadament, des d'aleshores ho vaig arreglar. La pràctica lineal sovint porta un guitarrista a ser molt hàbil en un nombre molt limitat d'àrees. Malauradament, tocar la guitarra en situacions reals, per exemple tocar una cançó de principi a fi o tocar un bon solo de guitarra, implica combinar un ventall d'habilitats. El ventall limitat d'habilitats molt desenvolupades que

paragraphs.en: guitar player can do are effectively worthless. Non-linear practice. This is a fancy way of saying practice several things at once. There is a balance to be struck. If you practice too many different things, then you end up in the reverse problem of the guitar player who practices linearly, where you practice so many different things that you are not skilled at any of them.
paragraphs.ca: el guitarrista pot fer és, efectivament, inútil. Pràctica no lineal. Aquesta és una manera elegant de dir practicar diverses coses alhora. Cal trobar un equilibri. Si practiques massa coses diferents, acabes en el problema invers del guitarrista que practica linealment: practiques tantes coses diferents que no ets hàbil en cap d'elles.

paragraphs.en: I usually find that when guitar players are wanting to work on their technique, having three to seven different items to work on is the right balance.
paragraphs.ca: Normalment trobo que, quan els guitarristes volen treballar la seva tècnica, tenir entre tres i set coses diferents per treballar és l'equilibri adequat.

paragraphs.en: If there is something in particular that you do want to be highly skilled at, for example speed, then you could split your practice time between focusing on your speed and the rest of your time on a range of skills.
paragraphs.ca: Si hi ha alguna cosa en particular en què vols ser molt hàbil, per exemple la velocitat, llavors pots repartir el temps de pràctica entre concentrar-te en la velocitat i dedicar la resta del temps a un ventall d'habilitats.

paragraphs.en: Setting your big picture goal It's important to take a moment to think about exactly who you want to be as a guitarist. Someone who wants to learn to write and play funk music is going to have a different learning path than someone who wants to compose neoclassical guitar instrumentals for an orchestra.
paragraphs.ca: Fixar el teu objectiu global. És important prendre's un moment per pensar exactament qui vols ser com a guitarrista. Algú que vol aprendre a escriure i tocar música funk tindrà un camí d'aprenentatge diferent d'algú que vol compondre instrumentals de guitarra neoclàssica per a una orquestra.

paragraphs.en: Someone that wants to learn to play rock songs is going to have a different learning path than someone who wants to play jazz music.
paragraphs.ca: Algú que vol aprendre a tocar cançons de rock tindrà un camí d'aprenentatge diferent d'algú que vol tocar jazz.

paragraphs.en: Now, when starting, it can be difficult to visualize where you want to go with your guitar playing. Part of the problem is that there are a lot of areas of guitar playing that you might not know about.
paragraphs.ca: Ara bé, quan comences, pot ser difícil visualitzar on vols arribar amb la teva manera de tocar la guitarra. Part del problema és que hi ha moltes àrees de la guitarra que potser no coneixes.

paragraphs.en: There might be genres you haven't heard of, techniques you don't know about, and you might have some misunderstandings about what's involved in certain aspects of playing.
paragraphs.ca: Potser hi ha gèneres que no has sentit mai, tècniques que no coneixes, i potser tens alguns malentesos sobre què impliquen certs aspectes de tocar.

paragraphs.en: But there will be something that takes your interest. You'll have music that you enjoy listening to, and maybe guitar players that you admire, so you can start there.
paragraphs.ca: Però hi haurà alguna cosa que et desperti interès. Tindràs música que t'agrada escoltar i, potser, guitarristes que admires, així que pots començar per aquí.

paragraphs.en: Take something that holds your interest, and move in that direction. You can always change direction as you learn more about guitar and music, but to get started, pick something, even if it's to learn three of your favorite songs.
paragraphs.ca: Agafa una cosa que et mantingui l'interès i mou-te en aquesta direcció. Sempre pots canviar de direcció a mesura que aprenguis més coses sobre la guitarra i la música, però per començar, tria alguna cosa, encara que sigui aprendre tres de les teves cançons preferides.

paragraphs.en: When setting your goal, it should be something positive and concrete. For example, I don't want to be a bad guitarist is not positive or concrete.
paragraphs.ca: A l'hora de fixar el teu objectiu, hauria de ser una cosa positiva i concreta. Per exemple, «no vull ser un mal guitarrista» no és ni positiu ni concret.

paragraphs.en: I want to be a good guitarist is positive, but it is not concrete. Being good doesn't mean anything. I want to be able to play five Iron Maiden songs is positive and concrete.
paragraphs.ca: «Vull ser un bon guitarrista» és positiu, però no és concret. Ser bo no vol dir res. «Vull ser capaç de tocar cinc cançons d'Iron Maiden» és positiu i concret.

paragraphs.en: This is a goal that we can break down into steps and work towards.
paragraphs.ca: Aquest és un objectiu que podem desglossar en passos i cap al qual podem treballar.

paragraphs.en: Deciding on your learning path Now that you know where you want to go with your playing, you have to decide how to get there.
paragraphs.ca: Decidir el teu camí d'aprenentatge. Ara que saps on vols arribar amb la teva manera de tocar, has de decidir com arribar-hi.

paragraphs.en: This has a bit of a catch-22 attached to it. You don't know how to get somewhere you have never been. So you'll have to find someone who can offer you advice.
paragraphs.ca: Això té una mica d'un peix que es mossega la cua. No saps com arribar a un lloc on no has estat mai. Així que hauràs de trobar algú que et pugui donar consell.

paragraphs.en: You can use forums and Facebook groups. You might have some friends who play at a level that you want to play at whom you can ask for advice.
paragraphs.ca: Pots fer servir fòrums i grups de Facebook. Potser tens amics que toquen a un nivell al qual vols arribar i a qui pots demanar consell.

paragraphs.en: The most effective thing is to find a great teacher who can put together a plan for you. You don't necessarily have to take lessons with a teacher, although I would recommend that, but you could contact two, three teachers, tell them your big-picture goal, and then pay them to put together a plan for you.
paragraphs.ca: La cosa més eficaç és trobar un bon professor que et pugui preparar un pla. No cal necessàriament que prenguis classes amb un professor, tot i que ho recomanaria, però podries contactar amb dos o tres professors, explicar-los el teu objectiu global i pagar-los perquè et preparin un pla.

paragraphs.en: Planning your weekly practice time This is a big secret to effective practice. Plan your practice time. Create a schedule for your practice in advance that you will stick to.
paragraphs.ca: Planificar el teu temps de pràctica setmanal. Aquest és un gran secret de la pràctica eficaç. Planifica el teu temps de pràctica. Crea amb antelació un horari per a la pràctica que compliràs.

paragraphs.en: I would go as far as writing down your schedule in your calendar, on paper, or however you organize your life. If you say to yourself, I'm going to practice this week, and leave it at that, chances are you are not going to practice very much.
paragraphs.ca: Jo arribaria fins i tot a escriure el teu horari al calendari, en paper o com organitzis la teva vida. Si et dius «aquesta setmana practicaré» i ho deixes aquí, és probable que no practiquis gaire.

paragraphs.en: When planning your practice time, you want to aim to have frequent practice sessions, ideally every day, even if it is just for a few minutes.
paragraphs.ca: Quan planifiquis el teu temps de pràctica, voldràs tenir sessions de pràctica freqüents, idealment cada dia, encara que sigui només uns quants minuts.

paragraphs.en: Practicing for 15 minutes every day, 105 minutes a week, will be more effective than practicing for 3 hours once a week, even though practicing for 3 hours once a week is more time in total than 15 minutes once a day.
paragraphs.ca: Practicar 15 minuts cada dia, 105 minuts a la setmana, serà més eficaç que practicar 3 hores un cop a la setmana, tot i que practicar 3 hores un cop a la setmana és més temps en total que 15 minuts un cop al dia.

paragraphs.en: This is due to several neurophysiological effects of how practice affects our brain that we will look at later in the book.
paragraphs.ca: Això es deu a diversos efectes neurofisiològics de com la pràctica afecta el nostre cervell, que veurem més endavant al llibre.

paragraphs.en: When planning your practice time, you always want to consider the time of day and what else is happening in your life. For example, if you practice after work, you're going to be tired, hungry, distracted and a little stressed.
paragraphs.ca: Quan planifiquis el teu temps de pràctica, sempre voldràs tenir en compte l'hora del dia i què més passa a la teva vida. Per exemple, si practiques després de la feina, estaràs cansat, amb gana, distret i una mica estressat.

paragraphs.en: If you practice before work, you're going to have your brain at maximum focus and you will be able to concentrate on what you are going.
paragraphs.ca: Si practiques abans de la feina, tindràs el cervell al màxim de concentració i podràs concentrar-te en què estàs

paragraphs.en: Knowing that, one of the most effective things you can do to improve your practice is to change your daily routine, go to bed a bit earlier in the evening and wake up earlier so that you can practice before work.
paragraphs.ca: Sabent això, una de les coses més eficaces que pots fer per millorar la teva pràctica és canviar la teva rutina diària: anar a dormir una mica més d'hora i llevar-te més d'hora per poder practicar abans de la feina.

paragraphs.en: I know that is not possible for everyone, but if it is possible for you, then seriously consider it. If you are wanting to make serious progress with your playing, you want to aim for a minimum of two hours of practice a day, six days a week. Make sure that if you do aim for this or more, you slowly build up to this much practice over several weeks. Do not go from playing zero minutes a day to playing two hours a day overnight. How to wake up. Some people have a hard time waking up in the morning.
paragraphs.ca: Sé que no és possible per a tothom, però si és possible per a tu, considera-ho seriosament. Si vols fer progressos seriosos amb la teva manera de tocar, voldràs apuntar a un mínim de dues hores de pràctica al dia, sis dies a la setmana. Assegura't que, si hi apuntes o a més, vas augmentant poc a poc fins a aquesta quantitat de pràctica al llarg de diverses setmanes. No passis de zero minuts al dia a dues hores al dia d'un dia per l'altre. Com llevar-se. Hi ha gent que ho passa malament per llevar-se al matí.

paragraphs.en: I understand it used to take me almost an hour to properly get my brain in gear in the mornings. I found the following things to help get my brain going as fast as possible.
paragraphs.ca: Ho entenc; abans em costava gairebé una hora posar el cervell en marxa al matí. Vaig trobar que les coses següents ajudaven a posar el meu cervell en marxa tan de pressa com fos possible.

paragraphs.en: When you wake up, don't look at your phone. A lot of people will waste 20, 30, 60 minutes in the morning mindlessly on their phones.
paragraphs.ca: Quan et llevis, no miris el telèfon. Molta gent malgasta 20, 30 o 60 minuts al matí amb el telèfon sense adonar-se'n.

paragraphs.en: Leave it in a different room overnight, or at least away from the bed, so you have to physically get out of bed before you can get to your phone.
paragraphs.ca: Deixa'l en una altra habitació durant la nit, o com a mínim lluny del llit, de manera que hagis de sortir físicament del llit abans de poder arribar al telèfon.

paragraphs.en: Get outside and take a 10-minute walk, no matter what the weather is. The sunlight, fresh air and light exercise will wake you up.
paragraphs.ca: Surt a fora i fes una caminada de 10 minuts, faci el temps que faci. La llum del sol, l'aire fresc i una mica d'exercici et despertaran.

paragraphs.en: Drink water. Don't drink anything with caffeine for 60 to 90 minutes after waking up. Or at least have a pint of water before your coffee.
paragraphs.ca: Beu aigua. No beguis res amb cafeïna durant 60 o 90 minuts després de llevar-te. O, com a mínim, beu una pinta d'aigua abans del cafè.

paragraphs.en: Consider quitting caffeine altogether, or at least switching to decaf. You'll probably sleep better after getting past the two-week detox hump.
paragraphs.ca: Considera deixar la cafeïna del tot, o com a mínim passar a la descafeïnada. Probablement dormiràs millor després de superar el mal tràngol de les dues setmanes de desintoxicació.

paragraphs.en: Do intermittent fasting. This is great because then you don't need to eat breakfast at all. Massive time saver. or at the very least cut out the sugary cereals and carbs at breakfast and eat real food.
paragraphs.ca: Fes dejuni intermitent. És fantàstic, perquè llavors no cal esmorzar gens. Un estalvi de temps enorme. O, com a mínim, elimina els cereals ensucrats i els hidrats de carboni de l'esmorzar i menja menjar de veritat.

chapters.title: What are you working on in each practice session?

segments.text: What are you working on for each specific practice session?
Now that you have planned your long-term goals, a way to reach them and when you will be practicing,
the last step is to think about what you will be practicing in those scheduled practice sessions.
In general, I recommend having three to seven things that you are working on with your playing at any one time.
You want to ensure that your practice time is balanced appropriately, which is an ongoing skill.
Be careful with taking on more than seven things to practice.
You will end up not being able to spend enough time on any one item to improve at it.
The perfect practice routine.
I want to take a minute here to point out that there is no such thing as the perfect practice routine,
only an appropriate practice routine for this point in time.
You will find that your practice routine changes and evolves as your abilities, goals and demands on your life change.
Anyway, back to talking about practice.
There are three ways you can consider organizing your practice time.
1. The rotating practice system.
2. AB system
3. 1. Item system
The rotating practice system
This system works best for people that are working on 3 to 7 different practice items,
which are exercises to work on different skill sets,
and the person in question also has a fluctuating amount of time that they can practice for each day.
We want to make sure that you can evenly practice all items.
Let's say there are 7 things you want to practice.
Practice items A, B, C, D, E, F, and G.
Let's also say that your weekly practice schedule looks like this.
Monday, 60 minutes.
Tuesday, 15 minutes.
Wednesday, 45 minutes.
Thursday, 15 minutes.
Friday, 30 minutes.
Saturday, 60 minutes.
Sunday, 45 minutes.
I would practice your items for 15 minutes each as follows.
Monday, 60 minutes total, A, B, C, D.
Tuesday, 15 minutes total, E.
Wednesday, 45 minutes total, F, G, A.
Thursday, 15 minutes total, B.
Friday, 30 minutes total, C, D.
Saturday, 60 minutes total, E, F, G, A.
Sunday, 45 minutes total, B, C, D.
This way, you rotate through your practice items evenly, ensuring that they all receive nearly the same attention.
You can physically organize this system by printing out or writing down your exercises.
Have one page per exercise.
Label each page if you want to and put them all on your music stand for practice.
Set your practice timer for 15 minutes and practice the exercise in front of you.
When your timer goes off, move that exercise to the back of the pile.
Set your timer for 15 minutes and start on the next exercise.
This system is incredibly simple and easy to follow.
It allows you to sit down and get started with no preparation or fluffing around.
This system does not have to be rigid.
When I was following this system several years ago,
if I found myself having a breakthrough moment with a certain exercise
and I was smashing my personal bests with the metronome,
I would run with it for the rest of that practice session
and see just how far I could go,
then resume the rotation system the following day.
A-B system.
This is effective for people that want to work on several areas of their playing
and have a consistent practice schedule
where they can practice for roughly the same amount of time each day.
You break up your practice items into Day A items and Day B items, and you're alternate between the two.
For example, you could have technique exercises on Day A and a song you are learning to focus on for Day B.
This practice schedule allows you to work a little deeper on certain items than the rotating system.
1. Item System
If you are practicing for a gig or a recording session, then you will want to distribute your time differently,
focusing on the project that you have to complete. Maybe you'll be putting 75% of your practice time
into practicing songs and only 25% into working on your technique. For this system, nearly all
your time goes into practicing for the project. I would still put some time, even if it is not much,
into working on technique and other skills, even if it is just a warm-up exercise or two.
Which system is right for you?
We've outlined three different systems for organizing your practice.
You'll have to decide which one is best for you.
Pick one system and stick to it for two to three months, then change it as you see necessary.
You don't have to stick to one system for the rest of your life,
but you do want to stick to it for at least two to three months.
You can create hybrids of these systems.
As with anything, think about what it is you're trying to achieve.
Figure out a way to do that.
Try a system out for a couple of months and then assess how it's going.
Feedback and improvement.
Whatever you are practicing, you want to be aware of what it is you are doing.
As obvious as that sounds, it can be surprisingly difficult.
When you are focusing on trying to move your fingers in a certain way with something a bit new,
it can be difficult to really listen to what you are doing and observe those motions objectively.
There will be things that you are aware of and also things that you are not aware of.
One benefit to having a teacher is you get instant feedback on what you are doing.
Another highly effective method of getting feedback is to record yourself.
This will allow you to focus on listening so you can dissect what you are doing
and figure out which bits of an exercise need the most work.
You will also find it beneficial to keep a short log of your practice.
Record things like the maximum tempos that you reach and mistakes you are making.
Is there a particular point of an exercise that you are consistently struggling with?
A chord change that is a bit ropey?
Whatever feedback you are getting, whether it's from a teacher or your own video audio recording,
make notes on it in your practice log.
If you have printed your exercises on paper, you can keep a practice log on the back of each sheet.
This way, when you next come to that practice item, you will know what it is you need to focus on.
This also stops you from fiddling around with computer programs and keeps you focused on the task at hand.
We will look at specific practice techniques later in the book.
How much should you practice?
Practicing more is better than practicing less.
If you want to play at the highest levels, then you'll need to be practicing for a few hours a day, at least three.
Steve Vai was famous for his immense nine-hour guitar workout that he used to do.
Michelangelo Battio would practice his picking for two hours every day
to develop the insane speed he achieved.
Ingwi Malmsteen would fall asleep with his guitar in his hands.
If you want to be at the top levels of playing, that's what it takes.
If you're a beginner, you want to build up your practice time over a period of weeks to months,
going from practicing for 10 minutes a day to practicing for 10 hours a day will result in injury.

Practicing for extended periods is very taxing on the nerves, tendons and ligaments, and by increasing practice time over a longer period, you give the body a chance to strengthen these connective tissues.
If you are wanting to increase your practice time, do so in 15-minute increments, a week at a time.
If you want to increase your practice time faster, add extra practice time at opposite ends of the day.
For example, if you practice for an hour in the morning,
you could add a 30-minute practice session in the evening.
By practicing at opposite ends of the day,
you give the body a chance to rest between sessions.
You also want to take micro-breaks when practicing.
For every repetition of an exercise,
take 5 seconds to consciously relax your arms and hands.
Every 10, 15 minutes, take a break,
get up and walk for 10 seconds before getting started on the next practice item.
Once a week, I like to take a day off from practicing to let my body rest.
I'll also take days off as needed.
For example, yesterday I was practicing and started feeling a bit sore,
so I took the rest of the day off from practicing.
Warning signs of injury.
This and the following sections are not medical advice, just my experience.
It is possible to injure yourself from playing the guitar.
This can be caused by practicing too much, and having bad technique can make this worse.
See the appendix for the correct way to sit with your guitar.
Common injuries that guitar players get are tennis elbow and carpal tunnel syndrome.
These are both quite serious problems that can be permanent.
More often than not, our body warns us before becoming injured,
and it is important to be able to spot these warning signs.
If your fingertips are sore, that is okay. While I don't recommend it, you can lose skin and get
blisters on your fingertips, and while uncomfortable, this will heal. If you ever feel shooting pains,
stabbing pains, like someone has stabbed you with a pointy pencil, burning sensations or pins and
needles, then you need to stop playing immediately and not play for the rest of the day. Usually,
resting for the day, and maybe the next day, will leave you feeling fine. Bathing the problem area
in icy cold water for a few minutes after practice can help recovery. Avoiding injury.
Doing a light yoga routine before and after practice can help prevent injuries. There are
books and DVDs available on Amazon that cover yoga for musicians. Any of them are probably fine.
I've used a DVD called Yoga for Musicians by Penelope Roskell
which I found very effective at a time when I was recovering from an injury
When practicing, take lots of little breaks
In the section on how to use a metronome properly
I advise that you have a bar of count-in between repetitions of exercises
In addition to refocusing your mind and figuring out where the count is
You can use this as an opportunity to purposely relax your arms and hands before the next repetition starts.
Every 15 minutes, put the guitar down for a few minutes and have a stretch.
Walk to the kitchen and back or something to get your body moving a little.
Again, when you start feeling warning signs of injury, put the guitar down.
Never play through the pain.
That is a stupid thing to do.
I know because I have made that mistake several times in the past, including one injury which
meant taking several months off from playing the guitar so that I could recover, during which my
arm was almost unusable. If you do any tasks in your daily life that have a risk of RSI,
such as a lot of typing, then research proper posture and technique to avoid repetitive injury.
Make sure you take breaks. This will take some strain off your connective tissues,
and they won't be quite as tired when it comes to practicing the guitar.
