paragraphs.ca: Això et dona la informació que necessites per arreglar el problema. Ara ja pots concentrar-te a moure correctament aquell primer dit i resoldre el problema.

paragraphs.en: So when you are trying to diagnose your guitar playing problems, take a minute to think through what is going on and be as specific as possible.
paragraphs.ca: Així que, quan intentis diagnosticar els problemes de la teva manera de tocar la guitarra, pren-te un minut per pensar què està passant i sigues tan específic com puguis.

paragraphs.en: Sometimes when playing, it can be difficult to figure out what our hands are doing as we are so focused on playing. If this is the case, video yourself on your phone and watch the video back and figure out what it is you are doing.
paragraphs.ca: De vegades, quan toquem, pot ser difícil esbrinar què fan les nostres mans, perquè estem tan concentrats a tocar. Si és el cas, grava't amb el mòbil i mira el vídeo per esbrinar què és el que estàs fent.

paragraphs.en: Next, we'll look at some specific strategies that you can use to fix the problems that you are having.
paragraphs.ca: A continuació veurem algunes estratègies concretes que pots fer servir per arreglar els problemes que tens.

paragraphs.en: Isolation Let's say you are working on a song that is five minutes long. Most guitar players tend to practice songs by playing through them from start to finish.
paragraphs.ca: L'aïllament. Diguem que estàs treballant una cançó de cinc minuts. La majoria de guitarristes tendeixen a practicar les cançons tocant-les de principi a fi.

paragraphs.en: Let's also say that there is a chord change you are struggling with towards the end of the song. A lot of players will practice by playing through the song, hitting the difficult chord change, screwing up and going back to the start for a second attempt.
paragraphs.ca: Diguem també que hi ha un canvi d'acord que et costa cap al final de la cançó. Molts guitarristes practiquen tocant la cançó sencera, arriben al canvi d'acord difícil, s'equivoquen i tornen al principi per a un segon intent.

paragraphs.en: Earlier in the book, we talked about the distinction between practicing and playing. In this case, you are spending most of your practice time playing the guitar and not practicing.
paragraphs.ca: Abans, al llibre, hem parlat de la diferència entre practicar i tocar. En aquest cas, passes la major part del temps de pràctica tocant la guitarra i no pas practicant.

paragraphs.en: 95% of the song is within your ability. It is only the 5%, that chord change at the end, that needs to be practiced. So why not spend all the practice time practicing the hard stuff?
paragraphs.ca: El 95% de la cançó està dins de les teves capacitats. Només cal practicar aquell 5%, el canvi d'acord del final. Així que per què no dedicar tot el temps de pràctica a practicar la part difícil?

paragraphs.en: A more efficient way to practice would be to take the chord change at the end and set up a loop using Guitar Pro, or your DAW, to practice that specific part of the song that you are struggling with.
paragraphs.ca: Una manera més eficient de practicar seria agafar el canvi d'acord del final i crear un bucle amb el Guitar Pro, o amb el teu DAW, per practicar aquella part concreta de la cançó que et costa.

paragraphs.en: Let's also say that you have 30 minutes to practice a day. In 30 minutes, the 5-minute song can be played 6 times. That's not very many times.
paragraphs.ca: Diguem també que tens 30 minuts al dia per practicar. En 30 minuts, la cançó de 5 minuts es pot tocar 6 vegades. No són gaires vegades.

paragraphs.en: It's going to take a while to get that last chord change correct if you can only play it 6 times. The problematic chord change is in a 15-second section of music.
paragraphs.ca: Trigarem una bona estona a encertar aquell últim canvi d'acord si només el podem tocar 6 vegades. El canvi d'acord problemàtic és en un fragment de música de 15 segons.

paragraphs.en: If you were to isolate and practice the difficult chord change, you could practice that 120 times in 30 minutes.
paragraphs.ca: Si aïllessis i practiquessis el canvi d'acord difícil, podries practicar-lo 120 vegades en 30 minuts.

paragraphs.en: 120 repetitions versus 6 repetitions. So in this example, by practicing using isolation, you will progress 120 times faster than if you play the song all the way through from start to finish.
paragraphs.ca: 120 repeticions contra 6 repeticions. Així, en aquest exemple, practicant amb aïllament progressaràs 120 vegades més de pressa que si toques la cançó sencera de principi a fi.

paragraphs.en: This isn't to say that you should never play songs from start to finish. You should, and doing so is important to practice, especially if you are rehearsing for a gig.
paragraphs.ca: Això no vol dir que no hagis de tocar mai les cançons de principi a fi. Sí que ho has de fer, i fer-ho és important per practicar, sobretot si estàs assajant per a un concert.

paragraphs.en: But when there is something you are struggling with, isolate it and work intensely on it to solve it. Then go back to playing the song all the way through.
paragraphs.ca: Però quan hi ha alguna cosa que et costa, aïlla-la i treballa-la intensament per resoldre-la. Després torna a tocar la cançó sencera.

paragraphs.en: Isolation to the ridiculous. When practicing, you may find that your hands do weird things from time to time. When you find this happening, you can take the concept of isolation to the extreme and isolate the specific hand that is causing the problem.
paragraphs.ca: L'aïllament portat a l'extrem. Quan practiquis, potser veuràs que les teves mans fan coses estranyes de tant en tant. Quan et passi això, pots portar el concepte d'aïllament a l'extrem i aïllar la mà concreta que causa el problema.

paragraphs.en: For example, if your left hand is doing something weird, take the motion that you are trying to achieve and practice moving your left hand that way.
paragraphs.ca: Per exemple, si la mà esquerra fa alguna cosa estranya, agafa el moviment que vols aconseguir i practica de moure la mà esquerra d'aquesta manera.

paragraphs.en: Don't worry about the right hand. Put it down by your side so that it doesn't distract you. Just focus on moving your left hand correctly.
paragraphs.ca: No et preocupis per la mà dreta. Baixa-la al costat del cos perquè no et distregui. Concentra't només a moure correctament la mà esquerra.

paragraphs.en: You will find that after 5 to 10 minutes, you have solved the problem. If you have a problem with your right hand, for example, trying a complex string skipping pattern, then you can do exactly the same thing. Put your left hand down by your side and practice moving the right hand correctly, just playing through open strings. You can take this even further and apply it to individual finer movements that are proving problematic.
paragraphs.ca: Veuràs que, al cap de 5 o 10 minuts, hauràs resolt el problema. Si tens un problema amb la mà dreta, per exemple per provar un patró complex de salts de corda, pots fer exactament el mateix. Baixa la mà esquerra al costat del cos i practica de moure correctament la mà dreta, tocant només cordes a l'aire. Ho pots portar encara més enllà i aplicar-ho a moviments individuals més fins que et resultin problemàtics.

paragraphs.en: Synchronization. This technique applies specifically to scale-based problems you may be having. When we start to push the limits of how fast we can play with scale-based exercises, the two hands often start to go out of sync with each other.
paragraphs.ca: Sincronització. Aquesta tècnica s'aplica específicament als problemes basats en escales que puguis tenir. Quan comencem a empènyer els límits de la velocitat a què podem tocar amb exercicis basats en escales, sovint les dues mans comencen a perdre la sincronia entre elles.

paragraphs.en: We can improve that by playing each note in the exercise twice. As an example, let's say you were working on the following melody.
paragraphs.ca: Ho podem millorar tocant cada nota de l'exercici dues vegades. Com a exemple, diguem que estaves treballant la melodia següent.

paragraphs.en: Figure 8, tab example. When we double up each note, we get figure 9, tab example. Note that we are keeping the same note value as the original.
paragraphs.ca: Figura 8, exemple de tablatura. Quan doblem cada nota, obtenim la figura 9, exemple de tablatura. Fixa't que mantenim el mateix valor de nota que a l'original.

paragraphs.en: In this case, everything is being played with 8th notes. We would be using alternate picking in this case. By playing the exercise like this, we force our hands to move at different rates.
paragraphs.ca: En aquest cas, tot es toca amb corxeres. En aquest cas faríem servir la pua alternada. Si toquem l'exercici així, forcem les mans a moure's a ritmes diferents.

paragraphs.en: In the original exercise, we pick eighth notes, and our fret hand also changes with eighth notes. In the second exercise, our pick hand is still playing eighth notes, but now the fretting hand is moving at a quarter note speed.
paragraphs.ca: A l'exercici original, piquem corxeres amb la pua, i la mà dels trastes també canvia al ritme de les corxeres. Al segon exercici, la mà de la pua continua tocant corxeres, però ara la mà dels trastes es mou a velocitat de negra.

paragraphs.en: You will find playing the exercise this way does wonders for your synchronization, and will help you push the original exercise to higher tempos while being more accurate.
paragraphs.ca: Veuràs que tocar l'exercici d'aquesta manera fa meravelles per a la teva sincronització i t'ajudarà a portar l'exercici original a tempos més alts amb més precisió.

paragraphs.en: Practicing chord changes. I thought I would add this section as something a lot of guitar players struggle with is improving their chord changes.
paragraphs.ca: Practicar els canvis d'acord. He pensat d'afegir aquesta secció perquè una cosa que costa molt a molts guitarristes és millorar els canvis d'acord.

paragraphs.en: They either can't change fast enough, or their fingers can't find the right place on the neck, or their fingers just do weird stuff.
paragraphs.ca: O bé no poden canviar prou de pressa, o bé els dits no troben el lloc correcte al mànec, o bé els dits fan coses estranyes.

paragraphs.en: So here are some of my best tips for improving your chord changes on guitar. Grip and release. This is a simple and highly effective exercise.
paragraphs.ca: Així que aquí tens alguns dels meus millors consells per millorar els canvis d'acord a la guitarra. Prémer i deixar anar. Aquest és un exercici senzill i molt efectiu.

paragraphs.en: Hold the cord down really, really hard. You should be holding it down so hard that the tips of your fingernails turn yellow.
paragraphs.ca: Agafa l'acord ben fort, molt fort. L'has de prémer tan fort que les puntes de les ungles se't tornin grogues.

paragraphs.en: Hold the cord down like this for 6 to 8 seconds, then relax. When you relax, completely relax your arm and hand down by your side.
paragraphs.ca: Aguanta l'acord així durant 6 o 8 segons, i després relaxa't. Quan et relaxis, relaxa completament el braç i la mà baixant-los al costat del cos.

paragraphs.en: When telling students to relax their arm completely, I often see them relax their hand partially, which is not what I ask them to do.
paragraphs.ca: Quan dic als alumnes que relaxin el braç completament, sovint els veig que relaxen la mà només parcialment, i això no és el que els demano.

paragraphs.en: So make sure that you relax your arm completely. You must relax your arm as you are introducing massive amounts of tension into your arm and that needs to be dissipated. Repeat the exercise five to six times for each chord that you are working on. You will find that this exercise helps your fingers find the chord faster. Slow changes. When it comes to moving your hand to a new chord, there are two stages. One, moving the hand so that the hand is roughly over the correct
paragraphs.ca: Així que assegura't de relaxar el braç completament. Has de relaxar el braç, perquè hi estàs introduint quantitats enormes de tensió i cal dissipar-la. Repeteix l'exercici cinc o sis vegades per a cada acord que treballis. Veuràs que aquest exercici ajuda els dits a trobar l'acord més de pressa. Canvis lents. A l'hora de moure la mà cap a un acord nou, hi ha dues etapes. Una, moure la mà de manera que quedi més o menys sobre els

paragraphs.en: frets. Two, move your fingers to the right strings and frets. Step one is quite easy. Moving your arm horizontally up or down a few frets on the guitar doesn't take any skill or thought. Step two is a lot trickier. You have to use precise motor skills to hold down the correct chord. Your ability to execute step one quickly will often far exceed your ability to execute step two quickly. Often, a student will move their hand quickly to the right position, then their fingers will flail
paragraphs.ca: trastes correctes. Dos, moure els dits cap a les cordes i els trastes correctes. L'etapa u és força fàcil. Moure el braç horitzontalment amunt o avall uns quants trastes a la guitarra no requereix cap habilitat ni cap pensament. L'etapa dos és molt més complicada. Has de fer servir habilitats motores precises per prémer l'acord correcte. Sovint, la teva capacitat d'executar l'etapa u de pressa superarà de bon tros la teva capacitat d'executar l'etapa dos de pressa. Sovint, un alumne mou la mà de pressa cap a la posició correcta, i llavors els dits es posen a voleiar

paragraphs.en: around as they try to hold down the cord as quickly as they move their hand, which they cannot do. I like to call this effect Bambi on ice, as their fingers look like a baby deer trying to stand whilst walking on ice. But in all seriousness, this creates a problem. Every time you move your hand this way, you are practicing wiggling your fingers. You are not practicing holding down the cord correctly. You need to practice moving your fingers directly to where
paragraphs.ca: d'una banda a l'altra mentre intenten prémer l'acord tan de pressa com mouen la mà, cosa que no poden fer. M'agrada anomenar aquest efecte «en Bambi sobre gel», perquè els seus dits semblen un cérvol petit que intenta estar dret mentre camina sobre gel. Però, parlant seriosament, això crea un problema. Cada vegada que mous la mà d'aquesta manera, practiques el fet de bellugar els dits. No practiques prémer l'acord correctament. Has de practicar de moure els dits directament allà on

paragraphs.en: they need to go, not going all over the neck before they find the right spot. To fix this, take your hand off the guitar, relax it by your side, then bring your hand back to the neck, slowly. Make sure each finger moves directly to where it needs to go to hold down the chord that you are learning. You should not be rearranging your fingers, and they should not be wiggling or dancing over the strings. If they do any of these things, you are moving too fast, and you must
paragraphs.ca: han d'anar, i no pas de recórrer tot el mànec abans de trobar el lloc correcte. Per arreglar-ho, treu la mà de la guitarra, relaxa-la al costat del cos i torna a portar la mà al mànec, a poc a poc. Assegura't que cada dit es mou directament allà on ha d'anar per prémer l'acord que estàs aprenent. No hauries de reordenar els dits, i no s'haurien de bellugar ni ballar sobre les cordes. Si fan cap d'aquestes coses, vas massa de pressa i has de

paragraphs.en: slow down. You may be surprised at just how slowly you need to move your fingers to do this correctly, but take the time. The secret to learning guitar quickly is to practice things slowly.
paragraphs.ca: reduir la velocitat. Potser t'estranyarà la lentitud amb què has de moure els dits per fer-ho correctament, però pren-te el temps. El secret per aprendre guitarra de pressa és practicar les coses a poc a poc.

paragraphs.en: Practicing too fast is not practicing at all, it's just wasting time. You can also apply this exercise to moving between two chords. Right hand always in time. We often struggle when practicing a new chord change because it's new. This is normal and to be expected. So when practicing, we'll be playing through a few chords, we get to the one that we are struggling with, and we can't quite play it in time. Every time we get to that chord, it takes us a little longer
paragraphs.ca: Practicar massa de pressa no és practicar, és només perdre el temps. També pots aplicar aquest exercici per moure't entre dos acords. La mà dreta sempre a temps. Sovint ens costa practicar un canvi d'acord nou perquè és nou. Això és normal i és d'esperar. Així que, quan practiquem, toquem uns quants acords, arribem al que ens costa i no som capaços de tocar-lo ben bé a temps. Cada vegada que hi arribem, triguem una mica més

paragraphs.en: to find it than the other chords that we are playing. We move our fret hand to the correct position, it takes us a little longer to find that position, and then our strumming hand finally strums the strings, much later than we wanted to. Every time we do this, we are practicing playing out of time. We are practicing leaving extra time for this particular chord. Here's how we fix that. Play through the chord progression using a metronome and keep the strumming hand
paragraphs.ca: a trobar-lo que amb els altres acords que toquem. Movem la mà dels trastes a la posició correcta, triguem una mica més a trobar aquesta posició, i llavors la mà del rasgueig finalment toca les cordes, molt més tard del que volíem. Cada vegada que fem això, practiquem tocar fora de temps. Practiquem deixar temps extra per a aquest acord concret. Aquí tens com arreglar-ho. Toca la progressió d'acords amb un metrònom i mantén la mà del rasgueig

paragraphs.en: perfectly in time, even if the left hand can't find the chord. This will be quite difficult, as you've been practicing playing the chord out of time for so long. And when you do this, you will find that you make a horrible sound from your guitar. And when you do it the next time, you will find that you still make a horrible sound from your guitar. But if you persist, you will find that after 10 to 15 repetitions, your chord change starts to feel a bit smoother.
paragraphs.ca: perfectament a temps, encara que la mà esquerra no trobi l'acord. Això serà força difícil, perquè fa tant de temps que practiques tocar l'acord fora de temps. I quan ho facis, veuràs que surt un so horrible de la teva guitarra. I quan ho facis el cop següent, veuràs que encara surt un so horrible de la teva guitarra. Però si hi persisteixes, veuràs que després de 10 o 15 repeticions el teu canvi d'acord comença a semblar una mica més fluid.

paragraphs.en: If it doesn't start feeling better after 10 to 15 repetitions, then slow down the metronome and isolate the chord change. See the previous section on isolation.
paragraphs.ca: Si no comença a anar millor després de 10 o 15 repeticions, afluixa el metrònom i aïlla el canvi d'acord. Consulta la secció anterior sobre l'aïllament.

paragraphs.en: This is a weird way to practice, but it is very effective. Think ahead. When you start to become a bit more advanced at guitar, you have to start moving your body and thinking out of time with the music to be able to play in time.
paragraphs.ca: Aquesta és una manera estranya de practicar, però és molt efectiva. Pensar per endavant. Quan comences a ser una mica més avançat a la guitarra, has de començar a moure el cos i a pensar fora del temps de la música per poder tocar a temps.

paragraphs.en: This is a good example of that idea. When you are holding down a particular chord, you are holding down that particular chord.
paragraphs.ca: Aquest és un bon exemple d'aquesta idea. Quan estàs prement un acord concret, estàs prement aquell acord concret.

paragraphs.en: Obvious, right? This means that you do not need to be thinking about that chord. This means that you can be thinking about the next chord that you want to play.
paragraphs.ca: És obvi, oi? Això vol dir que no cal que pensis en aquest acord. Vol dir que pots estar pensant en el proper acord que vols tocar.

paragraphs.en: While holding down any particular chord, have your brain think ahead about what the next chord will be. Try and visualize it in your mind and you will find your fingers can find it a little easier.
paragraphs.ca: Mentre prems qualsevol acord concret, fes que el teu cervell pensi per endavant en quin serà el proper acord. Intenta visualitzar-lo a la ment i veuràs que els dits el troben una mica més fàcilment.

chapters.title: Look where you want to play

segments.text: Look where you want to play. In addition to thinking about the chord you want to play, physically look at where you want your hand to be.
Often, new guitar players will only look at where they want to move their hand when it's time to play that chord, or even worse, they'll be staring off into space while practicing.
This means that the beat comes around, they move their head to look at where they want to play the next chord, and then they move their hands to play the chord.
By the time the beat has come around, it is already too late.
Moving your head creates a split second that is lost before you can start moving your hand.
In the previous idea, we talked about thinking ahead of time.
You also want to look ahead of time.
While playing a particular chord, you don't need to look at it,
so physically move your head and look at where the next chord will go.
This will save you a lot of time and help you play those chords more accurately.
This does not apply to just chord changes, but everything you want to do on guitar.
Physically look ahead before you need to and you'll find your playing improves.
Rubber band arm
This is a killer problem for getting your chords in time.
Often, a student will strum a chord, then their arm will rest between the high string and the floor.
They wait for the beat to come around, hold down the next chord,
and then bring their arm up to the bass strings so that they can then strum the chord.
The act of bringing the arm up creates a small delay between when they want to play the chord
and when they can play the chord, and that small delay often throws out their timing.
This is easy to fix.
After strumming a chord, bring the arm back up to the bass strings automatically.
Pretend that your arm has a giant rubber band attached, from your wrist to your neck,
and every time you strum down, bring the arm back up so that it is ready and waiting for the next chord.
This will save you a lot of time and make your strumming much better.
Anticipate the beat.
This is the final problem that students face when strumming, anticipating the beat.
Often, especially at the early stages, a student will wait for the click on the metronome to sound before they then play.
Of course, by the time you have heard the metronome, it is too late to play in time with the metronome.
The click must be anticipated.
At first, you will be effectively guessing when the click is going to sound,
but with practice, you will quickly improve and develop the skill to be able to anticipate the metronome.
The metronome must always be anticipated and never waited for
Set your practice for what you are practicing for
Recently, I played a couple of concerts with a cellist
I had written an album of duets for electric guitar and cello
And the cellist and I performed them at a couple of concerts
However, the first gig did not go so well for me
While I had practiced plenty, I found it much harder than I should have
This was partially down to nerves, but there was something else going on
After the gig, I tried to figure out what had made the performance so challenging
Eventually, I figured it out
I had been practicing listening to a metronome playing over the cello parts
And without that metronome, I had to listen to the cello to stay in time
Something that I had not practiced doing before, which I found incredibly taxing mentally
To put it another way, I had practiced focusing my listening on the metronome, not the cellist.
Without the metronome, I had to focus on the cellist to stay in time. There was a two-week
gap before the next gig, so I turned off the metronome, learned the cello score in depth,
and figured out which parts of the cello melody started each bar and my parts overlapped with
so that I could stay in time. I practiced listening to the cellist while playing my parts on top.
This is another great advantage of using a D.O.W. to practice, which we'll go over later.
The second gig went much better.
The moral of the story here is that you have to practice for the conditions that you are going to be playing in.
Now, this isn't to say, don't use a metronome.
Metronomes are a vital part of practice and should be an early step in learning whatever piece of music you are playing.
But once you can play in time with a metronome, you have to learn to play in time with whatever instruments you will be playing with.
For most of the people reading this, that will be a drum kit.
This isn't training your ability to stay in time, but it is training your ability to listen to specific instruments while playing.
If possible, get the drummer in your band to write out their parts in mid-D.
then you can import the MIDI into your DAW,
mock up some drums,
and learn how the drums work with your guitar parts.
Then you will always have rock-solid timing when playing with your band.
Practicing for speed
We previously discussed how when it comes to practice,
you want to practice playing accurately,
and that speed will naturally develop from accuracy.
But there are a few things we can do to push things along faster.
Practice technique exercises on acoustic guitar.
Spend a few minutes when you're working on your technique exercises playing them on an acoustic guitar.
Acoustic guitar strings, compared to electric guitar strings, are big and heavy.
After playing the acoustic for a few minutes, switch back to electric.
You will find that your fingers feel a lot lighter on the strings and will fly over the fretboard.
Time Expectations for Developing Speed
Developing speed takes time. Michael Angelo Battio, worth a listen if you've never heard of
him, has previously said that he spent two hours a day just working on his technique for two years
to take it to the insane levels he reached. Hitting those high levels of technique takes
a minimum of practicing three hours a day. If you're going to commit to an intensive training
program with this much practice, bear in mind everything we discussed earlier about warning
signs of injury, building up your practice over time, and keeping a healthy body.
How to practice without a guitar. We don't always have a guitar to hand,
so what can we do to practice in those situations? There are a few things that we can do.
1. Visualization. 2. Mental practice. 3. Picking practice. 4. Composing. 5. Reading.
Visualization
When it comes to playing scales and chords on the guitar,
we have to mentally recall the shape or pattern that we want to use,
then we create that pattern on the guitar.
If we are away from the guitar, we can practice recalling these shapes in our mind.
This can be a highly effective way to improve your ability to remember shapes.
A while ago, a student of mine went on a cycling holiday with her partner.
There were some challenging climbs on their route, and during those climbs, she would picture in her mind where different arpeggio shapes are on the guitar.
She came back from that holiday with excellent arpeggio recall.
You could give her a chord progression, and she would be able to play it as arpeggios on the spot.
While I wouldn't recommend you do this while you're driving or doing some complex skill where you have to focus,
if you are on the bus with a few minutes to kill, this is a great way to make that time productive.
Mental practice
Several studies have shown that practicing in your mind, where you picture yourself practicing in the short term, is just as effective as actually practicing with an instrument.
So when you are away from your guitar, you can shut your eyes and focus, and picture yourself playing a piece of music.
This is effective for about a week, after which real practice is more beneficial.
Another way you can practice in your mind is to go over music theory concepts.
You can run through the notes in a scale, scale harmonizations, notes in a chord, pivot chords for modulation.
Just about any music theory concept you can think of, you can run through in your mind or on paper.
Picking practice
This works well if you wear jeans.
Your jeans have a chunky seam down the side of the leg.
You can use this seam to simulate a string.
Take your pick, use a metronome on your phone that you can listen to with headphones,
and using your pick, pick a rhythm against the seam of your jeans in time with the metronome.
This is an incredibly effective way to focus on a particular rhythm that you may be struggling with.
If you're sitting on the train for 20 minutes, that's 20 minutes of intensive rhythm practice you can do.
If you're doing that once a day, Monday to Friday, that comes to 86.67 hours of extra rhythm practice a year.
These little things can add up when you take a long-term view of your playing.
Compose
This one may be a little harder depending on your environment, but is a great use of time.
You can use a laptop, tablet or paper and compose some music.
Write a chord progression, a prelude, a rondo, a sonata, or some other form.
Write a song.
Work on lyrics for a song.
Composing away from the guitar can be a great way to unlock creative ideas
that you wouldn't have had if you were composing on guitar.
Understanding some music theory is a real help when doing this,
as you won't rely on your improvisation skills to compose.
Reading.
Last, but certainly not least, if you are away from your guitar, you can read a book.
There are a lot of great music theory books that you can read that will give you a new
insight into music and how it works.
You can take a book of blank music notation and a pencil and work through problems.
When travelling to Spain a couple of years ago, I would take some blank notation and
a theory book and work on counterpoint problems in the airport lounge and on the plane.
It was a very productive flight. I'll include a list of music theory books I recommend in the
appendix. How to deal with bad practice days. Sometimes things are just not working on the
guitar. We can't focus, can't play like normal. We're just having a bit of an off day. On these
days, try and find something that you can do. Maybe it's something like jamming along to a
backing track, or practice a simple scale much slower than usual, or taking some normal aspect
of your practice routine and just doing 10 minutes on it before calling it quits.
Find something that you can do so that you avoid days where you don't do anything.
If you allow yourself days to do nothing aside from your rest day, then you will find these
days become more frequent. If you get yourself doing something, even if it isn't for long,
you will find you have fewer unproductive days and also develop your work ethic nicely.
Section 3. Studying

paragraphs.en: Look where you want to play. In addition to thinking about the chord you want to play, physically look at where you want your hand to be.
paragraphs.ca: Mira on vols tocar. A més de pensar en l'acord que vols tocar, mira físicament on vols que sigui la mà.

paragraphs.en: Often, new guitar players will only look at where they want to move their hand when it's time to play that chord, or even worse, they'll be staring off into space while practicing.
paragraphs.ca: Sovint, els guitarristes novells només miren on volen moure la mà quan toca tocar aquell acord o, encara pitjor, es queden mirant el buit mentre practiquen.

paragraphs.en: This means that the beat comes around, they move their head to look at where they want to play the next chord, and then they move their hands to play the chord.
paragraphs.ca: Això vol dir que arriba el temps, giren el cap per mirar on volen tocar l'acord següent i després mouen les mans per tocar l'acord.

paragraphs.en: By the time the beat has come around, it is already too late. Moving your head creates a split second that is lost before you can start moving your hand.
paragraphs.ca: Quan arriba el temps, ja és massa tard. Moure el cap crea una fracció de segon que es perd abans no puguis començar a moure la mà.

paragraphs.en: In the previous idea, we talked about thinking ahead of time. You also want to look ahead of time. While playing a particular chord, you don't need to look at it, so physically move your head and look at where the next chord will go.
paragraphs.ca: En la idea anterior, vam parlar de pensar amb antelació. També vols mirar amb antelació. Mentre toques un acord concret, no cal que el miris, així que mou físicament el cap i mira on anirà el proper acord.

paragraphs.en: This will save you a lot of time and help you play those chords more accurately. This does not apply to just chord changes, but everything you want to do on guitar.
paragraphs.ca: Això t'estalviarà molt de temps i t'ajudarà a tocar aquests acords amb més precisió. No s'aplica només als canvis d'acord, sinó a tot el que vulguis fer amb la guitarra.

paragraphs.en: Physically look ahead before you need to and you'll find your playing improves.
paragraphs.ca: Mira físicament endavant abans que calgui i veuràs com millora la teva manera de tocar.

paragraphs.en: Rubber band arm This is a killer problem for getting your chords in time. Often, a student will strum a chord, then their arm will rest between the high string and the floor.
paragraphs.ca: El braç de goma elàstica. Aquest és un problema terrible per fer que els acords arribin a temps. Sovint, un alumne rasqueja un acord i després el braç es queda descansant entre la corda aguda i el terra.

paragraphs.en: They wait for the beat to come around, hold down the next chord, and then bring their arm up to the bass strings so that they can then strum the chord.
paragraphs.ca: Espera que arribi el temps, prem l'acord següent i després aixeca el braç cap a les cordes greus per poder rasquejar l'acord.

paragraphs.en: The act of bringing the arm up creates a small delay between when they want to play the chord and when they can play the chord, and that small delay often throws out their timing.
paragraphs.ca: El fet d'aixecar el braç crea un petit retard entre quan vol tocar l'acord i quan pot tocar-lo, i aquest petit retard sovint li desbarata el tempo.

paragraphs.en: This is easy to fix. After strumming a chord, bring the arm back up to the bass strings automatically. Pretend that your arm has a giant rubber band attached, from your wrist to your neck, and every time you strum down, bring the arm back up so that it is ready and waiting for the next chord.
paragraphs.ca: Això és fàcil de corregir. Després de rasquejar un acord, torna a pujar el braç cap a les cordes greus automàticament. Imagina't que el braç té una goma elàstica gegant enganxada, del canell al coll de la guitarra, i cada cop que rasquegis cap avall, torna a pujar el braç perquè estigui a punt i esperant el proper acord.

paragraphs.en: This will save you a lot of time and make your strumming much better.
paragraphs.ca: Això t'estalviarà molt de temps i millorarà molt la teva manera de rasquejar.

paragraphs.en: Anticipate the beat. This is the final problem that students face when strumming, anticipating the beat. Often, especially at the early stages, a student will wait for the click on the metronome to sound before they then play.
paragraphs.ca: Anticipa el temps. Aquest és l'últim problema que afronten els alumnes quan rasquegen: anticipar el temps. Sovint, sobretot en les primeres etapes, un alumne espera que soni el clic del metrònom abans de tocar.

paragraphs.en: Of course, by the time you have heard the metronome, it is too late to play in time with the metronome. The click must be anticipated.
paragraphs.ca: És clar que, quan ja has sentit el metrònom, és massa tard per tocar a temps amb ell. El clic s'ha d'anticipar.

paragraphs.en: At first, you will be effectively guessing when the click is going to sound, but with practice, you will quickly improve and develop the skill to be able to anticipate the metronome.
paragraphs.ca: Al principi, en realitat endevinaràs quan sonarà el clic, però amb pràctica milloraràs de seguida i desenvoluparàs l'habilitat d'anticipar el metrònom.

paragraphs.en: The metronome must always be anticipated and never waited for
paragraphs.ca: El metrònom sempre s'ha d'anticipar i mai s'ha d'esperar

paragraphs.en: Set your practice for what you are practicing for Recently, I played a couple of concerts with a cellist I had written an album of duets for electric guitar and cello And the cellist and I performed them at a couple of concerts However, the first gig did not go so well for me While I had practiced plenty, I found it much harder than I should have This was partially down to nerves, but there was something else going on
paragraphs.ca: Prepara la pràctica per allò per què practiques. Fa poc vaig fer un parell de concerts amb una violoncel·lista per a qui havia escrit un disc de duets per a guitarra elèctrica i violoncel. I la violoncel·lista i jo els vam interpretar en un parell de concerts. Tanmateix, el primer concert no em va anar gaire bé. Tot i que havia practicat prou, em va costar molt més del que hauria estat normal. En part va ser pels nervis, però hi havia alguna cosa més.

paragraphs.en: After the gig, I tried to figure out what had made the performance so challenging Eventually, I figured it out I had been practicing listening to a metronome playing over the cello parts And without that metronome, I had to listen to the cello to stay in time Something that I had not practiced doing before, which I found incredibly taxing mentally To put it another way, I had practiced focusing my listening on the metronome, not the cellist.
paragraphs.ca: Després del concert, vaig intentar esbrinar què havia fet tan difícil l'actuació. Al final ho vaig entendre. Havia estat practicant escoltant un metrònom que tocava sobre les parts de violoncel. I sense aquell metrònom, havia d'escoltar el violoncel per mantenir el temps. Una cosa que no havia practicat mai abans i que em resultava increïblement feixuga mentalment. Dit d'una altra manera, havia practicat centrar l'escolta en el metrònom, no en la violoncel·lista.

paragraphs.en: Without the metronome, I had to focus on the cellist to stay in time. There was a two-week gap before the next gig, so I turned off the metronome, learned the cello score in depth, and figured out which parts of the cello melody started each bar and my parts overlapped with so that I could stay in time. I practiced listening to the cellist while playing my parts on top.
paragraphs.ca: Sense el metrònom, havia de centrar-me en la violoncel·lista per mantenir el temps. Hi havia un interval de dues setmanes abans del concert següent, així que vaig apagar el metrònom, vaig aprendre a fons la partitura de violoncel i vaig esbrinar quines parts de la melodia del violoncel començaven cada compàs i amb quines s'encavalcaven les meves per poder mantenir el temps. Vaig practicar escoltar la violoncel·lista mentre tocava les meves parts a sobre.

paragraphs.en: This is another great advantage of using a D.O.W. to practice, which we'll go over later. The second gig went much better.
paragraphs.ca: Aquest és un altre gran avantatge de fer servir una DAW per practicar, que veurem més endavant. El segon concert va anar molt millor.

paragraphs.en: The moral of the story here is that you have to practice for the conditions that you are going to be playing in. Now, this isn't to say, don't use a metronome.
paragraphs.ca: La moral de la història és que has de practicar per a les condicions en què tocaràs. Ara bé, això no vol dir que no facis servir un metrònom.

paragraphs.en: Metronomes are a vital part of practice and should be an early step in learning whatever piece of music you are playing.
paragraphs.ca: Els metrònoms són una part vital de la pràctica i haurien de ser un dels primers passos en aprendre qualsevol peça de música que toquis.

paragraphs.en: But once you can play in time with a metronome, you have to learn to play in time with whatever instruments you will be playing with.
paragraphs.ca: Però un cop saps tocar a temps amb un metrònom, has d'aprendre a tocar a temps amb qualsevol instrument amb què tocaràs.

paragraphs.en: For most of the people reading this, that will be a drum kit. This isn't training your ability to stay in time, but it is training your ability to listen to specific instruments while playing.
paragraphs.ca: Per a la majoria de la gent que llegeix això, serà una bateria. Això no entrena la teva capacitat de mantenir el temps, però sí que entrena la teva capacitat d'escoltar instruments concrets mentre toques.

paragraphs.en: If possible, get the drummer in your band to write out their parts in mid-D. then you can import the MIDI into your DAW, mock up some drums, and learn how the drums work with your guitar parts.
paragraphs.ca: Si és possible, demana al bateria de la teva banda que escrigui les seves parts en MIDI, i després podràs importar el MIDI a la teva DAW, muntar una maqueta de bateria i aprendre com funciona la bateria amb les teves parts de guitarra.

paragraphs.en: Then you will always have rock-solid timing when playing with your band.
paragraphs.ca: Així sempre tindràs un tempo sòlid com una roca quan toquis amb la teva banda.

paragraphs.en: Practicing for speed We previously discussed how when it comes to practice, you want to practice playing accurately, and that speed will naturally develop from accuracy.
paragraphs.ca: Practicar per a la velocitat. Abans hem parlat de com, pel que fa a la pràctica, vols practicar tocant amb precisió, i que la velocitat es desenvoluparà de manera natural a partir de la precisió.

paragraphs.en: But there are a few things we can do to push things along faster.
paragraphs.ca: Però hi ha unes quantes coses que podem fer per accelerar-ho tot plegat.

paragraphs.en: Practice technique exercises on acoustic guitar. Spend a few minutes when you're working on your technique exercises playing them on an acoustic guitar.
paragraphs.ca: Practica els exercicis de tècnica amb guitarra acústica. Dedica uns minuts, quan treballes els exercicis de tècnica, a tocar-los amb una guitarra acústica.

paragraphs.en: Acoustic guitar strings, compared to electric guitar strings, are big and heavy. After playing the acoustic for a few minutes, switch back to electric.
paragraphs.ca: Les cordes de la guitarra acústica, comparades amb les de la guitarra elèctrica, són gruixudes i pesades. Després de tocar l'acústica uns minuts, torna a l'elèctrica.

paragraphs.en: You will find that your fingers feel a lot lighter on the strings and will fly over the fretboard.
paragraphs.ca: Veuràs que els dits se senten molt més lleugers sobre les cordes i volaran pel mànec.

paragraphs.en: Time Expectations for Developing Speed Developing speed takes time. Michael Angelo Battio, worth a listen if you've never heard of him, has previously said that he spent two hours a day just working on his technique for two years to take it to the insane levels he reached. Hitting those high levels of technique takes a minimum of practicing three hours a day. If you're going to commit to an intensive training program with this much practice, bear in mind everything we discussed earlier about warning
paragraphs.ca: Expectatives de temps per desenvolupar la velocitat. Desenvolupar velocitat requereix temps. Michael Angelo Batio, que val la pena escoltar si no l'has sentit mai, ha dit que va passar dues hores al dia treballant només la seva tècnica durant dos anys per portar-la als nivells d'esbojament que va assolir. Assolir aquests nivells alts de tècnica requereix un mínim de tres hores de pràctica al dia. Si et compromets amb un programa d'entrenament intensiu amb tanta pràctica, tingues present tot el que hem comentat abans sobre els senyals

paragraphs.en: signs of injury, building up your practice over time, and keeping a healthy body.
paragraphs.ca: d'alerta de lesió, augmentar la pràctica gradualment i mantenir un cos saludable.

paragraphs.en: How to practice without a guitar. We don't always have a guitar to hand, so what can we do to practice in those situations? There are a few things that we can do.
paragraphs.ca: Com practicar sense guitarra. No sempre tenim una guitarra a mà, així que què podem fer per practicar en aquestes situacions? Hi ha unes quantes coses que podem fer.

paragraphs.en: 1. Visualization. 2. Mental practice. 3. Picking practice. 4. Composing. 5. Reading.
paragraphs.ca: 1. Visualització. 2. Pràctica mental. 3. Pràctica de pua. 4. Composició. 5. Lectura.

paragraphs.en: Visualization When it comes to playing scales and chords on the guitar, we have to mentally recall the shape or pattern that we want to use, then we create that pattern on the guitar.
paragraphs.ca: Visualització. A l'hora de tocar escales i acords a la guitarra, hem de recordar mentalment la forma o el patró que volem fer servir, i després creem aquest patró a la guitarra.

paragraphs.en: If we are away from the guitar, we can practice recalling these shapes in our mind. This can be a highly effective way to improve your ability to remember shapes.
paragraphs.ca: Si som lluny de la guitarra, podem practicar recordar aquestes formes mentalment. Aquesta pot ser una manera molt efectiva de millorar la teva capacitat de recordar formes.

paragraphs.en: A while ago, a student of mine went on a cycling holiday with her partner. There were some challenging climbs on their route, and during those climbs, she would picture in her mind where different arpeggio shapes are on the guitar.
paragraphs.ca: Fa un temps, una alumna meva se'n va anar de vacances en bicicleta amb la seva parella. Hi havia pujades exigents a la ruta i, durant aquestes pujades, s'imaginava on són les diferents formes d'arpegi a la guitarra.

paragraphs.en: She came back from that holiday with excellent arpeggio recall. You could give her a chord progression, and she would be able to play it as arpeggios on the spot.
paragraphs.ca: Va tornar d'aquelles vacances amb un record d'arpegis excel·lent. Li podies donar una progressió d'acords i era capaç de tocar-la com a arpegis a l'instant.

paragraphs.en: While I wouldn't recommend you do this while you're driving or doing some complex skill where you have to focus, if you are on the bus with a few minutes to kill, this is a great way to make that time productive.
paragraphs.ca: Tot i que no et recomanaria que ho fessis mentre condueixes o mentre fas alguna habilitat complexa que requereixi concentració, si ets a l'autobús amb uns minuts per matar, aquesta és una bona manera de fer que aquell temps sigui productiu.

paragraphs.en: Mental practice Several studies have shown that practicing in your mind, where you picture yourself practicing in the short term, is just as effective as actually practicing with an instrument.
paragraphs.ca: Pràctica mental. Diversos estudis han demostrat que practicar mentalment, imaginant-te a curt termini que practiques, és tan efectiu com practicar de debò amb un instrument.

paragraphs.en: So when you are away from your guitar, you can shut your eyes and focus, and picture yourself playing a piece of music. This is effective for about a week, after which real practice is more beneficial.
paragraphs.ca: Així, quan siguis lluny de la guitarra, pots tancar els ulls i concentrar-te, i imaginar-te tocant una peça de música. Això és efectiu durant aproximadament una setmana, després de la qual la pràctica real és més beneficiosa.

paragraphs.en: Another way you can practice in your mind is to go over music theory concepts. You can run through the notes in a scale, scale harmonizations, notes in a chord, pivot chords for modulation.
paragraphs.ca: Una altra manera de practicar mentalment és repassar conceptes de teoria musical. Pots repassar les notes d'una escala, les harmonitzacions d'escala, les notes d'un acord, els acords pivot per a la modulació.

paragraphs.en: Just about any music theory concept you can think of, you can run through in your mind or on paper.
paragraphs.ca: Gairebé qualsevol concepte de teoria musical que se t'acudeixi el pots repassar mentalment o sobre paper.

paragraphs.en: Picking practice This works well if you wear jeans. Your jeans have a chunky seam down the side of the leg. You can use this seam to simulate a string.
paragraphs.ca: Pràctica de pua. Això funciona bé si portes texans. Els texans tenen una costura gruixuda al llarg de la cama. Pots fer servir aquesta costura per simular una corda.

paragraphs.en: Take your pick, use a metronome on your phone that you can listen to with headphones, and using your pick, pick a rhythm against the seam of your jeans in time with the metronome.
paragraphs.ca: Agafa la pua, posa un metrònom al mòbil que puguis escoltar amb auriculars i, amb la pua, toca un ritme contra la costura dels texans a temps amb el metrònom.

paragraphs.en: This is an incredibly effective way to focus on a particular rhythm that you may be struggling with. If you're sitting on the train for 20 minutes, that's 20 minutes of intensive rhythm practice you can do.
paragraphs.ca: Aquesta és una manera increïblement efectiva de centrar-te en un ritme concret amb què potser tens dificultats. Si estàs assegut al tren durant 20 minuts, són 20 minuts de pràctica intensiva de ritme que pots fer.

paragraphs.en: If you're doing that once a day, Monday to Friday, that comes to 86.67 hours of extra rhythm practice a year. These little things can add up when you take a long-term view of your playing.
paragraphs.ca: Si ho fas un cop al dia, de dilluns a divendres, això són 86,67 hores de pràctica extra de ritme a l'any. Aquestes petites coses sumen quan mires la teva manera de tocar a llarg termini.

paragraphs.en: Compose This one may be a little harder depending on your environment, but is a great use of time. You can use a laptop, tablet or paper and compose some music.
paragraphs.ca: Compon. Aquest potser és una mica més difícil segons el teu entorn, però és un gran aprofitament del temps. Pots fer servir un portàtil, una tauleta o paper i compondre una mica de música.

paragraphs.en: Write a chord progression, a prelude, a rondo, a sonata, or some other form. Write a song. Work on lyrics for a song. Composing away from the guitar can be a great way to unlock creative ideas that you wouldn't have had if you were composing on guitar.
paragraphs.ca: Escriu una progressió d'acords, un preludi, un rondo, una sonata o alguna altra forma. Escriu una cançó. Treballa la lletra d'una cançó. Compondre lluny de la guitarra pot ser una gran manera de desbloquejar idees creatives que no hauries tingut si composessis amb la guitarra.

paragraphs.en: Understanding some music theory is a real help when doing this, as you won't rely on your improvisation skills to compose.
paragraphs.ca: Entendre una mica de teoria musical ajuda molt a fer això, perquè no dependràs de les teves habilitats d'improvisació per compondre.

paragraphs.en: Reading. Last, but certainly not least, if you are away from your guitar, you can read a book. There are a lot of great music theory books that you can read that will give you a new insight into music and how it works.
paragraphs.ca: Lectura. Per últim, però no per això menys important, si ets lluny de la guitarra, pots llegir un llibre. Hi ha molts bons llibres de teoria musical que pots llegir i que et donaran una nova visió de la música i de com funciona.

paragraphs.en: You can take a book of blank music notation and a pencil and work through problems. When travelling to Spain a couple of years ago, I would take some blank notation and a theory book and work on counterpoint problems in the airport lounge and on the plane.
paragraphs.ca: Pots agafar un llibre de notació musical en blanc i un llapis i resoldre problemes. Quan vaig viatjar a Espanya fa un parell d'anys, agafava notació en blanc i un llibre de teoria i treballava problemes de contrapunt a la sala d'espera de l'aeroport i a l'avió.

paragraphs.en: It was a very productive flight. I'll include a list of music theory books I recommend in the appendix. How to deal with bad practice days. Sometimes things are just not working on the guitar. We can't focus, can't play like normal. We're just having a bit of an off day. On these days, try and find something that you can do. Maybe it's something like jamming along to a backing track, or practice a simple scale much slower than usual, or taking some normal aspect
paragraphs.ca: Va ser un vol molt productiu. Inclouré una llista de llibres de teoria musical que recomano a l'apèndix. Com afrontar els dies de mala pràctica. De vegades les coses simplement no funcionen amb la guitarra. No ens podem concentrar, no podem tocar com de costum. Simplement tenim un dia fluix. En aquests dies, intenta trobar alguna cosa que puguis fer. Potser és improvisar sobre una base, o practicar una escala senzilla molt més a poc a poc del que és habitual, o agafar algun aspecte normal

paragraphs.en: of your practice routine and just doing 10 minutes on it before calling it quits. Find something that you can do so that you avoid days where you don't do anything.
paragraphs.ca: de la teva rutina de pràctica i fer-ne només 10 minuts abans de plegar. Troba alguna cosa que puguis fer per evitar dies en què no fas res.

paragraphs.en: If you allow yourself days to do nothing aside from your rest day, then you will find these days become more frequent. If you get yourself doing something, even if it isn't for long, you will find you have fewer unproductive days and also develop your work ethic nicely.
paragraphs.ca: Si et permets dies per no fer res a part del teu dia de descans, veuràs que aquests dies es fan més freqüents. Si aconsegueixes fer alguna cosa, encara que no sigui per gaire estona, veuràs que tens menys dies improductius i que també desenvolupes bé la teva ètica de treball.

paragraphs.en: Section 3. Studying
paragraphs.ca: Secció 3. Estudi

segments.text: Section 3. Studying
Towards the start of this book, we discussed how creativity can be seen as taking different concepts and mixing them.
So it stands to reason that the more concepts you know and truly understand,
the more ideas you will be able to experiment with and try out.
Hence, the more creative you will become.
In this section, we are going to go over some approaches you can take to studying to help you learn more effectively.
Learning effectively is key to creativity.
Some problems take a long time to solve.
Albert Einstein is famous for his theory of special relativity,
and later, general relativity.
Archimedes is famous for his theory on buoyancy.
When we hear the stories of great thinkers and their discoveries,
we are often told of the breakthrough moment when the pieces finally fell into place
and they figured out the problem.
What we are rarely told is the amount of thinking that happened before that moment,
thinking time that is often measured in months or even years. Einstein spent ten years thinking
over the problems around special relativity before he had a breakthrough that enabled him
to publish his groundbreaking theory. When considering a problem, people are often quick
to dismiss their ability to solve the problem or understand the lesson if they are unable to
instantly grasp it. Sometimes problems need a little time to solve. This is completely normal,
but something that seems to have been forgotten. Next time you are stuck with a problem you can't
figure out, sit for five minutes and try and crack it. When you are working on some music
theory concept you are struggling with, give yourself a few days to work through it. Some
more complex theories and topics may take you months to work through, or even years. That's okay.
The important thing is that you, one, stick at it, two, progress a little more than you did last week,
laying out your ideas. One of the biggest roadblocks people face in solving problems in
music is understanding the information. This applies to everything from writing chord
progressions to composing a symphony. Often people try and do things in their head,
but there is too much to consider and they get confused and make mistakes.
Lay out the relevant pieces of information on paper.
This lets you consider things more easily.
When laying things out on paper, make sure you do so in a way that makes sense.
Before you consider the problem, consider the best way to organize solving the problem.
Figuring out how to lay out the information clearly is a problem itself that needs to be solved,
and figuring this out might take a few attempts.
I usually find with music theory problems, once you lay out the information properly on paper, the solution becomes obvious.
Annotated scores or diagrammatic blocks are usually helpful ways to lay out ideas.
Tables can be useful when working with chords.
Prose is almost certainly the wrong way to lay out a music theory problem,
unless you are sketching plot ideas for a concept album, lyrics, or a libretto.
To summarize, problem solving has three steps.
1. Consider the best way to approach solving the problem.
2. Lay that out on paper.
3. Solve the problem.
Where to learn from.
We live in an age with countless sources of information at our fingertips.
The downside is that this can be overwhelming.
With so many sources of information available, where should you learn from?
There are four main sources I...

I'm going to recommend. One, textbooks. Two, courses. Three, teachers. Four, playing in a band slash duo slash ensemble, etc. Let's discuss a little bit about the concept of learning, then we will come back to these sources and others.
We mention towards the start of this book that concepts exist in an interconnected hierarchy.
Some concepts are simpler than others.
To understand complex concepts, we must first understand the simpler concepts on which they rely.
We can think of a song as being a complex concept, relying on the concepts of harmony, melody, structure, rhythm, and texture.
We can think of harmony as a complex concept relying on the simpler concepts of intervals and scales.
When learning any subject, especially something as complex as music, we want to move from lower-level concepts to higher-level concepts.
We need to understand how these concepts are structured vertically and also how they are interconnected to each other.
Good textbooks, courses and teachers achieve this by giving clear structure to the ideas that they are presenting.
You can also see why things such as YouTube and magazines are not so effective for proper learning.
The lessons are not structured.
This isn't to say that you shouldn't use things like YouTube and magazines.
They are a great way to supplement your learning, providing material around the subject you are studying,
but I would strongly advise against using them as your main source.
Additionally, while there is a wealth of information on YouTube,
it rarely goes into the depth that a textbook or teacher will go into.
How to find good books, courses, teachers
Now that we know what type of material we want to look for, we need to narrow it down.
First, how can you tell if something is relevant to what you are wanting to study?
And second, how can we tell if it is any good?
Reviews can be helpful.
If you are looking at a teacher or a course, you can look at the musical output of that teacher or course creator.
Do you like their records and the music that they have released?
Do you like their playing?
When it comes to courses, they often have testimonials on the sales page or website.
Try and find the people that gave the testimonial and ask them what they really think.
Testimonials are great, but they are sometimes taken out of context.
When looking at testimonials, make sure that the testimonial aligns with the outcome that you want.
For example, if you are looking at a course on how to write melodies,
and all the testimonials say things like,
I really enjoyed this course, and this is a great course,
then maybe that course isn't so good.
If the testimonials include recordings of the songs that the people who took the course wrote,
then there is a better chance the course will be helpful.
If the reviews say something like,
I went from struggling to compose to being able to easily write new melodies,
then there is a better chance the course will be useful.
If the testimonials include recordings of the songs that the people who took the course wrote,
then there is a better chance the course will be helpful.
If the reviews say something like,
I went from struggling to compose to being able to easily write new melodies,
then there is a better chance the course will be useful.
Getting opinions from others in Facebook groups and Reddit groups can also be useful.
A couple of years ago, I was trying to find a music theory textbook that would explain classical form
and had some very helpful advice from Reddit groups.
It might inevitably take a few tries to find what you were looking for.
You may have to try out a few different teachers, courses or books before you find one that clicks with you.
You may find you want to study with multiple sources at once.
When trying a source out, try and stick to it for at least a month before deciding if it is working for you, unless it is truly horrific.
Warning signs of bad teachers.
Having said that, there are a lot of bad teachers out there.
Here are a few signs you can use to filter out bad teachers and find a good teacher when you are searching.
1. You want a teacher that asks you about your specific goals.
2. Your teacher should not swear in your initial communications.
3. What do their previous students say about them?
4. Do you leave their lessons feeling like you have learned something or progressed?
5. Do they spend lessons talking about their life or teaching you?
6. If you make a serious effort but do not get the results, do they blame you?
Those are the warning signs of a bad teacher.
The major warning sign of an inexperienced teacher is that they will give you too much to do each lesson.
Every lesson will be new material, and you don't have enough time to practice the previous material properly,
even if you are practicing a reasonable amount each day.
They might be a good teacher, but are overestimating how much new material you need.
If you think they are worth continuing with, then ask them to rein things back a bit.
An extreme and slightly dark side to bad teachers is that some cultivate a cult-like attitude around them.
Yes, guitar cults do exist.
This is usually done as a marketing ploy, as those in a cult do not question it and will keep paying to be a member.
You can spot these cults by, one, looking at what the members say.
Are they all repeating buzzwords without really understanding or questioning those ideas?
2. What results are they getting? Are they all mediocre guitar players talking about the secrets
to playing well? 3. Do they posture to have insider knowledge or secrets that no one else does?
4. Does leaving the cult have negative consequences, no longer being able to talk to your former
friends? 5. Do they encourage you to stop talking to your friends? Fortunately, these are rare,
but they are out there, and it's worth knowing how to spot the warning signs.
The benefits of playing in a band. I'll include bands, slash duos, slash ensembles, etc.,
under this playing with other people. FYI an ensemble is just a group of musicians playing
together. Playing in a band is a real-world test of your musical abilities, and if there are any
holes or weaknesses, they will very quickly be exposed. It is also an incredibly fun thing to do.
Being in a band will force you to listen to all the other instruments that are playing
and make sure that you know the songs you are playing inside out. You will also find it's an
opportunity to work on your communication skills, leadership skills and management skills. Getting a
band to the level where you are playing small pub shows takes work in all these areas. If you look
at the biographies of great guitar players, it is quite common that they started playing in bands
that performed very early. If you're struggling to find other people to form a band with, you can
try. 1. Local Facebook groups. 2. Ask your teacher. 3. Phone local teachers of other instruments and
ask if any of their students want to form a band. 4. Internet websites for finding band members.
5. Ask online communities you are part of
6. University societies can be a good way to meet people if you are a student
7. Ask your friends if they know anyone
There is a lot that can go into a band that is outside the scope of this book, but I may write an article or two about it on the Study Guitar blog.

paragraphs.en: Section 3. Studying Towards the start of this book, we discussed how creativity can be seen as taking different concepts and mixing them.
paragraphs.ca: Secció 3. Estudi. A l'inici d'aquest llibre vam parlar de com la creativitat es pot entendre com agafar conceptes diferents i barrejar-los.

paragraphs.en: So it stands to reason that the more concepts you know and truly understand, the more ideas you will be able to experiment with and try out.
paragraphs.ca: Així doncs, és lògic pensar que com més conceptes coneguis i entenguis de debò, més idees podràs experimentar i provar.

paragraphs.en: Hence, the more creative you will become. In this section, we are going to go over some approaches you can take to studying to help you learn more effectively.
paragraphs.ca: Per tant, més creatiu seràs. En aquesta secció repassarem alguns enfocaments que pots adoptar per estudiar i aprendre més eficaçment.

paragraphs.en: Learning effectively is key to creativity. Some problems take a long time to solve. Albert Einstein is famous for his theory of special relativity, and later, general relativity.
paragraphs.ca: Aprendre eficaçment és clau per a la creativitat. Alguns problemes triguen molt a resoldre's. Albert Einstein és famós per la seva teoria de la relativitat especial i, més endavant, de la relativitat general.

paragraphs.en: Archimedes is famous for his theory on buoyancy. When we hear the stories of great thinkers and their discoveries, we are often told of the breakthrough moment when the pieces finally fell into place and they figured out the problem.
paragraphs.ca: Arquimedes és famós per la seva teoria sobre l'empenyiment. Quan sentim les històries de grans pensadors i els seus descobriments, sovint se'ns explica el moment de revelació en què les peces finalment van encaixar i van resoldre el problema.

paragraphs.en: What we are rarely told is the amount of thinking that happened before that moment, thinking time that is often measured in months or even years. Einstein spent ten years thinking over the problems around special relativity before he had a breakthrough that enabled him to publish his groundbreaking theory. When considering a problem, people are often quick to dismiss their ability to solve the problem or understand the lesson if they are unable to
paragraphs.ca: El que rarament se'ns explica és la quantitat de pensament que hi va haver abans d'aquell moment, un temps de reflexió que sovint es mesura en mesos o fins i tot en anys. Einstein va passar deu anys pensant en els problemes al voltant de la relativitat especial abans de tenir una revelació que li va permetre publicar la seva teoria revolucionària. Quan es considera un problema, la gent sovint s'afanya a descartar la seva capacitat de resoldre'l o d'entendre la lliçó si no és capaç de

paragraphs.en: instantly grasp it. Sometimes problems need a little time to solve. This is completely normal, but something that seems to have been forgotten. Next time you are stuck with a problem you can't figure out, sit for five minutes and try and crack it. When you are working on some music theory concept you are struggling with, give yourself a few days to work through it. Some more complex theories and topics may take you months to work through, or even years. That's okay.
paragraphs.ca: captar-la a l'instant. De vegades els problemes necessiten una mica de temps per resoldre's. Això és completament normal, però sembla que s'hagi oblidat. La propera vegada que estiguis encallat amb un problema que no aconsegueixes resoldre, seu cinc minuts i intenta desxifrar-lo. Quan treballis algun concepte de teoria musical amb què t'encallis, dona't uns quants dies per assimilar-lo. Algunes teories i temes més complexos et poden costar mesos, o fins i tot anys. No passa res.

paragraphs.en: The important thing is that you, one, stick at it, two, progress a little more than you did last week, laying out your ideas. One of the biggest roadblocks people face in solving problems in music is understanding the information. This applies to everything from writing chord progressions to composing a symphony. Often people try and do things in their head, but there is too much to consider and they get confused and make mistakes.
paragraphs.ca: L'important és que, primer, hi persistis i, segon, progressis una mica més que la setmana passada. Exposar les teves idees. Un dels obstacles més grans que troba la gent a l'hora de resoldre problemes de música és entendre la informació. Això s'aplica a tot, des d'escriure progressions d'acords fins a compondre una simfonia. Sovint la gent intenta fer les coses de cap, però hi ha massa coses a tenir en compte i es confonen i cometen errors.

paragraphs.en: Lay out the relevant pieces of information on paper. This lets you consider things more easily. When laying things out on paper, make sure you do so in a way that makes sense.
paragraphs.ca: Posa les peces d'informació rellevants sobre el paper. Això et permet considerar les coses amb més facilitat. Quan ho facis sobre el paper, assegura't de fer-ho d'una manera que tingui sentit.

paragraphs.en: Before you consider the problem, consider the best way to organize solving the problem. Figuring out how to lay out the information clearly is a problem itself that needs to be solved, and figuring this out might take a few attempts.
paragraphs.ca: Abans de considerar el problema, considera la millor manera d'organitzar-ne la resolució. Esbrinar com exposar la informació amb claredat és un problema en si mateix que cal resoldre, i descobrir-ho pot requerir uns quants intents.

paragraphs.en: I usually find with music theory problems, once you lay out the information properly on paper, the solution becomes obvious.
paragraphs.ca: Normalment trobo que, amb els problemes de teoria musical, un cop exposes la informació correctament sobre el paper, la solució es fa evident.

paragraphs.en: Annotated scores or diagrammatic blocks are usually helpful ways to lay out ideas. Tables can be useful when working with chords.
paragraphs.ca: Les partitures anotades o els blocs diagramàtics solen ser maneres útils d'exposar les idees. Les taules poden ser útils quan es treballa amb acords.

paragraphs.en: Prose is almost certainly the wrong way to lay out a music theory problem, unless you are sketching plot ideas for a concept album, lyrics, or a libretto.
paragraphs.ca: La prosa és gairebé segur que és la manera equivocada d'exposar un problema de teoria musical, tret que estiguis esbossant idees d'argument per a un àlbum conceptual, lletres o un llibret.

paragraphs.en: To summarize, problem solving has three steps. 1. Consider the best way to approach solving the problem. 2. Lay that out on paper.
