chapters.title: The fifth source of information: analysis

segments.text: The fifth source of information, analysis
When it comes to learning how to be creative, it is vital to learn from the masters.
Take your favorite songs and pieces of music and analyze how they have been put together.
There are seven elements of music, and by analyzing each element, you will understand how the piece of music works the way it does.
These seven elements are
1. Harmony
2. Melody
3. Form
4. Dynamics
5. Texture
6. Rhythm
7. Timbre
You will have to learn a lot of theory to be able to analyze pieces to a degree of detail where you can learn something from them.
You will have to study each element of music individually.
Having a teacher walk you through some pieces to analyze would be helpful.
You can also consider finding a teacher to specifically help you do musical analysis.
When doing analysis, you will start by cataloguing the different elements of music that are being used.
To go back to an earlier section, we could consider this the perceptual level of understanding the music,
which isn't to say this is easy. It can be difficult to figure out what is going on.
After figuring out what is being done, you want to think about how that creates the musical effect that it does.
Exactly what about the music do you like?
Exactly what elements of music are being used to create that effect?
In the earlier section on learning guitar,
we talked about being specific when it came down to problem shooting your technique.
Be specific here too.
Is there a specific emotion or feeling that you like at a specific point in the song?
What specific elements of music are creating that?
The harmony? The rhythm? The ornamentation on the guitar? Something else?
Take the time to sit down and figure it out.
Information and entertainment.
Sometimes students want to be more productive with their studying,
but take a very unproductive approach to it.
It's usually from confusing entertainment with education.
Things like guitar magazines and YouTube videos,
aside from a few select channels, usually fall under entertainment.
Textbooks, courses and work from a teacher are education.
Sometimes people want to feel like they are doing more,
for their education, by watching loads of videos about guitar playing on YouTube or reading guitar
magazines. While you may pick up the odd tip here and there, you are not achieving anything.
In the business world, this is called action faking. You get the feeling that you are doing
something productive, but really, you have achieved as much as if you had watched a movie.
At least watching a movie would be relaxing. If you instead took that time to practice,
read a music theory textbook, or even read the manual for the recording program or other software
you use, you would have improved and learned something. Now, I'm not saying that you should
completely remove entertainment from your life. Entertainment is great for relaxing,
which is an important part of the day. But you may find there are ways you can easily fit something
more productive into your day. And don't cut into your practice under the pretense that you are
doing something useful when you are entertaining yourself. Practice time is for practice time,
not YouTube and magazines, conferences and live events. This could range from a barbecue or garden
party to a full 10-day in-person course. If you are taking lessons with a teacher, then you may
find they do events where students can meet each other. With my students, we would occasionally
have a dinner out at a local pub, barbecue, or play at the local open mic night. With my students,
we would occasionally have a dinner out at a local pub, barbecue, or play at the local open mic
night. Some international teachers or course creators may offer live events. I would recommend
trying these out if you can. I've been on a few, and they have always been a great experience,
and you often make friends there, some of whom will be friends for life. If nothing else,
you get a total immersion in your interest, and you get to be around people trying things out that
you can learn from. You will find people that can give you recommendations and advice,
people you can collaborate with, play gigs with, or just hang out and have fun.
In addition, or instead of attending a conference on guitar and composition,
you can always find conferences and events for your other interests.
I recently attended a philosophy conference in London, UK, where I met a lot of interesting
people, a few of whom I've kept in contact with since. People who attend conferences tend to be
people who are doing things with their lives. If you give it a chance and introduce yourself to as
many people as you can, you are bound to find a few people that you click with. When it comes to
success, having a network, which is a fancy way of saying friends that are competent at what they do,
can make your life a lot easier. Conferences and live events are great ways to find those people.
Be ruthless in your pursuit of understanding.
How hard do you push yourself when learning something new?
There are several levels of understanding that students can take.
1. Cursory reading of the material.
2. Being able to recite key terms and definitions.
3. Replicating examples.
4. Being able to explain key terms and definition.
5. Replicating examples in different keys.
6. Replicating examples in different contexts
Let's illustrate these ideas with an example.
Let's say we are learning about composition and have just read about passing tones.
At level 1, we read about passing tones and that is it.
We might be able to tell someone that we read about passing tones at the weekend,
but we couldn't say much more than reciting the name, Passing Tone, to someone.
At level 2, we have pushed the boat out a little further and have memorized key definitions.
We can recite that a passing tone is when we have two chord tones a third apart and add in the note in between.
In our notes, we would have an annotated score to demonstrate the idea.
Level 3 is quite similar to level 2, but we can replicate the notation example of how a passing tone works.
We'll discuss this a bit more later, but notation examples are much more effective at reminding you how a music theory concept works than a sentence.
At level 4, we can reword the definition in a few different ways.
This is a good way to start to test your understanding as your brain now has to work conceptually.
At levels 1 and 2, you are merely reciting words, and you are not doing much better than a parrot.
By rewording definitions, you have to consider what the words mean,
create a mental model of what the concepts that words are representing,
and figure out a new way to explain the key elements of that model to someone.
At level 5, we start with a mental model.

We can start to understand how passing tones work. We can take an example of a passing tone over an A minor harmony and create an example over an E major harmony that uses a passing tone. At level 6, we can say that we really understand what is going on, being able to take the concept of passing tones and apply them in different contexts.
Maybe we apply it to compose a melody for a singer,
to bending notes on electric guitar,
or composing a four-part model for orchestra.
Perceptual and Conceptual Levels of Understanding
We could break the six levels of understanding into two main categories.
One, perceptual.
Two, conceptual.
At the perceptual level, we are in monkey see monkey do mode.
Unfortunately, a lot of us are programmed to think this way at school,
where we are taught that learning consists of memorizing and repeating endless lists of random
facts. Figure 10. Perceptual and conceptual thinking. The conceptual level of thinking
is where we start to become creative. Good teachers and textbooks will push you to think
conceptually about the material that you are covering. The point of exercises in textbooks
and assignments from teachers is to push your understanding to more conceptual levels. It's
important to note that thinking this way is a process, and more often than not we have to move
through the levels. We are going to struggle to think conceptually if we can't replicate examples
or give a simple definition. This process also takes time. When working on a topic, it may take
several lessons or longer to move you from perceptual to conceptual levels of understanding.
When studying, you want to bear these levels in mind and make sure that you are working through
them. Test yourself as you go. Sometimes students read the words on the page and do not consider
the meaning of those words. When reading a textbook, ask yourself, so what? What does this
paragraph mean? Don't settle for looking at words on a page. Challenge your understanding as you go.
Those who understand, create. It's fine to read through a music theory or composition concept
and think, sure, I understand this. It's another to take that idea and use it to create a short
piece of music. When we talked about the six levels of understanding, at level six we talked
about changing the context of the concept we are studying, or to put it another way,
composing a short piece of music using that idea. Creation is the litmus test for understanding.
Creation is the purpose of studying in the first place. There is no point in studying if you are
not going to apply it to something and use that knowledge to create. In addition to creation being
the purpose of studying, it is also a fantastic way to study. By taking an idea that you are
learning and trying to compose with it, this composition may only be two bars long or a whole
sonata depending on the topic you are studying, you will very quickly expose any holes in your
knowledge that you need to then solve. These holes could be caused by not understanding the material
properly, or it could be a flaw with the material that you are studying. Not all courses and
textbooks are perfect. If you have a teacher, keep track of these questions throughout the week in a
notebook or computer file and ask them at the next lesson. I have taught several lessons where we
just went through student questions. If you don't have a teacher, then you may need to consult other
textbooks or sources to find the answers that you are looking for. You can always try reaching out
to the course creator or book author, a lot of people are surprisingly reachable via email.
The worst that they will do is not reply, so it doesn't hurt to reach out and ask a question or
two. So as soon as you learn a new idea, find a way to use it and try it out. You will find you
learn a lot faster and more thoroughly by doing this. How to learn any song. This applies to songs,
your songs, exercises, your compositions, anything where you have more than a few bars of music to work through.
There are several ways to approach learning a piece of music, most of which are incredibly inefficient.
One way is to work through the song from the start.
Every time you make a mistake, go back to the start of the song.
This is very inefficient, as you spend a lot of time playing through bits you already know
rather than working on the bits that need work.
This is probably the most common approach.
A better way to approach learning a song is as follows.
Start with bar one.
Apply the following process.
1. Figure out what frets the notes are on and what fingers you're going to use to play those notes.
2. Annotate your music with the fingers if you need a reminder.
This is a very useful tip when starting with a piece.
3. Play through a few times,
making sure that you play it the same way every time using the fingers you previously specified.
Do this slowly so that you don't make too many mistakes. Many students rush this phase.
4. Work out the rhythm of the piece. You may want to write this under the music.
5. Play through that bar slowly, counting the rhythm out loud. Counting out loud is important.
If you count in your head, you will make mistakes.
6. Take your metronome at a slow tempo and clap the rhythm, counting out loud to the metronome.
7. Take your guitar and play along to the metronome, counting out loud.
8. Once you can play the bar three times in a row, with a break between each repetition, learn the next bar.
This process will help you learn anything on guitar.
It's helpful if you memorize what you are working on.
In terms of how you work through the song, use the following approach.
1. Learn bar 1.
2. Learn bar 2.
3. Practice the transition between bars 1 and bar 2.
4. Practice bars 1 and 2 together.
5. Practice bar 3.
6. Practice the transition between bars 2 and 3.
7. Practice bars 2 and 3 together.
8. Etc.
This way you can work through the song in focused slices.
When you complete larger sections of the song, for example the phrase or verse,
practice playing through those larger sections.
Eventually, you will be able to tie those sections together into the entire song.
Tips for studying
Use diagrams and notation examples.
Words are terrible.
Music theory needs music.
When taking notes, make sure you do so in a format that makes sense for the information that you are trying to remember.
Do not go and write a paragraph of prose to describe a music theory concept.
Use notation or diagrams with supporting text to explain specific features of your diagram notation.
Pace yourself.
Take your time.
It's not a race.
It is easy to fall into the trap of, I read X pages today, therefore I am making progress.
It doesn't matter how many pages you read if you don't understand them.
Take your time and make sure you understand the material that you are working on.
Have a schedule.
Regularly scheduled time is the best way to approach learning anything.
If you read something once a week, by the time you come back to it next week,
you will have forgotten what you covered.
Every day is best, and every couple of days is also effective.
Having said that, once a week is better than nothing.
Schedule your time on paper at the start of the week.
Having said that, once a week is better than nothing.
Schedule your time on paper at the start of the week.
The fastest way to learn
Without a doubt, the fastest way to learn is to find the best possible teacher,
throw money at them, and study with them part-time slash
full-time. After attending music college, studying books and courses, and studying with various
teachers and courses, I can say without a doubt that the fastest I progressed was by taking one-to-one
lessons with an excellent teacher. However, this is expensive and time-consuming and may not be an
option for most people. This was closely followed by a well-organized course of lessons I took.
A good course is better than a mediocre teacher.
One thing to bear in mind is that you don't necessarily have to study with a teacher full-time.
You could take lessons for a few months or do intensive lessons for a week
to get material to practice and study throughout the year.

Podem agafar un exemple de nota de pas sobre una harmonia de la menor i crear un exemple sobre una harmonia de mi major que faci servir una nota de pas. Al nivell 6, podem dir que realment entenem què passa, sent capaços d'agafar el concepte de nota de pas i aplicar-lo en contextos diferents.

paragraphs.en: Maybe we apply it to compose a melody for a singer, to bending notes on electric guitar, or composing a four-part model for orchestra.
paragraphs.ca: Potser l'apliquem per compondre una melodia per a un cantant, per fer bends de notes a la guitarra elèctrica o per compondre una peça a quatre veus per a orquestra.

paragraphs.en: Perceptual and Conceptual Levels of Understanding We could break the six levels of understanding into two main categories.
paragraphs.ca: Nivells perceptius i conceptuals de comprensió Podríem dividir els sis nivells de comprensió en dues categories principals.

paragraphs.en: One, perceptual. Two, conceptual. At the perceptual level, we are in monkey see monkey do mode. Unfortunately, a lot of us are programmed to think this way at school, where we are taught that learning consists of memorizing and repeating endless lists of random facts. Figure 10. Perceptual and conceptual thinking. The conceptual level of thinking is where we start to become creative. Good teachers and textbooks will push you to think
paragraphs.ca: Una, perceptiu. Dues, conceptual. Al nivell perceptiu, estem en mode «el mico ho veu, el mico ho fa». Malauradament, molts de nosaltres estem programats per pensar així a l'escola, on ens ensenyen que aprendre consisteix a memoritzar i repetir llistes infinites de fets aleatoris. Figura 10. Pensament perceptiu i conceptual. El nivell conceptual de pensament és on comencem a esdevenir creatius. Els bons professors i els bons llibres de text t'empenyeran a pensar

paragraphs.en: conceptually about the material that you are covering. The point of exercises in textbooks and assignments from teachers is to push your understanding to more conceptual levels. It's important to note that thinking this way is a process, and more often than not we have to move through the levels. We are going to struggle to think conceptually if we can't replicate examples or give a simple definition. This process also takes time. When working on a topic, it may take
paragraphs.ca: conceptualment sobre el material que estàs treballant. L'objectiu dels exercicis dels llibres de text i de les tasques dels professors és empenyer la teva comprensió cap a nivells més conceptuals. És important tenir en compte que pensar així és un procés i que, molt sovint, hem de passar pels nivells. Ens costarà pensar conceptualment si no podem replicar exemples o donar una definició simple. Aquest procés també requereix temps. Quan treballes un tema, pot caldre

paragraphs.en: several lessons or longer to move you from perceptual to conceptual levels of understanding. When studying, you want to bear these levels in mind and make sure that you are working through them. Test yourself as you go. Sometimes students read the words on the page and do not consider the meaning of those words. When reading a textbook, ask yourself, so what? What does this paragraph mean? Don't settle for looking at words on a page. Challenge your understanding as you go.
paragraphs.ca: diverses classes o més temps per portar-te dels nivells perceptius als conceptuals de comprensió. Quan estudiïs, tingues presents aquests nivells i assegura't de recórrer-los. Posa't a prova a mesura que avances. De vegades els alumnes llegeixen les paraules de la pàgina i no consideren el significat d'aquestes paraules. Quan llegeixis un llibre de text, pregunta't: i què? Què vol dir aquest paràgraf? No et conformis amb mirar paraules en una pàgina. Qüestiona la teva comprensió a mesura que avances.

paragraphs.en: Those who understand, create. It's fine to read through a music theory or composition concept and think, sure, I understand this. It's another to take that idea and use it to create a short piece of music. When we talked about the six levels of understanding, at level six we talked about changing the context of the concept we are studying, or to put it another way, composing a short piece of music using that idea. Creation is the litmus test for understanding.
paragraphs.ca: Qui entén, crea. Està bé llegir un concepte de teoria musical o de composició i pensar: sí, això ho entenc. És una altra cosa agafar aquesta idea i fer-la servir per crear una peça curta de música. Quan parlàvem dels sis nivells de comprensió, al nivell sis parlàvem de canviar el context del concepte que estudiem o, dit d'una altra manera, compondre una peça curta de música fent servir aquella idea. La creació és la prova de foc de la comprensió.

paragraphs.en: Creation is the purpose of studying in the first place. There is no point in studying if you are not going to apply it to something and use that knowledge to create. In addition to creation being the purpose of studying, it is also a fantastic way to study. By taking an idea that you are learning and trying to compose with it, this composition may only be two bars long or a whole sonata depending on the topic you are studying, you will very quickly expose any holes in your
paragraphs.ca: La creació és la finalitat d'estudiar, al capdavall. No té cap sentit estudiar si no ho aplicaràs a alguna cosa i faràs servir aquest coneixement per crear. A més de ser la finalitat d'estudiar, crear és també una manera fantàstica d'estudiar. Agafant una idea que estàs aprenent i intentant compondre amb ella —aquesta composició pot tenir només dos compassos o ser tota una sonata, segons el tema que estudies—, exposaràs molt de pressa qualsevol forat en el teu

paragraphs.en: knowledge that you need to then solve. These holes could be caused by not understanding the material properly, or it could be a flaw with the material that you are studying. Not all courses and textbooks are perfect. If you have a teacher, keep track of these questions throughout the week in a notebook or computer file and ask them at the next lesson. I have taught several lessons where we just went through student questions. If you don't have a teacher, then you may need to consult other
paragraphs.ca: coneixement que després hagis de resoldre. Aquests forats poden venir de no entendre bé el material, o bé poden ser un defecte del material que estàs estudiant. No tots els cursos i llibres de text són perfectes. Si tens un professor, pren nota d'aquestes preguntes durant la setmana en un quadern o un fitxer d'ordinador i planteja-les a la classe següent. He fet diverses classes en què només vam repassar les preguntes dels alumnes. Si no tens professor, potser hauràs de consultar altres

paragraphs.en: textbooks or sources to find the answers that you are looking for. You can always try reaching out to the course creator or book author, a lot of people are surprisingly reachable via email.
paragraphs.ca: llibres de text o fonts per trobar les respostes que busques. Sempre pots intentar contactar amb el creador del curs o l'autor del llibre; molta gent és sorprenentment accessible per correu electrònic.

paragraphs.en: The worst that they will do is not reply, so it doesn't hurt to reach out and ask a question or two. So as soon as you learn a new idea, find a way to use it and try it out. You will find you learn a lot faster and more thoroughly by doing this. How to learn any song. This applies to songs, your songs, exercises, your compositions, anything where you have more than a few bars of music to work through.
paragraphs.ca: El pitjor que faran és no respondre, així que no costa res escriure i fer una pregunta o dues. Així doncs, tan bon punt aprenguis una idea nova, troba una manera d'utilitzar-la i prova-la. Veuràs que aprens molt més de pressa i més a fons fent això. Com aprendre qualsevol cançó. Això s'aplica a les cançons, a les teves cançons, als exercicis, a les teves composicions, a qualsevol cosa on tinguis més d'uns quants compassos de música per treballar.

paragraphs.en: There are several ways to approach learning a piece of music, most of which are incredibly inefficient. One way is to work through the song from the start.
paragraphs.ca: Hi ha diverses maneres d'afrontar l'aprenentatge d'una peça musical, la majoria de les quals són increïblement ineficients. Una manera és treballar la cançó des del principi.

paragraphs.en: Every time you make a mistake, go back to the start of the song. This is very inefficient, as you spend a lot of time playing through bits you already know rather than working on the bits that need work.
paragraphs.ca: Cada vegada que comets un error, tornes al principi de la cançó. Això és molt ineficient, perquè passes molt de temps tocant trossos que ja saps en lloc de treballar els trossos que necessiten feina.

paragraphs.en: This is probably the most common approach. A better way to approach learning a song is as follows. Start with bar one. Apply the following process.
paragraphs.ca: Aquest és probablement l'enfocament més comú. Una manera millor d'afrontar l'aprenentatge d'una cançó és la següent. Comença pel compàs u. Aplica el procés següent.

paragraphs.en: 1. Figure out what frets the notes are on and what fingers you're going to use to play those notes. 2. Annotate your music with the fingers if you need a reminder.
paragraphs.ca: 1. Esbrina en quins trastes estan les notes i quins dits faràs servir per tocar aquestes notes. 2. Anota la partitura amb els dits si necessites un recordatori.

paragraphs.en: This is a very useful tip when starting with a piece. 3. Play through a few times, making sure that you play it the same way every time using the fingers you previously specified.
paragraphs.ca: Aquest és un consell molt útil quan comences una peça. 3. Toca-la unes quantes vegades, assegurant-te que la toques sempre de la mateixa manera amb els dits que has especificat abans.

paragraphs.en: Do this slowly so that you don't make too many mistakes. Many students rush this phase. 4. Work out the rhythm of the piece. You may want to write this under the music.
paragraphs.ca: Fes-ho a poc a poc per no cometre massa errors. Molts alumnes es precipiten en aquesta fase. 4. Esbrina el ritme de la peça. Potser voldràs escriure'l sota la música.

paragraphs.en: 5. Play through that bar slowly, counting the rhythm out loud. Counting out loud is important. If you count in your head, you will make mistakes.
paragraphs.ca: 5. Toca aquell compàs a poc a poc, comptant el ritme en veu alta. Comptar en veu alta és important. Si comptes mentalment, cometràs errors.

paragraphs.en: 6. Take your metronome at a slow tempo and clap the rhythm, counting out loud to the metronome. 7. Take your guitar and play along to the metronome, counting out loud.
paragraphs.ca: 6. Agafa el metrònom a un tempo lent i picota el ritme, comptant en veu alta seguint el metrònom. 7. Agafa la guitarra i toca seguint el metrònom, comptant en veu alta.

paragraphs.en: 8. Once you can play the bar three times in a row, with a break between each repetition, learn the next bar. This process will help you learn anything on guitar.
paragraphs.ca: 8. Quan puguis tocar el compàs tres vegades seguides, amb una pausa entre cada repetició, aprèn el compàs següent. Aquest procés t'ajudarà a aprendre qualsevol cosa a la guitarra.

paragraphs.en: It's helpful if you memorize what you are working on. In terms of how you work through the song, use the following approach.
paragraphs.ca: Ajuda que memoritzis allò que estàs treballant. Pel que fa a com treballar la cançó, fes servir l'enfocament següent.

paragraphs.en: 1. Learn bar 1. 2. Learn bar 2. 3. Practice the transition between bars 1 and bar 2. 4. Practice bars 1 and 2 together. 5. Practice bar 3.
paragraphs.ca: 1. Aprèn el compàs 1. 2. Aprèn el compàs 2. 3. Practica la transició entre el compàs 1 i el compàs 2. 4. Practica els compassos 1 i 2 junts. 5. Practica el compàs 3.

paragraphs.en: 6. Practice the transition between bars 2 and 3. 7. Practice bars 2 and 3 together. 8. Etc. This way you can work through the song in focused slices.
paragraphs.ca: 6. Practica la transició entre els compassos 2 i 3. 7. Practica els compassos 2 i 3 junts. 8. Etc. D'aquesta manera pots treballar la cançó en talls concentrats.

paragraphs.en: When you complete larger sections of the song, for example the phrase or verse, practice playing through those larger sections.
paragraphs.ca: Quan completis seccions més grans de la cançó, per exemple la frase o l'estrofa, practica tocar aquestes seccions més grans.

paragraphs.en: Eventually, you will be able to tie those sections together into the entire song. Tips for studying Use diagrams and notation examples.
paragraphs.ca: Finalment, podràs lligar aquestes seccions en la cançó sencera. Consells per estudiar Fes servir diagrames i exemples de notació.

paragraphs.en: Words are terrible. Music theory needs music. When taking notes, make sure you do so in a format that makes sense for the information that you are trying to remember.
paragraphs.ca: Les paraules són terribles. La teoria musical necessita música. Quan prenguis apunts, assegura't de fer-ho en un format que tingui sentit per a la informació que intentes recordar.

paragraphs.en: Do not go and write a paragraph of prose to describe a music theory concept. Use notation or diagrams with supporting text to explain specific features of your diagram notation.
paragraphs.ca: No vagis a escriure un paràgraf de prosa per descriure un concepte de teoria musical. Fes servir notació o diagrames amb text de suport per explicar característiques concretes de la teva notació o del teu diagrama.

paragraphs.en: Pace yourself. Take your time. It's not a race. It is easy to fall into the trap of, I read X pages today, therefore I am making progress.
paragraphs.ca: Vés a poc a poc. Pren-te el teu temps. No és una cursa. És fàcil caure en la trampa de «avui he llegit X pàgines, per tant estic progressant».

paragraphs.en: It doesn't matter how many pages you read if you don't understand them. Take your time and make sure you understand the material that you are working on.
paragraphs.ca: No importa quantes pàgines llegeixis si no les entens. Pren-te el teu temps i assegura't d'entendre el material que estàs treballant.

paragraphs.en: Have a schedule.
paragraphs.ca: Tingues un horari.

paragraphs.en: Regularly scheduled time is the best way to approach learning anything. If you read something once a week, by the time you come back to it next week, you will have forgotten what you covered.
paragraphs.ca: Un temps programat regularment és la millor manera d'afrontar l'aprenentatge de qualsevol cosa. Si llegeixes una cosa un cop a la setmana, quan hi tornis la setmana següent hauràs oblidat el que havies après.

paragraphs.en: Every day is best, and every couple of days is also effective. Having said that, once a week is better than nothing. Schedule your time on paper at the start of the week.
paragraphs.ca: Cada dia és el millor, i cada dos dies també és efectiu. Dit això, un cop a la setmana és millor que res. Programa el teu temps en paper a principi de setmana.

paragraphs.en: Having said that, once a week is better than nothing. Schedule your time on paper at the start of the week. The fastest way to learn Without a doubt, the fastest way to learn is to find the best possible teacher, throw money at them, and study with them part-time slash full-time. After attending music college, studying books and courses, and studying with various teachers and courses, I can say without a doubt that the fastest I progressed was by taking one-to-one
paragraphs.ca: Dit això, un cop a la setmana és millor que res. Programa el teu temps en paper a principi de setmana. La manera més ràpida d'aprendre Sens dubte, la manera més ràpida d'aprendre és trobar el millor professor possible, no escatimar-hi diners i estudiar amb ell a temps parcial o a temps complet. Després d'assistir a l'escola de música, estudiar llibres i cursos i estudiar amb diversos professors i cursos, puc dir sens dubte que el progrés més ràpid el vaig fer fent classes individuals

paragraphs.en: lessons with an excellent teacher. However, this is expensive and time-consuming and may not be an option for most people. This was closely followed by a well-organized course of lessons I took.
paragraphs.ca: amb un professor excel·lent. Tanmateix, això és car i requereix temps, i potser no és una opció per a la majoria de la gent. Això va ser seguit de prop per un curs de classes ben organitzat que vaig fer.

paragraphs.en: A good course is better than a mediocre teacher. One thing to bear in mind is that you don't necessarily have to study with a teacher full-time.
paragraphs.ca: Un bon curs és millor que un professor mediocre. Una cosa a tenir en compte és que no cal necessàriament estudiar amb un professor a temps complet.

paragraphs.en: You could take lessons for a few months or do intensive lessons for a week to get material to practice and study throughout the year.
paragraphs.ca: Podries fer classes durant uns quants mesos o fer classes intensives durant una setmana per obtenir material per practicar i estudiar durant tot l'any.

segments.text: Section 4. Your Equipment
There are a few things worth saying about equipment for your practice and creativity.
Guitar tone
One of the easiest ways to make your music sound good is to have a good tone.
If you read about tone online, you will find a lot of misinformation.
So let's quickly clear up what we are referring to.
Guitar tone is the timbre of a particular note.
It is the sonic quality of the note.
If you take two different amplifiers, or even instruments,
and play the same note the same way, it will sound different.
This difference in sound is the timbre.
and when we refer to tone, technically we are referring to timbre.
Note ornamentation is how a particular note is played.
Is the player sliding into the note?
Are then bending into the note?
How fast is the bend?
Are they using vibrato?
What is the depth, width and timing of that vibrato?
When you read about tone being in the fingers, that is a mistake.
What the writer means is that ornamentation is in the fingers.
It is a player's ornamentation that gives them their unique sound.
It is due to ornamentation that Ingwi Malmsteen playing through a $30 amplifier still sounds like Ingwi Malmsteen.
What affects tone?
Several factors affect your tone roughly in the following order.
1. Amplifier
2. Effects
3. Pickups
4. Strings
5. Guitar body
6. The tone control on the guitar
The amplifier
Your amplifier will have the biggest effect on tone.
There are several types of amplifiers that are available today.
Valve, solid state and modelling.
How amplifiers work
Before we look at what these different types of amplifiers are and how they work,
we should probably talk a little about how amplifiers work in general.
When you play an electric guitar, the string vibrates.
The string is vibrating above a pickup.
The pickup is a set of magnets that are wrapped in electrical wire.
There is a wrapped magnet underneath each string.
When the guitar string vibrates inside this magnetic field,
an electrical voltage is induced in the wire around the pickup.
If you want to learn more about how this works, look up Faraday's Law of Induction online.
This voltage then goes from the guitar through the cable into your amplifier.
Your amplifier has several controls, but the basics of what it does is to use your guitar output to regulate a more powerful signal.
You can imagine the amplifier is a powerful river with a gate.
The output from your guitar regulates how open or closed the gate in the river is, controlling how much of the powerful river can flow through the gate.
This variation in the flow of the powerful river matches the varying voltage coming from your guitar.
It's like taking a small key and cutting a much bigger key that has the same shape.
This is how you take the weak signal from your guitar
and turn it into something powerful enough to be heard from your amplifier speaker.
Amplifiers are usually broken into three sections.
1. Preamp
2. Poweramp
3. Speaker Cabinet
The preamp is a section that does most of the tone shaping.
You can fiddle with EQ buttons and overdrive here.
The power amp is mainly what we described above.
It's the bit that makes your guitar signal loud.
The speaker cabinets are the speakers.
They take the powerful signal from the power amplifier and turn it from electricity into sound.
All three of these sections affect your tone.
Combo amps are amps with all three sections built into one.
Heads are a box that combines the preamp and power amp.
Cabs are speaker cabinets that you can plug your head into.
Speaker cabinets can have different speakers in them, which has a big impact on tone.
They can also come in different sizes, be chambered, this is the internal construction,
and be built from different thickness woods, which can affect the tone.
Rack units are effectively a way to build your own amp, where the preamp and power amp are separate.
This gives you more control over the tone.
Racks are usually MIDI controlled, which is a system whereby you can press one button on a pedal board
and change all your preamp and effects settings at once.
You may have seen inputs and outputs on your amplifier labelled effects loop.
This gives you a way to put guitar effects between the preamp and power amp.
Solid state amplifiers
Solid state refers to the method by which the signal is amplified.
In a solid-state amplifier, transistors are used to control the amplification.
There are different types of transistors which can affect the quality of the signal.
The big benefit to using transistors is that they are cheap and reliable.
They last forever.
Valve amplifiers.
These, unsurprisingly, use valves to amplify the signal.
Valves are also known as vacuum tubes.
Vacuum tubes were used in the first electronic computers before moving into commercial technology.
They were used in everything from old TV sets to AM, FM radio.
These days, most valve electronics are obsolete.
They're only being used in high-end hi-fis and guitar amplifiers.
Due to how valves work, when they are pushed hard,
the signal that is being amplified starts to break down in a way that is deemed favorable,
which is the source of valve overdrive. Valve amplifiers tend to sound best when they are
pushed hard to create more of this signal breakdown, hence the term overdrive from
the valves being driven hard.

Generally speaking, valve amplifiers are accepted as having the best guitar tone. The benefit of valve amplifiers is the sound. The downside is that they are more expensive, heavier and require expensive maintenance. The valves will fail over time and need to be replaced.
Modeling amplifiers. Modeling amplifiers seek to take the distortions that a valve introduces into the guitar signal and model how that distortion behaves.
The model is put into an algorithm and applied to your guitar signal.
This is what units such as the Kemper and Fractalax FX do.
The benefits of modeling units are that they are much more portable than a valve amplifier.
They are also more reliable.
Usually, they are plugged straight into a PA system or a speaker cabinet.
Cost-wise, they are usually about the same price or more than a full valve setup, head and cab.
The sound quality is very close, but usually not quite the same as a valve amplifier.
Effects
The next biggest impact on your tone will be from your effects.
There are many types of effects that you can use and they will impact your tone.
There are two ways the effects can impact your tone.
One, the way they change your sound, the effect they are adding.
Two, the quality of the DAC in the pedal, if it has it.
DAC stands for Digital to Analog Converter.
This is sometimes known as ADA, Analog to Digital to Analog.
The signal coming out of your guitar is analog.
It's a continuously varying voltage.
Some guitar pedals will use a tiny computer, a couple of microchips, inside the pedal to add the effect.
This computer requires the signal from the guitar, analog, to be chopped up and quantized via a DAC,
after which it will process the signal, add the effect,
and then take the digital signal and put it back into analog.
If the DAC is cheap, it can hurt the tone.
Most higher-end pedals will be fine for this.
Bear in mind that all music you listen to
has been through multiple rounds of ADA conversion.
The negative influence that effects can have on your tone
is known as tone suck.
A good way around this is to have a completely dry signal,
Dry means no effects, wet means effects have been added, with the effects added on top of the dry signal.
This can be done in stereo and is known as a WDW setup, wet-dry-wet.
Big rack systems sometimes use WDW to create a huge guitar sound.
Pickups
The next biggest factor in your tone is the pickups in your guitar.
If your guitar has come with stock, that is manufacturer-supplied pickups, you will find a big difference by changing them to top-tier pickups.
As a note, higher-end guitars tend to come with good pickups.
There are two types of pickups. One, active. Two, passive.
Passive pickups are magnets wrapped in wire, and that's it.
Active pickups use fewer turns of higher gauge wire than passive pickups.
This results in lower output than passive pickups, so they have a small pre-amp built into them,
which requires a battery to run and in turn leads to a higher output than passive pickups.
Footnote 7. Active pickups are often popular amongst extreme metal players.
Passive pickups tend to have a more organic feel.
An additional consideration with your pickups is how close they are to the strings.
When the pickups are raised, they will give a higher output,
but the magnetic field of the pickup will fight against the vibration of the strings,
reducing the length of time that the strings will ring out, known as the sustain.
When the pickups are lowered, they are further from the strings,
reducing the output but increasing the sustain.
Balancing output and sustain takes a bit of trial and error.
This is something that a luthier or tech may do for you when setting up your guitar.
Strings

paragraphs.ca: Si agafes dos amplificadors diferents, o fins i tot dos instruments, i toques la mateixa nota de la mateixa manera, sonarà diferent.

paragraphs.en: This difference in sound is the timbre. and when we refer to tone, technically we are referring to timbre. Note ornamentation is how a particular note is played.
paragraphs.ca: Aquesta diferència de so és el timbre, i quan parlem del so, tècnicament ens referim al timbre. L'ornamentació de la nota és com es toca una nota concreta.

paragraphs.en: Is the player sliding into the note? Are then bending into the note? How fast is the bend? Are they using vibrato? What is the depth, width and timing of that vibrato?
