paragraphs.en: Two, using those programs effectively. Using the correct programs. The types of programs that you use will fall into two main categories.
paragraphs.ca: Dos, fer servir aquests programes de manera efectiva. Fer servir els programes correctes. Els tipus de programes que facis servir es divideixen en dues categories principals.

paragraphs.en: One, writing guitar tablature, usually called TAB for short. Two, recording audio. Some programs will do both. Why write guitar tab?
paragraphs.ca: Un, escriure tablatura de guitarra, normalment anomenada TAB. Dos, enregistrar àudio. Alguns programes fan les dues coses. Per què escriure tablatura de guitarra?

paragraphs.en: If you are learning to play the guitar, you're going to be working through a lot of guitar tabs. You will be getting exercises, maybe from a teacher, and writing out your ideas.
paragraphs.ca: Si estàs aprenent a tocar la guitarra, treballaràs amb moltes tablatures de guitarra. Rebràs exercicis, potser d'un professor, i escriuràs les teves idees.

paragraphs.en: The benefit of using a computer program to write guitar tabs is that you can 1. Play the tab back so you can hear how it should sound.
paragraphs.ca: L'avantatge de fer servir un programa d'ordinador per escriure tablatures de guitarra és que pots: 1. Reproduir la tablatura per sentir com hauria de sonar.

paragraphs.en: 2. Add custom metronome drum tracks to help you understand the rhythm. We go over how to do this in the appendix on programming metronomes.
paragraphs.ca: 2. Afegir pistes de bateria de metrònom a mida per ajudar-te a entendre el ritme. Expliquem com fer-ho a l'apèndix sobre programar metrònoms.

paragraphs.en: 3. Store things efficiently so that you don't have hundreds of pieces of paper lying around. 4. Create backing tracks for pieces that you are practicing.
paragraphs.ca: 3. Emmagatzemar les coses de manera eficient per no tenir centenars de fulls escampats. 4. Crear pistes de base per als fragments que practiques.

paragraphs.en: 5. Slow down the song or exercise that you are learning. 6. Compose ideas and share them with your friends to collaborate.
paragraphs.ca: 5. Alentir la cançó o l'exercici que estàs aprenent. 6. Compondre idees i compartir-les amb els amics per col·laborar.

paragraphs.en: 7. Export your tab scores to PDF, slash audio, slash print, slash MyDi, slash MusicXML, etc.
paragraphs.ca: 7. Exportar les teves partitures de tablatura a PDF, àudio, impressió, MIDI, MusicXML, etcètera.

paragraphs.en: Why record audio? As a beginner, you will probably not need to record audio. In fact, given the learning curve that recording programs can have, I would recommend that you don't worry about this until you're reaching the late beginner, intermediate level.
paragraphs.ca: Per què enregistrar àudio? Com a principiant, probablement no necessitaràs enregistrar àudio. De fet, donada la corba d'aprenentatge que poden tenir els programes d'enregistrament, et recomanaria que no t'hi amoïnssis fins que arribis al nivell de principiant avançat o intermedi.

paragraphs.en: For most people, this is after several months of lessons. But when you do reach that level, it is a great tool. Recording your playing will allow you to listen back to your playing and analyze your mistakes.
paragraphs.ca: Per a la majoria de la gent, això és després de diversos mesos de classes. Però quan arribes a aquest nivell, és una eina fantàstica. Enregistrar el que toques et permet escoltar-ho després i analitzar els teus errors.

paragraphs.en: One thing that is quite useful is being able to visually see your recording against a grid, which visually tells you if your playing is in time or not, and if it isn't in time, you will be able to see if you're early, late, or just all over the place.
paragraphs.ca: Una cosa força útil és poder veure visualment la teva gravació sobre una graella, que et diu visualment si el que toques està dins del temps o no i, si no ho està, podràs veure si vas avançat, endarrerit o directament per tot arreu.

paragraphs.en: Figure 11. Waveforms. Recording programs become useful when you want to compose music. This could be anything from backing tracks to improvise over to composing your own songs and instrumental pieces of music.
paragraphs.ca: Figura 11. Formes d'ona. Els programes d'enregistrament es tornen útils quan vols compondre música. Això pot anar des de pistes de base per improvisar-hi fins a compondre les teves pròpies cançons i peces instrumentals.

paragraphs.en: The top-level recording programs are known as digital audio workstations, often abbreviated to DAWs. DAWs will allow you to 1. Record and manipulate audio.
paragraphs.ca: Els programes d'enregistrament de més nivell es coneixen com a estacions de treball d'àudio digital, sovint abreujades com a DAW. Els DAW et permeten: 1. Enregistrar i manipular àudio.

paragraphs.en: 2. Input musical notes and play them back via MIDI data. 3. Use different sound libraries to play back your compositions. See below for an explanation.
paragraphs.ca: 2. Introduir notes musicals i reproduir-les mitjançant dades MIDI. 3. Fer servir diferents biblioteques de sons per reproduir les teves composicions. Vegeu més avall una explicació.

paragraphs.en: 4. Control sound libraries from an external keyboard. For example, use your keyboard to play the cello. 5. Loop sections. Very useful for practice.
paragraphs.ca: 4. Controlar biblioteques de sons des d'un teclat extern. Per exemple, fer servir el teu teclat per tocar el violoncel. 5. Fer bucles de seccions. Molt útil per a la pràctica.

paragraphs.en: 6. Mix, EQ, and add effects to your tracks. 7. Use VST or AU. See below for explanation. 8. And more. For example, you could record a guitar riff into a DAW, then loop it so that it plays several times in a row.
paragraphs.ca: 6. Mesclar, equalitzar i afegir efectes a les teves pistes. 7. Fer servir VST o AU. Vegeu més avall l'explicació. 8. I més coses. Per exemple, podries enregistrar un riff de guitarra en un DAW i després fer-ne un bucle perquè soni diverses vegades seguides.

paragraphs.en: Every piece of professionally released music that you have listened to in the last 20 years has used a DAW. DAW are used for composing, recording, mixing and mastering music.
paragraphs.ca: Cada peça de música publicada professionalment que has escoltat en els últims 20 anys ha fet servir un DAW. Els DAW serveixen per compondre, enregistrar, mesclar i masteritzar música.

paragraphs.en: MIDI, spelt M-I-D-I. Data. MIDI stands for Musical Instrument Digital Interface. This is a computer protocol for connecting musical instruments, usually keyboards, to computers and each other.
paragraphs.ca: MIDI, lletrejat M-I-D-I. Dades. MIDI són les sigles de Musical Instrument Digital Interface. És un protocol informàtic per connectar instruments musicals, normalment teclats, a ordinadors i entre ells.

paragraphs.en: A MIDI device can connect to a computer via a sound interface or other MIDI-capable devices. MIDI is also a way to write...
paragraphs.ca: Un dispositiu MIDI es pot connectar a un ordinador mitjançant una interfície de so o altres dispositius compatibles amb MIDI. MIDI també és una manera d'escriure...

paragraphs.en: I can write musical notes to a computer file to share between different programs. Nearly all music programs can create MIDI files. For example, I can write a tab in Guitar Pro, export that to MIDI and open it in Logic Pro.
paragraphs.ca: Puc escriure notes musicals en un fitxer d'ordinador per compartir-les entre programes diferents. Gairebé tots els programes de música poden crear fitxers MIDI. Per exemple, puc escriure una tablatura a Guitar Pro, exportar-la a MIDI i obrir-la a Logic Pro.

paragraphs.en: Sound libraries. These are collections of pre-recorded sounds. Let's say you were writing a drum part for a guitar riff that you wrote.
paragraphs.ca: Biblioteques de sons. Són col·leccions de sons enregistrats prèviament. Diguem que estàs escrivint una part de bateria per a un riff de guitarra que has compost.

paragraphs.en: You could purchase a sound library where someone has recorded different parts of a drum kit, and these sounds are played back with your programmed drum part.
paragraphs.ca: Podries comprar una biblioteca de sons en què algú ha enregistrat diferents parts d'una bateria, i aquests sons es reprodueixen amb la part de bateria que has programat.

paragraphs.en: Sound libraries usually include different articulations, which are different ways of playing a note. A simple example is that a cello could be played arco, bowed, or pizzicato, plucked.
paragraphs.ca: Les biblioteques de sons normalment inclouen diferents articulacions, que són maneres diferents de tocar una nota. Un exemple senzill és que un violoncel es pot tocar arco, amb l'arquet, o pizzicato, pinçant les cordes.

paragraphs.en: More articulations with better programming, how the library moves between notes, gives better quality and more realistic playback, but also tend to make libraries more expensive.
paragraphs.ca: Més articulacions i una millor programació, és a dir, com es mou la biblioteca entre notes, donen més qualitat i una reproducció més realista, però també solen fer que les biblioteques siguin més cares.

paragraphs.en: Sound libraries exist for every instrument imaginable, including orchestral instruments and the human voice. They are a great way to make realistic demos and are used in commercial releases.
paragraphs.ca: Hi ha biblioteques de sons per a tots els instruments imaginables, incloent-hi els instruments orquestrals i la veu humana. Són una manera fantàstica de fer maquetes realistes i s'utilitzen en publicacions comercials.

paragraphs.en: For those that want a challenge, you can even record your own sound library. There is an appendix at the end with some recommendations on different sound libraries you can try.
paragraphs.ca: Per a qui vulgui un repte, fins i tot pots enregistrar la teva pròpia biblioteca de sons. Al final hi ha un apèndix amb algunes recomanacions de biblioteques de sons que pots provar.

paragraphs.en: VST and AU VST stands for Virtual Studio Technology and AU stands for Audio Unit. VST are used for Windows systems and AU are used for Apple systems.
paragraphs.ca: VST i AU. VST són les sigles de Virtual Studio Technology i AU són les sigles d'Audio Unit. Els VST s'utilitzen en sistemes Windows i els AU en sistemes Apple.

paragraphs.en: Logic Pro and GarageBand. They accomplish the same thing. They allow you to add extra software to your DAW so that it can do more stuff. This could be anything from a reverb plugin to a software guitar amplifier to a sound library that allows you to play back any orchestral instrument realistically. Software companies typically release their products in both VST and AU versions.
paragraphs.ca: Logic Pro i GarageBand. Fan la mateixa funció. Et permeten afegir programari addicional al teu DAW perquè pugui fer més coses. Això pot ser qualsevol cosa, des d'un connector de reverberació fins a un amplificador de guitarra de programari o una biblioteca de sons que et permet reproduir de manera realista qualsevol instrument orquestral. Les empreses de programari solen publicar els seus productes tant en versió VST com en versió AU.

paragraphs.en: Program recommendations For writing tab, I recommend GuitarPro. Creates professional-looking guitar tabs and plays them back.
paragraphs.ca: Recomanacions de programari. Per escriure tablatures, recomano GuitarPro. Crea tablatures de guitarra d'aspecte professional i les reprodueix.

paragraphs.en: GuitarPro is designed around a tab-first input. You can add chord and scale diagrams to your tabs and compose for multiple instruments.
paragraphs.ca: GuitarPro està dissenyat al voltant d'una entrada basada primer en la tablatura. Pots afegir diagrames d'acords i d'escales a les teves tablatures i compondre per a diversos instruments.

paragraphs.en: It's designed for guitar players. It's great for writing songs, exercises, and collaborating with other musicians. GuitarPro retails at around $80.
paragraphs.ca: Està dissenyat per a guitarristes. Va molt bé per escriure cançons, exercicis i col·laborar amb altres músics. GuitarPro es ven per uns 80 dòlars.

segments.text: MuseScore. This is a program designed around musical notation input.
If you are wanting to compose for classical instrumental or compose notation first rather than guitar first, MuseScore is great.
It can also do guitar tabs but does not give you as many articulation options as GuitarPro does for guitar.
MuseScore is free. MuseScore is a bit harder to use than GuitarPro.
For a DAW, I recommend Logic Pro or other DAW.
Great for recording and editing audio and composing.
I now use Logic Pro for writing tabs.
Logic Pro costs around $200.
One feature I love is Logic can scroll through a tab while you record it.
Other DWs that are popular, Pro Tools.
Has more audio editing options than Logic Pro, but you probably don't need these.
but isn't as good at handling MIDI as Logic Pro.
Pro tools will only work with specific hardware.
Cubase.
Recording and MIDI editing.
My metal album, Impetuous Desire, was recorded in Cubase.
Hans Zimmer, film score composer,
uses Cubase for composing movie scores.
Studio One.
A couple of my students use this.
I haven't used it myself.
It's cheap and they seem happy with it.
Reaper.
This is shareware, so you can use it for free or pay the $25 for a license.
Reaper allows you to record and edit audio, use VST, etc.
It seems similar in capability to Qubus, but without the price tag.
It has a big community and is becoming very popular.
Using computer programs correctly.
Music technology programs are complex programs.
They can do an enormous amount to make your life easier if you learn how to use them.
Many students settle for a very basic understanding of the programs they use,
and this hinders them by slowing down their workflow.
For example, let's say you wanted to enter a riff that repeats 20 times.
You could type out that riff 20 times,
or you could type it out once and then copy and paste it 20 times.
This is a simple example, but the point I'm making is this.
These programs are packed with features that will make your life easier if you learn how to use them.
Read the manual for these programs.
Watch YouTube tutorials.
Reach out and ask questions.
All of these programs have forums, Facebook groups and subreddits
with communities that will help answer your questions.
If you ever find yourself using a program and thinking it would be nice if...
then the feature you are after probably exists.
Read the manual, ask a question, and see if someone knows the answer.
If the feature doesn't exist,
another user may be able to recommend a different way of approaching the problem.
Keyboard shortcuts
Another vital part of using computer programs correctly
is learning keyboard shortcuts.
Using the mouse to do everything in these programs is horribly inefficient.
We spent a large section of this book dealing with how to make your guitar practice more efficient.
You want to apply this search for efficiency to the programs that you use.
As an example of using programs efficiently, I often practice using Logic Pro.
I will set up a backing track for the piece I'm practicing and focus on a particular section.
Now I could use my mouse, press play, play the section, get my mouse again, press stop,
move the playhead back to the start, press play again, or I can set up a loop and press the space
bar to start and let the loop play over and over for me to practice to. Then press the space bar
to stop. Which method would you rather use? For a given amount of practice time, my method with
the loop will allow you to get more repetitions in. It will also be less stressful because all
All you have to think about is your guitar playing.
You don't have to fiddle around with the mouse and set up the program for every repetition.
Programs like Logic Pro are highly customizable with keyboard shortcuts, allowing you to assign
a shortcut to nearly every function.
Over large periods, these workflow and time-saving hacks compound to make incredible differences
in the total time you spend actually on your guitar.
Yes, it is something else that you have to go and learn.
Yes, these programs have a steep learning curve, but work through it, and long-term you will reap the rewards in your playing.
Using templates.
Templates are a fantastic way to save a lot of time and work.
When setting up Guitar Pro or your DAW, you may find that you're doing a lot of the same things.
Maybe you're always adding the same instruments.
Maybe you're always loading the same virtual instruments and adding the same AU or VST over and over again.
Maybe you're making the same changes to your score settings.
You can get your computer to do all of this for you.
Open a blank file and add all the things that you would typically add.
Change the layout and score settings to things you normally use.
Then save that file as a template.
Next time you want to use those settings in a project,
all you have to do is load that template and everything is loaded for you.
Huge time savings.
You may want to make a few templates for the different types of projects you use.
For example, in Logic Pro, I have a template for rock songs and a template for orchestral projects.
Labeling your tabs and scores
When creating a tab or score, it should be correctly labelled.
When composing, you will know exactly what you are doing, but if you were to revisit your score in a few months,
you will probably find that you have forgotten a lot of what you have done and why.
You should label 1. Title 2. Structure 3. Harmony
Chord names and numerals 4. The composer
Organize your files Once you have been playing the guitar for a while,
you will start to accumulate a lot of computer files. Tabs, songs, backing tracks and exercises.
It is easy to end up with hundreds of files. You want to make sure they are organized so that you
can find them. This means using suitable file names. New song is not helpful. Exercise 2 is
not helpful. Use a file name that describes the file. Using a sensible file name will also make
it easy to search your files for what you are looking for. Create a directory structure that
makes sense. For example, you could organize your exercises into 1. Scales, 2. Sweep picking,
3. Chords
4. Theory
5. Rhythm
I took lessons from a great guitar player called George Bellis for a few years.
I would copy his lessons twice, once into a date-based hierarchy,
which made it easy to track exercises and assignments for submission week by week,
and then I would copy every lesson into a category-based hierarchy,
which has made it easy for me to reference lessons years later.
Command plus S-Twitch and backups. Save, save, save.
When working, you want to constantly be saving your work as you go.
Learn the keyboard shortcut.
Remember that whole section on learning keyboard shortcuts properly,
so that you can save in a split second while you are working without interrupting your workflow.
Make sure you have backups.
If you use a Mac, the built-in program Time Machine is a fantastic way to create backups automatically as you go.
You'll want an external hard drive that you can leave plugged in for backups.
There is a program called Backblaze, which offers very cheap, secure and automated cloud backups of your files.
Computer specifications
How powerful a computer do you need?
I've been using a late 2015 iMac since, well, around 2015. I'm writing this in 2022. It has a 3.2
gigahertz Intel quad-core i5 and 8 gigabytes of RAM. When running my DAW, Logic Pro, I'll make
sure everything else is closed and it can handle everything I throw at it okay. Apple is my
preference, but it's not necessary. I tend to find Apple computers' age well compared to Windows
machines. I've run a full orchestra through sample libraries and recorded rock music,
and it has been able to manage now and then having to pause and start again because the RAM is maxed
out. So 8GB is manageable, but you may want 16GB, or even 32GB if your budget can handle it.
Any modern computer with 8GB RAM should be fine for recording a rock band track by track with
some virtual instruments. If you're going to record multiple instruments at once, have dozens
of tracks playing back at once, and many virtual instruments get as much RAM as possible.

paragraphs.ca: Al llarg de períodes llargs, aquests trucs de flux de treball i d'estalvi de temps es van acumulant i marquen diferències increïbles en el temps total que passes realment amb la guitarra.

paragraphs.en: Yes, it is something else that you have to go and learn. Yes, these programs have a steep learning curve, but work through it, and long-term you will reap the rewards in your playing.
paragraphs.ca: Sí, és una altra cosa que has d'anar a aprendre. Sí, aquests programes tenen una corba d'aprenentatge pronunciada, però supera-la i, a llarg termini, recolliràs les recompenses en la teva manera de tocar.

paragraphs.en: Using templates. Templates are a fantastic way to save a lot of time and work. When setting up Guitar Pro or your DAW, you may find that you're doing a lot of the same things.
paragraphs.ca: Utilitzar plantilles. Les plantilles són una manera fantàstica d'estalviar molt de temps i feina. Quan configurem Guitar Pro o el teu DAW, potser descobreixes que fas moltes vegades les mateixes coses.

paragraphs.en: Maybe you're always adding the same instruments. Maybe you're always loading the same virtual instruments and adding the same AU or VST over and over again.
paragraphs.ca: Potser sempre afegeixes els mateixos instruments. Potser sempre carregues els mateixos instruments virtuals i afegeixes el mateix AU o VST una vegada i una altra.

paragraphs.en: Maybe you're making the same changes to your score settings. You can get your computer to do all of this for you. Open a blank file and add all the things that you would typically add.
paragraphs.ca: Potser fas els mateixos canvis a la configuració de la partitura. Pots aconseguir que l'ordinador faci tot això per tu. Obre un fitxer buit i afegeix-hi tot el que normalment afegeixes.

paragraphs.en: Change the layout and score settings to things you normally use. Then save that file as a template. Next time you want to use those settings in a project, all you have to do is load that template and everything is loaded for you.
paragraphs.ca: Canvia la disposició i la configuració de la partitura pels valors que fas servir normalment. Després desa aquest fitxer com a plantilla. La propera vegada que vulguis fer servir aquesta configuració en un projecte, només hauràs de carregar aquesta plantilla i tot es carregarà per tu.

paragraphs.en: Huge time savings. You may want to make a few templates for the different types of projects you use. For example, in Logic Pro, I have a template for rock songs and a template for orchestral projects.
paragraphs.ca: Un estalvi de temps enorme. Potser vols fer unes quantes plantilles per als diferents tipus de projectes que fas servir. Per exemple, a Logic Pro tinc una plantilla per a cançons de rock i una plantilla per a projectes orquestrals.

paragraphs.en: Labeling your tabs and scores When creating a tab or score, it should be correctly labelled. When composing, you will know exactly what you are doing, but if you were to revisit your score in a few months, you will probably find that you have forgotten a lot of what you have done and why.
paragraphs.ca: Etiquetar les teves tablatures i partitures. Quan crees una tablatura o una partitura, hauria d'estar correctament etiquetada. Quan compons, saps exactament què fas, però si tornessis a la teva partitura uns quants mesos després, probablement descobriries que has oblidat bona part del que has fet i per què.

paragraphs.en: You should label 1. Title 2. Structure 3. Harmony Chord names and numerals 4. The composer Organize your files Once you have been playing the guitar for a while, you will start to accumulate a lot of computer files. Tabs, songs, backing tracks and exercises.
paragraphs.ca: Hauries d'etiquetar: 1. Títol 2. Estructura 3. Harmonia: noms dels acords i xifres 4. El compositor. Organitza els teus fitxers. Un cop portes un temps tocant la guitarra, comences a acumular molts fitxers d'ordinador. Tablatures, cançons, bases d'acompanyament i exercicis.

paragraphs.en: It is easy to end up with hundreds of files. You want to make sure they are organized so that you can find them. This means using suitable file names. New song is not helpful. Exercise 2 is not helpful. Use a file name that describes the file. Using a sensible file name will also make it easy to search your files for what you are looking for. Create a directory structure that makes sense. For example, you could organize your exercises into 1. Scales, 2. Sweep picking,
paragraphs.ca: És fàcil acabar amb centenars de fitxers. Vols assegurar-te que estan organitzats per poder-los trobar. Això vol dir fer servir noms de fitxer adequats. «Cançó nova» no ajuda. «Exercici 2» no ajuda. Fes servir un nom de fitxer que descrigui el fitxer. Fer servir un nom de fitxer sensat també et facilitarà cercar allò que busques entre els teus fitxers. Crea una estructura de directoris que tingui sentit. Per exemple, podries organitzar els teus exercicis en 1. Escales, 2. Sweep picking,

paragraphs.en: 3. Chords 4. Theory 5. Rhythm I took lessons from a great guitar player called George Bellis for a few years. I would copy his lessons twice, once into a date-based hierarchy, which made it easy to track exercises and assignments for submission week by week, and then I would copy every lesson into a category-based hierarchy, which has made it easy for me to reference lessons years later.
paragraphs.ca: 3. Acords 4. Teoria 5. Ritme. Vaig prendre classes d'un gran guitarrista anomenat George Bellis durant uns quants anys. Copiava les seves lliçons dues vegades: una en una jerarquia basada en dates, que facilitava el seguiment dels exercicis i les tasques per lliurar setmana a setmana, i després copiava cada lliçó en una jerarquia basada en categories, que m'ha facilitat consultar les lliçons anys després.

paragraphs.en: Command plus S-Twitch and backups. Save, save, save. When working, you want to constantly be saving your work as you go.
paragraphs.ca: Command + S: desar i còpies de seguretat. Desa, desa, desa. Quan treballes, vols desar la feina constantment a mesura que avances.

paragraphs.en: Learn the keyboard shortcut. Remember that whole section on learning keyboard shortcuts properly, so that you can save in a split second while you are working without interrupting your workflow.
paragraphs.ca: Aprèn la drecera de teclat. Recorda tota aquella secció sobre aprendre bé les dreceres de teclat, perquè puguis desar en una fracció de segon mentre treballes sense interrompre el teu flux de treball.

paragraphs.en: Make sure you have backups. If you use a Mac, the built-in program Time Machine is a fantastic way to create backups automatically as you go.
paragraphs.ca: Assegura't de tenir còpies de seguretat. Si fas servir un Mac, el programa integrat Time Machine és una manera fantàstica de crear còpies de seguretat automàticament a mesura que avances.

paragraphs.en: You'll want an external hard drive that you can leave plugged in for backups. There is a program called Backblaze, which offers very cheap, secure and automated cloud backups of your files.
paragraphs.ca: Voldràs un disc dur extern que puguis deixar connectat per a les còpies de seguretat. Hi ha un programa anomenat Backblaze que ofereix còpies de seguretat al núvol dels teus fitxers molt barates, segures i automatitzades.

paragraphs.en: Computer specifications How powerful a computer do you need? I've been using a late 2015 iMac since, well, around 2015. I'm writing this in 2022. It has a 3.2 gigahertz Intel quad-core i5 and 8 gigabytes of RAM. When running my DAW, Logic Pro, I'll make sure everything else is closed and it can handle everything I throw at it okay. Apple is my preference, but it's not necessary. I tend to find Apple computers' age well compared to Windows
paragraphs.ca: Especificacions de l'ordinador. Quant de potent ha de ser un ordinador? Faig servir un iMac de finals del 2015 des del, bé, cap al 2015. Escric això el 2022. Té un Intel quad-core i5 de 3,2 gigahertz i 8 gigabytes de RAM. Quan faig anar el meu DAW, Logic Pro, m'asseguro que tot la resta estigui tancat, i pot gestionar tot el que li llanço, més o menys. Apple és la meva preferència, però no és necessari. Acostumo a trobar que els ordinadors Apple envelleixen bé en comparació amb les màquines

paragraphs.en: machines. I've run a full orchestra through sample libraries and recorded rock music, and it has been able to manage now and then having to pause and start again because the RAM is maxed out. So 8GB is manageable, but you may want 16GB, or even 32GB if your budget can handle it.
paragraphs.ca: Windows. He fet anar una orquestra completa amb biblioteques de mostres i he enregistrat música rock, i ha estat capaç de gestionar-ho, amb alguna pausa i reinici de tant en tant perquè la RAM s'esgotava. Així que 8 GB és gestionable, però potser voldràs 16 GB, o fins i tot 32 GB si el teu pressupost ho pot assumir.

paragraphs.en: Any modern computer with 8GB RAM should be fine for recording a rock band track by track with some virtual instruments. If you're going to record multiple instruments at once, have dozens of tracks playing back at once, and many virtual instruments get as much RAM as possible.
paragraphs.ca: Qualsevol ordinador modern amb 8 GB de RAM hauria de ser suficient per enregistrar un grup de rock pista a pista amb alguns instruments virtuals. Si vols enregistrar diversos instruments alhora, tenir desenes de pistes sonant alhora i molts instruments virtuals, aconsegueix tanta RAM com puguis.

segments.text: Section 6. Healthy Living. This is a book on learning guitar and creativity. Why are we
talking about health? Firstly, I am not a doctor, and this is not medical advice. If you want to
improve your health, talk to your doctor. These are just ideas that I have found useful.
You should use this section as a list of things to research and a recollection of my own experiences
There is a modern trend of treating the mind and body as separate entities
In philosophy, this is a problem referred to as the mind-body dichotomy
The mind and the body are two parts of the same thing
A human being
A healthy mind helps have a healthy body and vice versa
Taking care of your health helps your mind work more effectively, which in turn helps you be more creative.
Here are a few things that I have found useful.
What you put into your body.
Food is a modern vice.
63% of adults in the UK are overweight, footnote 9.
Over 73% of adults in America are overweight, footnote 10.
While it is a testament to the modern world that we can supply calories in abundance at a lower cost
than ever before in human history, it has become a problem. Controlling the food you eat is an
important part of looking after your health. You want to keep an eye on how much of the following
you consume. 1. Processed food. 2. Refined sugar. 3. Seed oils. Refined oils. 4. Flour.
If you're eating trash, try to find healthier substitutes. You probably eat a lot of what you
do from habit, not from enjoyment. Make sure that you get enough protein. If you have things like
fizzy drinks, replace them with water with some apple or lemon. Fizzy drinks are a disaster for
your health. Foods with vegetable oils, seed oils are also quite bad for your health. There is a
great book called The Mood Cure, which goes over the effects these substances have on your body.
This doesn't mean don't have fun food, but save them as a weekly treat rather than something you
eat every day. Having something each day that is around 10% of your daily calories is a good way
to have something fun. It goes without saying that if you are abusing drugs or having an excess of
alcohol, removing those from your diet will be incredibly beneficial. Try and focus on fresh
whole foods, such as fresh meat and fresh vegetables. Cook using roasting or butter,
and avoid using seed oils or processed oils. Exercise. Have a walk every day, ideally two
walks. Do some resistance training a few times a week. One of the most time-effective workouts
I've tried is Convict Conditioning by Coach Paul Wade. This book is a series of bodyweight exercises
you can do two to three times a week. They don't take very long, sometimes 20 minutes for a workout.
Simple and Sinister by Pavel Fzatzulein
is a great guide to using a kettlebell for a daily workout. Disclaimer, I haven't used this program, but it's on my list to try.
I don't recommend other exercise regimens such as CrossFit. I did CrossFit for a couple of years, and while I got quite strong quite quickly, I also took more injuries than I'd have liked.
Bodybuilding is effective for increasing strength, but can wear out your joints over time, and people who do bodybuilding to an extreme degree tend to die young.
Fasting. Something I've particularly enjoyed is fasting. There is an idea in the modern world
that we need to eat three square meals a day, and with snacks in between, we're effectively
eating nearly every waking hour. Intermittent fasting is a great way to help lose some weight
and also free up some time. I usually eat between 2pm and 8pm. I rarely feel hungry in the mornings
and use the time I save to do something useful, like work on my guitar playing.
I know that some people love breakfast foods.
In my opinion, they're the best foods, so I still enjoy them.
I sometimes have a cooked breakfast as my lunch.
My main meal is usually at 2 p.m. with meat, eggs, green vegetables,
sometimes kale, and a natural carbohydrate, either rice or baked potatoes.
My second meal at around 6-8pm is usually some whole wheat pasta with cheese on top.
There are several ways you can try intermittent fasting.
One of my friends dropped a ton of weight recently when she stopped eating after 6pm.
In general, the idea is that you eat inside an 8-hour window and don't eat for 16 hours each day.
Longer fasts for 24 hours with just water and some salt if you're feeling sleepy
are a good way to curb your appetite and rest your body.
I usually do a 24-hour fast once or twice a week.
I recently did a two-day fast and will be doing three and four-day fasts in a couple of months.
Get sunlight
If you are in California, southern Europe, or somewhere similarly sunny,
this won't apply to you so much.
but if you are in a cloudy place such as northern Europe, then get more sunlight.
Sunlight creates vitamin D, which is vital for the immune system and general well-being slash
happiness. It also helps your body clock with your circadian rhythm. Most people would benefit
from spending more time outside in general and getting fresh air. Something I've adopted into
my mornings is to take 20 to 30 minutes to sit in my garden and listen to music. It's quite relaxing
and it's enjoyable to listen to music rather than having it as a background to my day.

segments.text: Section 7. Completing projects. This entire section is something that I only came to understand
relatively recently. In retrospect, like many things in retrospect, it seems obvious.
Be prolific. A lot of the greatest creatives in history were prolific. A lot of people will think
I need to be creative to be prolific, but this logic is back to front. Being prolific helps
you become more creative. There is a story of a pottery teacher who experimented with their class.
The class was split in two. One half had to create one pot. They could take as long as they wanted
to make it, and their grade would be based on that single pot. The other half of the class would be
graded on the number of pots that they created. Who made the best pots? You may be surprised that
the half of the class that were prolific and created as many pots as possible ended up creating
the best pots. Every time they made a pot, they learned a little bit more about what does and
doesn't work. Reading and studying theory and composition is a vital part of becoming more
creative, but it is a step in the right direction. Eventually, you have to put pen to page and
compose something. And the more you compose, the more you will learn about what works and doesn't
work, the more you will learn about weaknesses in your understanding that need correcting,
and the more you will learn about what you enjoy composing.
Perfectionism. What if it sucks? A stumbling block that creatives, and aspiring creatives,
often face when it comes to being prolific, is perfectionism. Believe me, I understand this.
In 2017, I released a heavy metal album called Impetuous Desire. It's fair to say that it's
pretty good. For three months before releasing it, I listened to it every night, picking apart
every tiny flaw I could find, wondering if I should just delete it. In retrospect, that was
a bit neurotic, but whatever you want to call it, perfectionism, imposter syndrome, who am I to
release music, is a real psychological effect that you will have to face. I've seen students go
through this when they start composing music or recording their own songs. There is a real
fear when it comes to releasing their creations to the public. One of the most effective ways
I have found of dealing with this is to take the following stance. It is not my job to judge my
work. It is my job to create to the best of my ability with as much effort as I can and then
to release it. It is someone else's job to judge it. How to choose your next project. Earlier,
we discuss the mindset of improving our playing, where we set perfection as the direction that we
want to move in, and being 1% better than we were last week is the goal of practicing.
We will use a similar idea for choosing the projects that we want to work on.
Dream big, move small. Entertain big dreams. What does a big dream look like for you?
Playing a show to 10,000 people? Releasing an album? Recording a song with an orchestra?
Take some time right now to think about it for a moment.
You'll know you've hit the right big idea when you get a jolt of excitement.
Maybe you'll have an uncontrollable smile when you picture yourself doing the big idea.
Now break that big idea down into smaller ideas.
For example, let's say you want to, one day, compose an album.
We could break down composing an album into the following steps.
1. Compose a riff.
2. Compose a verse or chorus.
3. Compose a song.
4. Compose an album.
So if you want to one day compose your own album, you can start today by writing a riff.
Maybe you spend a few months or a couple of years composing riffs and learning how to arrange other instruments, drums, bass, etc. around those riffs.
Write 100 riffs.
Then you have a go at writing a verse.
Then write 50 verses.
Then you have a go at writing a full song.
We are slowly moving up in levels of complexity.
Let's say you want to play a show for 10,000 people.
We could break that down like this.
1. Perform to 20 people, open mic night.
2. Perform to 100 people, bar show.
3. Perform to 500 people, club show.
4. Perform to 1,000 people, small festival show.
5. Perform to 10,000 people, festival show.
and now you have to figure out how to slowly move through this ladder.
For an open mic night, you need to learn a few songs.
Maybe you can do instrumental songs or you go down to watch a few times,
find a singer and ask if you can accompany them in a couple of weeks.
Once you've done a few of those, maybe you're going to look for a band you can join
or start and play a few bar shows together.
Most big cities will have hundreds of places you can play at.
Once your band is getting regular experience playing and building a bit of a following,
you can think about contacting promoters to position yourself to be an opening act for bigger bands coming through on tour, etc.
We start at a small level and slowly build up our ability.
This process will take several years, but like anything else, if you just keep chipping away at it, you will make progress.
What's possible at this point in time?
In the real world, we have limits on our resources.
When deciding what projects we are going to take on,
we have to know what is required to complete those projects,
and if we have the resources to do so.
If there is a mismatch between what the project requires and the resources we have,
we need to find a way to bridge the gap, so that our project becomes possible.
And usually, given the amount of technology that is available,
there is a way to bridge the gap.
For example, let's say that you want to record an album,
but you can't afford to hire a drummer and the studio time that a drummer would need.
An album of drums would take two to five days depending on the drummer.
At $250 per day for a studio, we are talking $500 to one, $250 in studio time.
The drummer may want $1.50 per hour.
With six-hour days, that's $300 per day,
so $600 to one, $500 for your drummer, bringing you to a total cost of one, $100 to two,
$750 just to record drums. At $250 per day for a studio, we are talking $500 to $1,250 in studio
time. The drummer may want $50 per hour. With six-hour days, that's $300 per day, so $600 to
$1,500 for your drummer, bringing you to a total cost of $1,100 to $2,750 just to record drums.
Maybe that's in your budget, or maybe it isn't. What other options do you have? You could find an
online marketplace for session musicians, there are a few of these, and hire someone there who
has a home studio and will record for $100 per song. You now have studio quality drums for $1,000
assuming 10 songs on your album.
Is that too much?
You could use a drum sample library.
A sample library is when someone records an instrument being played,
such as a drum kit, and then plays those sounds back.
So you program the sample library to play the snare at certain points,
the hi-hats at others, etc.
Your sample library for a drum kit
could be anything from $150 to $450.
I'll include a list of sample libraries in the appendix.
Something worth pointing out is that you may have to apply just as much creativity
to finding a way to see your project through to completion as you do in the project itself.
It's worth noting that finding a cheaper way to do something
does not necessarily mean getting a worse result.
Here is a list of options that you can use for different projects
to help get your creative juices flowing.
Record drums for an album.
1. Hire a famous drummer and go to a recording studio.
2. Hire a drum teacher from a local music school and go to a recording studio.
3. Hire a drum teacher from a music school that can record from home.
I did this for the drums on Impetuous Desire and they sound great.
4. Hire a session drummer online who can record.
5. Hire a session drummer to record an electric drum kit
and send you the MIDI data to put into a drum sample library.
6. Program a drum sample library yourself.
Record guitars for your song.
1. Go to a fancy studio with nice amps and record using their amps.
2. Build a recording room to keep your amps in and record them.
3. Record your own amps at home with a cabinet isolation box.
4. Record your own amps at home with a microphone and a power attenuator.
5. Use a Kemper, Axe FX, AMP cloner.
Get some good presets online.
6. Use digital AMP simulators such as Positive Grid Bias.
7. Use default digital AMP simulators in Logic Pro X.
No matter what your level of resources is,
there is something that you can do to get your project completed.
Figure it out and do it.
Sure, it might not be the quality that you want,
But a completed project that is imperfect is better than a perfect project that never happens.
And you will probably find that as you complete projects,
your ability to find ways to complete them and access to resources increases.
Choosing a musical direction
Some people know exactly what they want to do musically, and some don't.
You will probably find that as you put more time into studying music,
you become aware of options that you didn't know originally existed
and what you are interested in develops.
You may find your original interests and musical desires change over time,
and this is okay.
Some people aren't sure what they are interested in,
so how can you become prolific if you are not sure what it is you want to do?
The best way to approach this is similar to how you would approach that problem
with other areas in your life.
Try out a whole bunch of different things, give them a serious go,
and then spend some time reflecting on whether you enjoyed them or not.
If you enjoyed them, then try more things in that direction.
If you didn't enjoy them, ask yourself why.
Did you not enjoy it because...
1. You tried something that was too far beyond your ability level,
so maybe you would enjoy it in the future when you're at a higher level.
2. You dislike everything about what you tried.
3. Or maybe there was only an element of the thing you tried that you disliked.
Figure out what that thing is and try again.
Let's use some examples.
Let's say you aren't too sure about a genre that you like.
So you choose five songs from different genres,
and over the next five months, you're going to learn them.
One of the songs you choose is a heavy metal song.
When you listen to the song, it's quite exciting,
but you struggle to play it.
You just can't crack getting those riffs to sound correct,
and as a consequence, you don't enjoy the process of trying to learn this song.
Does that mean that you shouldn't try learning any metal songs?
A better approach would be to try again with some easier songs in that genre
or possibly choose sections of songs to play rather than playing entire songs.
Maybe across the five genres you find that you can play the songs okay,
but the whole process of learning other people's music is just boring to you.
You enjoy playing the guitar and want to do more with it.
In that case...
Maybe you need to explore improvisation and composition. Maybe learning the songs isn't that interesting, but performing them gives you a thrill like nothing you've experienced in life.
Maybe learning the songs is okay and there are elements of each song you like, which you use as criteria to develop your taste in music and find other pieces to play.
by honing in on precisely what it is that we do and don't like
and can then create a hypothesis and experiments
to find something that we do like
and then we can do more of that.
This process may take some time
and you may also find that figuring out precisely what it is you do
and don't like is a challenge
and takes a bit more introspection than you at first thought
but if you work the process
you will find that you can deepen your enjoyment of music and the guitar.
Completing projects
Most guitar players find it easy to start projects, and much harder to complete projects.
Usually, guitar players who have been playing for a while have an archive of riffs, licks,
and ideas that they have created over the years that sit on their computer, gathering
metaphorical dust.
It's important to be able to complete projects, not just start them.
There are a few possible components to this problem.
1. Time management
2. Knowledge gaps
3. Insecurity
4. Technology
5. Premature judgment
You may find you have a mix of all four.
Let's break down each one and see how it can impact completing projects and what you can do about it.
Time management
Having a flash of inspiration, writing a cool riff and recording it and tabbing it out doesn't take very long.
It may even take as little as 5, 10 minutes.
However, writing out parts for other instruments, getting a structure together,
and practicing so you can play the parts accurately can take an enormous amount of time.
If you are struggling to complete projects, you may have to reorganize your priorities.
For example, let's say that you currently practice for one hour a day.
You do a 10-minute warm-up, 15 minutes on a scale, 15 minutes on improvisation, 10 minutes on theory, and 10 minutes on writing new ideas.
So you effectively have 10 minutes, your new ideas time, to work on completing your song.
It's probably going nowhere fast.
You may find that you have to reduce your other elements of practice to 5 minutes each so that you can spend 40 minutes a day completing your song.
or you use an A-B schedule
we covered this in the section on how to practice
and do your guitar practice on day A
and work on your song on day B
or maybe you change something else in your life
so that you can put an extra hour a day
into working on your song
and getting your practice done
Most problems on guitar can be solved with time
and completing a song is certainly one of them

paragraphs.ca: 6. Programar tu mateix una biblioteca de mostres de bateria. Gravar les guitarres de la teva cançó. 1. Anar a un estudi luxós amb amplificadors bons i gravar amb els seus amplificadors.

paragraphs.en: 2. Build a recording room to keep your amps in and record them. 3. Record your own amps at home with a cabinet isolation box.
paragraphs.ca: 2. Construir una sala de gravació per guardar-hi els teus amplificadors i gravar-los. 3. Gravar els teus amplificadors a casa amb una caixa d'aïllament per a altaveus.

paragraphs.en: 4. Record your own amps at home with a microphone and a power attenuator. 5. Use a Kemper, Axe FX, AMP cloner. Get some good presets online.
paragraphs.ca: 4. Gravar els teus amplificadors a casa amb un micròfon i un atenuador de potència. 5. Fer servir un Kemper, Axe FX, clonador d'amplificadors. Baixa't bons presets en línia.

paragraphs.en: 6. Use digital AMP simulators such as Positive Grid Bias. 7. Use default digital AMP simulators in Logic Pro X. No matter what your level of resources is, there is something that you can do to get your project completed.
paragraphs.ca: 6. Fer servir simuladors digitals d'amplificador com Positive Grid Bias. 7. Fer servir els simuladors digitals d'amplificador per defecte de Logic Pro X. Sigui quin sigui el teu nivell de recursos, hi ha alguna cosa que pots fer per completar el teu projecte.

paragraphs.en: Figure it out and do it. Sure, it might not be the quality that you want, But a completed project that is imperfect is better than a perfect project that never happens.
paragraphs.ca: Esbrina-ho i fes-ho. És clar que potser no tindrà la qualitat que vols, però un projecte acabat i imperfecte és millor que un projecte perfecte que mai no passa.

paragraphs.en: And you will probably find that as you complete projects, your ability to find ways to complete them and access to resources increases.
paragraphs.ca: I probablement veuràs que, a mesura que completes projectes, augmenta la teva capacitat de trobar maneres de completar-los i el teu accés a recursos.

paragraphs.en: Choosing a musical direction Some people know exactly what they want to do musically, and some don't. You will probably find that as you put more time into studying music, you become aware of options that you didn't know originally existed and what you are interested in develops.
paragraphs.ca: Triar una direcció musical. Algunes persones saben exactament què volen fer musicalment, i d'altres no. Probablement veuràs que, com més temps dediques a estudiar música, més conscient ets d'opcions que originalment no sabies que existien i els teus interessos es van desenvolupant.

paragraphs.en: You may find your original interests and musical desires change over time, and this is okay. Some people aren't sure what they are interested in, so how can you become prolific if you are not sure what it is you want to do?
paragraphs.ca: Potser descobriràs que els teus interessos i desitjos musicals originals canvien amb el temps, i això està bé. Algunes persones no estan segures de què els interessa, així que com pots ser prolífic si no estàs segur de què vols fer?

paragraphs.en: The best way to approach this is similar to how you would approach that problem with other areas in your life. Try out a whole bunch of different things, give them a serious go, and then spend some time reflecting on whether you enjoyed them or not.
paragraphs.ca: La millor manera d'afrontar-ho és similar a com afrontaries aquest problema en altres àmbits de la teva vida. Prova un munt de coses diferents, pren-t'ho seriosament i després dedica una estona a reflexionar sobre si t'han agradat o no.

paragraphs.en: If you enjoyed them, then try more things in that direction. If you didn't enjoy them, ask yourself why. Did you not enjoy it because...
paragraphs.ca: Si t'han agradat, prova més coses en aquella direcció. Si no t'han agradat, pregunta't per què. No t'ha agradat perquè...

paragraphs.en: 1. You tried something that was too far beyond your ability level, so maybe you would enjoy it in the future when you're at a higher level.
paragraphs.ca: 1. Has provat una cosa que estava massa enllà del teu nivell de capacitat, així que potser t'agradaria en el futur, quan estiguessis a un nivell més alt.

paragraphs.en: 2. You dislike everything about what you tried. 3. Or maybe there was only an element of the thing you tried that you disliked.
paragraphs.ca: 2. No t'agrada res del que has provat. 3. O potser només hi havia un element d'allò que has provat que no t'agradava.

paragraphs.en: Figure out what that thing is and try again. Let's use some examples. Let's say you aren't too sure about a genre that you like.
paragraphs.ca: Esbrina què és aquesta cosa i torna-ho a provar. Fem servir alguns exemples. Posem que no estàs gaire segur de quin gènere t'agrada.

paragraphs.en: So you choose five songs from different genres, and over the next five months, you're going to learn them. One of the songs you choose is a heavy metal song.
paragraphs.ca: Així que tries cinc cançons de gèneres diferents i, durant els cinc mesos següents, les aprens. Una de les cançons que tries és una cançó de heavy metal.

paragraphs.en: When you listen to the song, it's quite exciting, but you struggle to play it. You just can't crack getting those riffs to sound correct, and as a consequence, you don't enjoy the process of trying to learn this song.
paragraphs.ca: Quan escoltes la cançó, és força emocionant, però et costa tocar-la. No aconsegueixes que aquells riffs sonin correctes i, en conseqüència, no gaudeixes del procés d'intentar aprendre aquesta cançó.

paragraphs.en: Does that mean that you shouldn't try learning any metal songs? A better approach would be to try again with some easier songs in that genre or possibly choose sections of songs to play rather than playing entire songs.
paragraphs.ca: Vol dir això que no hauries de provar d'aprendre cap cançó de metal? Una millor manera d'afrontar-ho seria tornar-ho a provar amb cançons més fàcils d'aquell gènere o, possiblement, triar seccions de cançons per tocar en lloc de cançons senceres.

paragraphs.en: Maybe across the five genres you find that you can play the songs okay, but the whole process of learning other people's music is just boring to you.
paragraphs.ca: Potser, entre els cinc gèneres, trobes que pots tocar les cançons bé, però tot el procés d'aprendre música d'altres persones simplement t'avorreix.

paragraphs.en: You enjoy playing the guitar and want to do more with it. In that case... Maybe you need to explore improvisation and composition. Maybe learning the songs isn't that interesting, but performing them gives you a thrill like nothing you've experienced in life.
paragraphs.ca: Gaudeixes tocant la guitarra i vols fer-ne més coses. En aquest cas... Potser has d'explorar la improvisació i la composició. Potser aprendre les cançons no és tan interessant, però interpretar-les et dona una emoció com cap altra que hagis viscut.

paragraphs.en: Maybe learning the songs is okay and there are elements of each song you like, which you use as criteria to develop your taste in music and find other pieces to play.
paragraphs.ca: Potser aprendre les cançons està bé i hi ha elements de cada cançó que t'agraden, que fas servir com a criteri per desenvolupar el teu gust musical i trobar altres peces per tocar.

paragraphs.en: by honing in on precisely what it is that we do and don't like and can then create a hypothesis and experiments to find something that we do like and then we can do more of that.
paragraphs.ca: fixant-nos precisament en què ens agrada i què no, podem crear una hipòtesi i experiments per trobar alguna cosa que ens agradi i després fer-ne més.

paragraphs.en: This process may take some time and you may also find that figuring out precisely what it is you do and don't like is a challenge and takes a bit more introspection than you at first thought but if you work the process you will find that you can deepen your enjoyment of music and the guitar.
paragraphs.ca: Aquest procés pot trigar una mica i també pots trobar que esbrinar exactament què t'agrada i què no és un repte i requereix una mica més d'introspecció del que pensaves al principi, però si treballes el procés veuràs que pots aprofundir en el teu gaudi de la música i de la guitarra.

paragraphs.en: Completing projects Most guitar players find it easy to start projects, and much harder to complete projects. Usually, guitar players who have been playing for a while have an archive of riffs, licks, and ideas that they have created over the years that sit on their computer, gathering metaphorical dust.
paragraphs.ca: Completar projectes. La majoria de guitarristes troben fàcil començar projectes i molt més difícil completar-los. Normalment, els guitarristes que fa temps que toquen tenen un arxiu de riffs, licks i idees que han creat al llarg dels anys i que descansen al seu ordinador, acumulant pols metafòrica.

paragraphs.en: It's important to be able to complete projects, not just start them. There are a few possible components to this problem.
paragraphs.ca: És important saber completar projectes, no només començar-los. Hi ha uns quants components possibles d'aquest problema.

paragraphs.en: 1. Time management 2. Knowledge gaps 3. Insecurity 4. Technology 5. Premature judgment You may find you have a mix of all four.
paragraphs.ca: 1. Gestió del temps 2. Llacunes de coneixement 3. Inseguretat 4. Tecnologia 5. Judici prematur. Potser veuràs que tens una barreja dels quatre.

paragraphs.en: Let's break down each one and see how it can impact completing projects and what you can do about it. Time management Having a flash of inspiration, writing a cool riff and recording it and tabbing it out doesn't take very long.
paragraphs.ca: Desglossem cadascun i vegem com pot afectar el fet de completar projectes i què hi pots fer. Gestió del temps. Tenir un rampell d'inspiració, escriure un riff genial, gravar-lo i fer-ne la tablatura no triga gaire.

paragraphs.en: It may even take as little as 5, 10 minutes. However, writing out parts for other instruments, getting a structure together, and practicing so you can play the parts accurately can take an enormous amount of time.
paragraphs.ca: Potser fins i tot triga només 5 o 10 minuts. Tanmateix, escriure les parts d'altres instruments, muntar una estructura i practicar per poder tocar les parts amb precisió pot trigar una quantitat enorme de temps.

paragraphs.en: If you are struggling to complete projects, you may have to reorganize your priorities. For example, let's say that you currently practice for one hour a day.
paragraphs.ca: Si et costa completar projectes, potser hauràs de reorganitzar les teves prioritats. Per exemple, posem que actualment practiques una hora al dia.

paragraphs.en: You do a 10-minute warm-up, 15 minutes on a scale, 15 minutes on improvisation, 10 minutes on theory, and 10 minutes on writing new ideas.
paragraphs.ca: Fas un escalfament de 10 minuts, 15 minuts d'escala, 15 minuts d'improvisació, 10 minuts de teoria i 10 minuts d'escriure idees noves.

paragraphs.en: So you effectively have 10 minutes, your new ideas time, to work on completing your song. It's probably going nowhere fast.
paragraphs.ca: Així que efectivament tens 10 minuts, el teu temps d'idees noves, per treballar a completar la teva cançó. Probablement no va enlloc de pressa.

paragraphs.en: You may find that you have to reduce your other elements of practice to 5 minutes each so that you can spend 40 minutes a day completing your song.
paragraphs.ca: Potser veuràs que has de reduir els altres elements de la pràctica a 5 minuts cadascun per poder dedicar 40 minuts al dia a completar la teva cançó.

paragraphs.en: or you use an A-B schedule we covered this in the section on how to practice and do your guitar practice on day A and work on your song on day B or maybe you change something else in your life so that you can put an extra hour a day into working on your song and getting your practice done Most problems on guitar can be solved with time and completing a song is certainly one of them
paragraphs.ca: o fas servir un programa A-B; ho vam tractar a la secció sobre com practicar, i fas la pràctica de guitarra el dia A i treballes la teva cançó el dia B, o potser canvies alguna altra cosa de la teva vida per poder dedicar una hora extra al dia a treballar la teva cançó i fer la teva pràctica. La majoria de problemes amb la guitarra es poden resoldre amb temps, i completar una cançó és sens dubte un d'ells.

segments.text: Knowledge gaps
Collaboration
You may understand, or get the inspiration, to write a riff, but you may not understand how to write parts for drums, bass, voice or lead.
Or maybe you don't understand structure or form in music.
If you can identify these problems, you can then find resources or teachers to help you fix those problems.
This can be a slow process.
You may find that it takes a year or two to fix those knowledge gaps,
but you will be a much more competent musician and more creative after doing so.
You can also hire people to help you.
When I did Impetuous Desire, I had no idea how to write drum parts,
something I have since rectified.
I recorded demos of the guitar parts, recorded to a click,
and sent them to a great drummer who made drum parts and recorded them.
I think he did the entire thing in one to two days.
I was also quite poor at writing vocal melodies
I had the singer on the album improvise different vocal melodies
and send me recordings
He would send me three takes of each instrumental demo
with him going ooh, ah, etc. over the top
I would then cut and edit the bits I liked best
into one master demo
and then I wrote lyrics to that melody
I found that the quality of my lyrics improved dramatically
by having a good vocal melody to write to
An interesting side note on the vocal melodies,
there were some parts where I liked the melodies the singer had made,
but the lyrics weren't right for that part of the song.
I turned those sections into an instrumental break with some lead guitar
based on the vocal melody the singer had created.
When it comes to structuring how you collaborate, there are two ways.
One, the collaborator takes a percentage of the songwriting credits.
2. The collaborator is paid, and you own 100% of the song. How you structure things is up to you,
but at a lower level, people will only collaborate to get paid, unless you are starting a band with
someone. Insecurity. Maybe you make a riff, and then think to yourself, this sucks. The truth is,
it's probably not as bad as you think. And even if it is, there are still plenty of people that
enjoy awful music. As cheesy as it sounds, we are often our own worst critics. At the start of this
section, we discussed perfectionism, and that is quite applicable here. Let's go with the idea that
your riff does suck. So what? That doesn't mean that you suck. It just means that the little piece
of music you wrote sucks. You don't have to show this to anyone or release it. Take the idea and
roll with it. Take your sucky riff and turn it into a whole song. I guarantee that you will learn
much more by taking a bad riff and turning it into a song than by waiting to write the perfect riff
before you start working on your songwriting. The best way to write a great song is to write
100 bad songs. No one has to hear them. Write 100 bad songs, accept that they won't be great,
but that you're working through a process, maybe they're practice songs, and I guarantee that if
you do go and work through writing 100 songs, you will write a few that you quite enjoy and can take
some pride in. Technology. Is there a problem with technology that is holding you back from
completing your project? This was something that we discussed under what's possible at this point
in time. Can you borrow gear from a friend? Go to a practice studio and use gear there?
Rent gear? Save up over time for a piece of gear? Make do with something that isn't quite as good?
If the problem is operating your gear software, read the manual, ask a friend to help you,
get help from a Facebook group forum, find someone who knows how to use it and get lessons,
or find a book on Amazon. There are plenty of options. Figure something out and move forwards.
Even if you aren't sure if you have a solution, give something a go, then evaluate and try again.
Premature judgment. Sometimes we don't complete projects because we write off our ideas before
they have had a chance to blossom. As guitar players, we often have a guitar-centric view
of writing music. We write some guitar parts and then arrange the other instruments around that.
There is nothing wrong with this approach. We'll look at it, and others, later when we look at
creativity techniques. But it is important to remember that there are other instruments.
Unless you are writing a piece where the guitar is the only instrument, you have to bear in mind
that the guitar does not exist in a vacuum. Even the simplest riff, for example, a few power chords
can sound incredible when matched with drums and bass guitar. There are plenty of great songs that
do this. So next time you have an idea, don't write it off. Have your idea, work on your idea,
maybe refine it, create some variations, add some context to your idea with other instruments,
and then decide if you want to keep it or not. Only judge your idea once it is complete.
I would go as far as not judging your ideas at all.
Occasionally I will trash an idea if it isn't working,
but most of the time I'll keep working on my ideas until they're finished as a complete song.
Dealing with ideas
Once you start having ideas, what should you do with them?
I would recommend that you record the idea somehow, whether that is a tab or a recording.
I try to put all my new ideas into a new Logic Pro project,
then I can record them and have the tab all within the same program.
I can then easily work on it at a later date.
Try and give your idea a file name that is more descriptive than New Idea 20
so you have some chance of remembering what it is when you next look at it.
And at a minimum, keep your new ideas inside the same folder on your computer.
What do people listen to when they listen to music?
Before we think about recording our music,
it's worth thinking about what the average person is listening to when they listen to music.
There are two main things the average person is listening to when they listen to music.
1. Production quality. This is the guitar tone, quality of the mix, etc.
2. Timing. Do the instruments sound in time? Some genres defy these conventions, for example,
punk and black metal. But even there, if you compare the successful commercial releases to
the unsuccessful or more underground releases, you can see that these two factors are at play.
So when it comes to recording our musical creations, we want to make sure that we can play in time,
which should be a given if you've been practicing correctly, and we also want to make sure the
production quality is as good as possible from getting a great tone to mixing.
Recording tips. Completing projects means that you're going to be doing a lot of recording,
whether it's creating demos, going to a studio or recording at home.
In this section, we'll cover a few tips on how to record effectively.
There are a few tools you should understand how to use within your DOW, which we'll outline here.
Use this section as a list of things to check out and find some tutorials for.
If there is demand for it, I'll create some tutorials on how to do the following inside Logic Pro.
You will be able to find tutorials on YouTube for how to do the following inside the DAW that you use.
Note, some entry-level DWs won't have all these features, but all top-level DAW will have them, or something very similar.
Buy a bass guitar.
Real bass is a great way to add some realism to your demos.
Buy a cheap guitar and use a software amplifier inside your DAW and record bass parts onto your songs.
It will feel a bit awkward at first, but it can be treated like an oversized guitar.
A bass guitar is great for songwriting and making demos.
Crossfades.
You will probably find that you record the song in sections rather than recording it all at once.
When moving from one section of the song to another, you want to record an overlapping section.
Say, for example, you are recording a verse that goes straight into the chorus.
You record the verse and then record the chorus.
When recording the chorus, start from the last few chords of the verse.
Then create a crossfade between the two sections.
A crossfade will fade out the first section while simultaneously fading in the new section.
This gives you a seamless transition across multiple recordings through the song.
Comping.
Most modern DAW will have what is called comping.
Learning how to use this will save you an enormous amount of time
and very quickly speed up the quality of your recordings.
Comping is recording on a loop.
You record multiple takes of the same section,
then choose the bits you want from each take.
When selecting the sections you want,
the DAW will automatically cross-fade between takes to create a seamless take.
In and out fades.
If you create a series of individual recordings within your DAW, you will notice that when you
play back, you get a small series of clicks at the start and end of each sound file.
You can overcome this by creating small fade-ins and fade-outs on each file.
You can do this with automation, not recommended, but many DAWs have the option for adding short
fades on the inspector for the audio file.
This is the best way to add these types of fades.
