paragraphs.ca: completar el teu projecte? Això és una cosa que vam tractar a l'apartat de què és possible en aquest moment. Pots demanar prestat equip a un amic? Anar a un estudi de pràctica i fer servir l'equip que hi ha?

paragraphs.en: Rent gear? Save up over time for a piece of gear? Make do with something that isn't quite as good? If the problem is operating your gear software, read the manual, ask a friend to help you, get help from a Facebook group forum, find someone who knows how to use it and get lessons, or find a book on Amazon. There are plenty of options. Figure something out and move forwards.
paragraphs.ca: Llogar equip? Estalviar amb el temps per a una peça d'equip? Arreglar-te amb una cosa que no és tan bona? Si el problema és fer funcionar el programari del teu equip, llegeix el manual, demana a un amic que t'ajudi, busca ajuda en un grup o fòrum de Facebook, troba algú que sàpiga fer-lo servir i pren classes, o busca un llibre a Amazon. Hi ha moltes opcions. Troba una solució i tira endavant.

paragraphs.en: Even if you aren't sure if you have a solution, give something a go, then evaluate and try again.
paragraphs.ca: Encara que no estiguis segur de tenir una solució, prova alguna cosa, després valora-ho i torna-ho a intentar.

paragraphs.en: Premature judgment. Sometimes we don't complete projects because we write off our ideas before they have had a chance to blossom. As guitar players, we often have a guitar-centric view of writing music. We write some guitar parts and then arrange the other instruments around that.
paragraphs.ca: Judici prematur. De vegades no acabem els projectes perquè descartem les nostres idees abans que hagin tingut l'oportunitat de florir. Com a guitarristes, sovint tenim una visió molt centrada en la guitarra a l'hora d'escriure música. Escrivim unes quantes parts de guitarra i després arreglem els altres instruments al voltant d'això.

paragraphs.en: There is nothing wrong with this approach. We'll look at it, and others, later when we look at creativity techniques. But it is important to remember that there are other instruments.
paragraphs.ca: Aquest enfocament no té res de dolent. El mirarem, a ell i a d'altres, més endavant, quan veiem les tècniques de creativitat. Però és important recordar que hi ha altres instruments.

paragraphs.en: Unless you are writing a piece where the guitar is the only instrument, you have to bear in mind that the guitar does not exist in a vacuum. Even the simplest riff, for example, a few power chords can sound incredible when matched with drums and bass guitar. There are plenty of great songs that do this. So next time you have an idea, don't write it off. Have your idea, work on your idea, maybe refine it, create some variations, add some context to your idea with other instruments,
paragraphs.ca: Tret que estiguis escrivint una peça en què la guitarra sigui l'únic instrument, has de tenir present que la guitarra no existeix al buit. Fins i tot el riff més senzill, per exemple uns quants power chords, pot sonar increïble quan s'hi afegeixen bateria i baix. Hi ha moltes cançons fantàstiques que ho fan. Així que la propera vegada que tinguis una idea, no la descartis. Tingues la idea, treballa-la, potser refina-la, crea'n algunes variacions, dona context a la teva idea amb altres instruments,

paragraphs.en: and then decide if you want to keep it or not. Only judge your idea once it is complete. I would go as far as not judging your ideas at all.
paragraphs.ca: i després decideix si vols quedar-te-la o no. Judica la teva idea només quan estigui acabada. Jo aniria fins i tot més enllà i no jutjaria les teves idees en absolut.

paragraphs.en: Occasionally I will trash an idea if it isn't working, but most of the time I'll keep working on my ideas until they're finished as a complete song.
paragraphs.ca: De tant en tant descarto una idea si no funciona, però la majoria de les vegades segueixo treballant les meves idees fins que estan acabades com una cançó completa.

paragraphs.en: Dealing with ideas Once you start having ideas, what should you do with them? I would recommend that you record the idea somehow, whether that is a tab or a recording.
paragraphs.ca: Què fer amb les idees. Un cop comences a tenir idees, què hauries de fer amb elles? Et recomanaria que enregistressis la idea d'alguna manera, ja sigui en una tablatura o en una gravació.

paragraphs.en: I try to put all my new ideas into a new Logic Pro project, then I can record them and have the tab all within the same program.
paragraphs.ca: Intento posar totes les meves idees noves en un projecte nou de Logic Pro; així les puc gravar i tenir la tablatura dins del mateix programa.

paragraphs.en: I can then easily work on it at a later date. Try and give your idea a file name that is more descriptive than New Idea 20 so you have some chance of remembering what it is when you next look at it.
paragraphs.ca: Així després hi puc treballar fàcilment en una data posterior. Intenta donar a la teva idea un nom de fitxer més descriptiu que «Idea nova 20», perquè tinguis alguna possibilitat de recordar què és la propera vegada que la miris.

paragraphs.en: And at a minimum, keep your new ideas inside the same folder on your computer. What do people listen to when they listen to music?
paragraphs.ca: I com a mínim, guarda les teves idees noves dins de la mateixa carpeta de l'ordinador. Què escolta la gent quan escolta música?

paragraphs.en: Before we think about recording our music, it's worth thinking about what the average person is listening to when they listen to music.
paragraphs.ca: Abans de pensar a gravar la nostra música, val la pena pensar en què escolta la persona mitjana quan escolta música.

paragraphs.en: There are two main things the average person is listening to when they listen to music. 1. Production quality. This is the guitar tone, quality of the mix, etc.
paragraphs.ca: Hi ha dues coses principals que la persona mitjana escolta quan escolta música. 1. La qualitat de producció. És el so de la guitarra, la qualitat de la mescla, etc.

paragraphs.en: 2. Timing. Do the instruments sound in time? Some genres defy these conventions, for example, punk and black metal. But even there, if you compare the successful commercial releases to the unsuccessful or more underground releases, you can see that these two factors are at play.
paragraphs.ca: 2. El timing. Sonen els instruments a temps? Alguns gèneres desafien aquestes convencions, per exemple el punk i el black metal. Però fins i tot aquí, si compares els llançaments comercials d'èxit amb els que no ho són o són més underground, veuràs que aquests dos factors hi tenen un paper.

paragraphs.en: So when it comes to recording our musical creations, we want to make sure that we can play in time, which should be a given if you've been practicing correctly, and we also want to make sure the production quality is as good as possible from getting a great tone to mixing.
paragraphs.ca: Així doncs, a l'hora de gravar les nostres creacions musicals, volem assegurar-nos que sabem tocar a temps, cosa que hauria de ser un fet si has practicat correctament, i també volem assegurar-nos que la qualitat de producció sigui tan bona com sigui possible, des d'aconseguir un bon so fins a la mescla.

paragraphs.en: Recording tips. Completing projects means that you're going to be doing a lot of recording, whether it's creating demos, going to a studio or recording at home.
paragraphs.ca: Consells de gravació. Completar projectes vol dir que gravaràs molt, ja sigui creant maquetes, anant a un estudi o gravant a casa.

paragraphs.en: In this section, we'll cover a few tips on how to record effectively. There are a few tools you should understand how to use within your DOW, which we'll outline here.
paragraphs.ca: En aquesta secció tractarem uns quants consells sobre com gravar eficaçment. Hi ha unes quantes eines que hauries de saber fer servir dins de la teva DAW, que descriurem aquí.

paragraphs.en: Use this section as a list of things to check out and find some tutorials for. If there is demand for it, I'll create some tutorials on how to do the following inside Logic Pro.
paragraphs.ca: Fes servir aquesta secció com una llista de coses per explorar i buscar-hi tutorials. Si hi ha demanda, crearé alguns tutorials sobre com fer les coses següents dins de Logic Pro.

paragraphs.en: You will be able to find tutorials on YouTube for how to do the following inside the DAW that you use. Note, some entry-level DWs won't have all these features, but all top-level DAW will have them, or something very similar.
paragraphs.ca: Podràs trobar tutorials a YouTube sobre com fer les coses següents dins de la DAW que facis servir. Nota: algunes DAW d'entrada no tindran totes aquestes funcions, però totes les DAW de primer nivell les tindran, o alguna cosa molt semblant.

paragraphs.en: Buy a bass guitar. Real bass is a great way to add some realism to your demos. Buy a cheap guitar and use a software amplifier inside your DAW and record bass parts onto your songs.
paragraphs.ca: Compra un baix. El baix real és una manera fantàstica d'afegir realisme a les teves maquetes. Compra una guitarra barata, fes servir un amplificador de programari dins de la teva DAW i grava parts de baix a les teves cançons.

paragraphs.en: It will feel a bit awkward at first, but it can be treated like an oversized guitar. A bass guitar is great for songwriting and making demos.
paragraphs.ca: Al principi et semblarà una mica estrany, però es pot tractar com una guitarra sobredimensionada. Un baix és fantàstic per compondre i fer maquetes.

paragraphs.en: Crossfades. You will probably find that you record the song in sections rather than recording it all at once. When moving from one section of the song to another, you want to record an overlapping section.
paragraphs.ca: Fundits encreuats. Probablement descobriràs que graves la cançó per seccions en lloc de gravar-la tota d'una vegada. Quan passes d'una secció de la cançó a una altra, convé gravar una secció que se superposi.

paragraphs.en: Say, for example, you are recording a verse that goes straight into the chorus. You record the verse and then record the chorus.
paragraphs.ca: Diguem, per exemple, que graves una estrofa que va directament a la tornada. Graves l'estrofa i després graves la tornada.

paragraphs.en: When recording the chorus, start from the last few chords of the verse. Then create a crossfade between the two sections.
paragraphs.ca: Quan gravis la tornada, comença pels últims acords de l'estrofa. Després crea un fundit encreuat entre les dues seccions.

paragraphs.en: A crossfade will fade out the first section while simultaneously fading in the new section. This gives you a seamless transition across multiple recordings through the song.
paragraphs.ca: Un fundit encreuat fa desaparèixer la primera secció mentre alhora apareix la nova secció. Això et dona una transició sense fissures entre diverses gravacions al llarg de la cançó.

paragraphs.en: Comping. Most modern DAW will have what is called comping. Learning how to use this will save you an enormous amount of time and very quickly speed up the quality of your recordings.
paragraphs.ca: Comping. La majoria de DAW modernes tenen el que s'anomena comping. Aprendre a fer-lo servir t'estalviarà una quantitat enorme de temps i millorarà molt de pressa la qualitat de les teves gravacions.

paragraphs.en: Comping is recording on a loop. You record multiple takes of the same section, then choose the bits you want from each take.
paragraphs.ca: El comping consisteix a gravar en bucle. Graves diverses preses de la mateixa secció i després tries els fragments que vols de cada presa.

paragraphs.en: When selecting the sections you want, the DAW will automatically cross-fade between takes to create a seamless take. In and out fades.
paragraphs.ca: Quan selecciones les seccions que vols, la DAW farà automàticament un fundit encreuat entre preses per crear una presa sense fissures. Fundits d'entrada i de sortida.

paragraphs.en: If you create a series of individual recordings within your DAW, you will notice that when you play back, you get a small series of clicks at the start and end of each sound file.
paragraphs.ca: Si crees una sèrie de gravacions individuals dins de la teva DAW, notaràs que quan les reprodueixes apareix una petita sèrie de clics a l'inici i al final de cada fitxer de so.

paragraphs.en: You can overcome this by creating small fade-ins and fade-outs on each file. You can do this with automation, not recommended, but many DAWs have the option for adding short fades on the inspector for the audio file.
paragraphs.ca: Ho pots resoldre creant petits fundits d'entrada i de sortida a cada fitxer. Ho pots fer amb automatització, cosa que no recomano, però moltes DAW tenen l'opció d'afegir fundits curts a l'inspector del fitxer d'àudio.

paragraphs.en: This is the best way to add these types of fades.
paragraphs.ca: Aquesta és la millor manera d'afegir aquest tipus de fundits.

segments.text: Order to record in.
When recording instruments, you usually want to record in the following order.
1. Drums
2. Bass
3. Rhythm guitars
4. Vocals
4. Vocals
5. Lead guitars
Microphone considerations.
Part of the tone you get when recording guitars will come from the microphone and the placement of the microphone.
Usually, an SM57 is the microphone of choice for recording guitars.
You may also want to use another microphone to capture the sound of the room.
This can add a nice ambience to your recording.
This ambience can also be added via a room modeling or reverb plugin.
For reference, Impetuous Desire was recorded using a single SM57 up close to the speaker,
Celestian Vintage 30 Speakers.
If you're going to a studio, they should have a selection of microphones and also understand how to use them.
This is part of what you pay for when going to a studio.
When using multiple microphones, you have to be aware of phase.
Again, in a studio, this is something that the engineer should be taking care of.
Phase can be thought of as how in time the microphones are with each other.
A quick Google of microphone phase will tell you all you need to know about this.
Tune the guitar for the range you're using.
The guitar is never exactly in tune.
Due to some physics and convenience reasons, the frets on a guitar are all in slightly the wrong place.
This is mostly compensated for by making sure the intonation is properly set,
something a guitar tech will do for you when getting your guitar set up, but the frets are still slightly out.
If you are playing a particular range on your guitar for a recording, you may find you get a sweeter sound by tuning your guitar to that range.
You will need a chromatic tuner for this.
For example, say you are playing a riff that is entirely around fret 7.
Tune your strings to the note on fret 7.

Fret 7 rather than the open string. You will find that the guitar sounds a bit nicer. Additionally, when tuning strings, make sure you pick them as hard as you will be playing them. Sometimes when tuning, guitarists will tickle the string. Then when it comes to playing, we'll go absolutely to town on them. Then tuning of the string changes ever so slightly the harder it is picked, so make sure you represent playing conditions when tuning.
Doubling rhythm parts
For almost every rock and metal song that you have ever listened to, the rhythm guitar has been doubled.
This means it was recorded twice.
One recording is panned slightly left, and the other recording is panned to the right.
This creates a wider and thicker sound.
When doing this, you need to make sure that both rhythm parts are precisely in time.
An easy way to check the timing is to listen back to the recording using headphones.
pan one recording to the left and one to the right.
If the rhythm part is in time,
you will hear the recording in the centre of the stereo field.
If the recording is out of time,
you will hear it bounce back and forth, left to right.
Give yourself extra time.
Things such as recording almost always take more time than you think they will.
If you're going to a studio, you will want a budget for this.
Some studios may be open to an arrangement where you book five days
and have the option to do two additional days at the end, or something to that effect.
Don't ask. Don't get.
However much time you give yourself, put a few extra days on the end, you'll probably need it.
If going to a studio, you can also ask the engineer for their opinion on how much time you should need.
Why use a studio?
There are three main benefits to using a recording studio.
1. The engineer
2. The gear
3. The focus
You get an engineer to operate the computer and set up the recording equipment.
They'll help you get a good tone from your amp and problem, solve any problems that will come up.
They can also give you a second opinion on any decisions that have to be made while recording.
An experienced engineer will have a lot of well experience.
So while you don't have to do what they say, they can have valuable input.
I always try to say something along the lines of I'll welcome their ideas but may decide differently.
All this allows you to focus on the guitar playing and let someone else deal with everything else.
Studios also have a ton of gear.
Nice amps are expensive and a studio will usually have a few amps that you can choose from.
This can help you get the best sound possible for your recording.
If you want session players, a studio will probably know people that can help you out.
I found the main vocalist for impetuous desire through the recording studio I used to record the album.
If you want a commercial quality recording, then go to a commercial studio.
Look at some albums you like.
They usually list the recording studio in the liner notes.
Look the studio up and ask for a quote.
The obvious downside to using a studio is the cost.
Studios can range from $180 per day to over $400 per day.
However, that's the price of getting a professional sound.
The last main benefit is the psychological benefit.
Often, our emotional states are partially tied to the location we are in.
Going to a studio gives you a focused, distraction-free environment
where you can fully apply yourself to the task at hand
and also have an emotionally blank slate.
Something as simple as having someone else operate the door
frees up your mind to focus on your playing.
Having someone there to give you instant feedback is also very helpful.
Personally, working with great professionals in a studio is something I love doing.
I'd recommend you try it at least once.
Two methods of recording.
There are two ways you can record a band, live or individually.
With live recording, the whole band is recorded live, sometimes without the singer.
Each instrument is mic'd up and there are often sound isolation panels between amplifiers and the drummer.
Solos are often added afterwards.
The benefit of recording this way is that you will get a more natural sound.
Often the vocalist will record their parts separately.
Apart from anything else, this helps save their voice.
A singer can't sing for the same amount of time that a guitarist can play.
Usually, singers are limited to being able to sing for a couple of hours a day before their voice gets tired.
By recording separately, the singer doesn't have to do the same parts over and over again when someone else in the band makes a mistake.
A downside to recording this way is that there will be bleed in every instrument.
Every instrument's microphone will pick up a bit of every other instrument.
Your band has to be very well rehearsed to do this.
The second method of recording is individual tracking.
This is where every part is recorded one at a time and layered on top of each other.
The benefits of recording this way are that you can get a pure signal for each instrument
and there won't be any problems with bleed.
You can also easily add recordings from other studios
if the musicians you are using are spread out across the world.
Control room and live room
Studios are usually split into two rooms, the control room and the live room.
The control room is where you and the engineer spend most of your time.
It has the mixing desk, monitors, computer, etc.
The live room is where the noise is made.
This is where your amplifiers will be, the drummer, the singer, etc.
When it comes to recording guitars, if you're recording individually,
Usually, you'll want the guitar head and effects in the control room and the speaker cabinet in the live room.
Studios will have cables going through the wall that you can use to send the signal from your head to the cab.
This will allow you to twiddle the amplifier settings and effects and perform without destroying your ears from your amplifier going full whack.
This also allows you to push a valve amplifier.
Valves tend to sound best when they are turned up loud.
The recording process.
There are a few steps to the recording process, so let's cover them one at a time.
Composition.
This is when you are composing your music.
You're figuring out what notes to use, the structure for the song,
what the lyrics will be if you're going to have lyrics, the instrumentation, etc.
Once you have your notes on a page or computer file, you are ready for the next step.
Demos.
This is creating a rough recording of your song, using whatever you have available at home.
This is sometimes done in tandem with the composition stage.
If you are writing riffs, etc. using your guitar, you will probably be recording them as you go.
Things don't need to be perfect at this stage, you are just getting everything recorded,
so you can get a rough idea of what your song will sound like.
Tracking
This is when you start working on the final recording.
You go through each instrument one at a time and take care to get a great recording for each part.
One effective method is to record in sections.
Record the rhythm guitar for the verse, then the chorus, etc.
If you can record the song in one go, do that.
You can record each section two or three times, then use the comping tool to select the best bits from each take.
Your engineer may do some editing at this level as you go.
Mixing
Once everything has been recorded, it is time for mixing.
Mixing is the art of making the music that you have recorded fit together.
This involves things like
1. Adding effects
2. EQing instruments
3. Setting the stereo balance
4. Setting levels
5. Adding any volume automation and fades
This stage can take several days and cost as much as the recording.
A single song can take a few hours to a day or two to mix.
An album can take a week or two to mix.
Mastering
This is the final stage in the audio creation of your music
and involves fine-tuning the EQ and effects at a song level.
The mastering engineer will take a stereo mix of your song,
so they will have two channels, left and right,
and create fine adjustments with EQ, compression, and other effects.
Mastering requirements will vary depending on the medium in which the song will be consumed.
For example, vinyl, radio and mp3 all have slightly different mastering requirements.
Marketing
How are you going to promote the song once it is done?
Are you going to promote it at all?
This can be anything from making a video of you playing the song at home and putting it on YouTube to concerts or paid ads online.
Whatever your project, I would recommend at least making a play-along video at home
If you went to a studio, you can make a play-along video in the studio
Or take a few cameras and make a studio music video
This is something I didn't do when recording Impetuous Desire, which was a huge mistake
Release
Everything is finally finished, and it's time to release your song
Congratulations, this is a huge achievement
I guess it's time to get started on the next one.
Preparing for a studio session.
When preparing for a studio recording session,
you want to plan out the song for the engineer.
The engineer will want to set up the project on their DAW.
This means entering the time signature and time signature changes.
They may want to add project markers to show the song sections.
Remember, this person won't know your songs as you do.
You can prepare all of this information beforehand to make their job as easy as possible.
Remember, the easier the engineer's job is, the more brainpower they can put into helping you record as well as possible,
rather than putting their brainpower into getting lost between verses and choruses.
You will want to make a list of
1. Song name
2. Tempo
3. Time signature
4. Sections and lengths in bars
5. Any changes in bars
in time signature or tempo and the bar at which that happens. As an example, here is a song sheet
I created for recording impetuous desire. I made one of these for every song. Song,
the path. Tempo, 140 BPM. Time, signature 4-4. Structure, intro, 8 bars, verse 1, 16 bars.
Chorus 8 bars
Re-intro 8 bars
Verse 2 16 bars
Chorus 8 bars
Re-intro 8 bars
Break 1 bar
Bridge 1 24 bars
Bridge 2 8 bars
Re-intro solo 1 8 bars
Outro solo 2 12 bars
We spent a few minutes at the start of the session putting this info into Cubase and then got busy recording.
You may not need all of this information, but it's always better to have this information to hand and not need it than need it and not have it.
You will also want to make sure that your equipment is ready.
At the least, this means getting new strings on your guitar and getting it set up would be better.
Get new batteries for your pedals and if your amp has any problems, get that scene to before you go to the studio.
Take spares of everything. You don't want to be halfway through a recording session and have a string break.
meaning you have to stop to go buy a new string.
You'll also want new picks.
New picks will have a slightly sharper edge than a used pick,
giving you better contact with the string.
In addition to preparing the song sheets,
you'll want to practice recording yourself at home.
Before you go to a recording studio,
simulate the experience at home and practice recording your songs.
Record your album, then delete it,
or copy and paste the DAW session and do it again.
This way, when you get to the recording studio, you'll be confident in your ability to perform.
Another trick you may find useful is to practice the songs you're going to play 5% to 10% faster than you want to record them.
Your ability on any given day fluctuates, so being able to play the songs faster than you need gives you some leeway with your ability.
Section 8. Techniques for being more creative with specific musical ideas.

paragraphs.ca: La fase es pot entendre com el grau de sincronia temporal entre els micròfons. Una cerca ràpida a Google sobre la fase dels micròfons et dirà tot el que necessites saber sobre això.

paragraphs.en: Tune the guitar for the range you're using. The guitar is never exactly in tune. Due to some physics and convenience reasons, the frets on a guitar are all in slightly the wrong place.
paragraphs.ca: Afina la guitarra per al registre que fas servir. La guitarra mai està exactament afinada. Per raons físiques i de comoditat, els trastes d'una guitarra estan tots en un lloc lleugerament equivocat.

paragraphs.en: This is mostly compensated for by making sure the intonation is properly set, something a guitar tech will do for you when getting your guitar set up, but the frets are still slightly out.
paragraphs.ca: Això es compensa en bona part assegurant que la afinació estigui ben ajustada, cosa que farà un tècnic de guitarres quan et posi a punt la guitarra, però els trastes encara queden una mica desviats.

paragraphs.en: If you are playing a particular range on your guitar for a recording, you may find you get a sweeter sound by tuning your guitar to that range.
paragraphs.ca: Si toques un registre concret de la teva guitarra per a un enregistrament, potser descobriràs que obtens un so més dolç afinant la guitarra per a aquest registre.

paragraphs.en: You will need a chromatic tuner for this. For example, say you are playing a riff that is entirely around fret 7. Tune your strings to the note on fret 7.
paragraphs.ca: Per això necessitaràs un afinador cromàtic. Per exemple, posem que toques un riff que està completament al voltant del traste 7. Afina les cordes a la nota del traste 7.

paragraphs.en: Fret 7 rather than the open string. You will find that the guitar sounds a bit nicer. Additionally, when tuning strings, make sure you pick them as hard as you will be playing them. Sometimes when tuning, guitarists will tickle the string. Then when it comes to playing, we'll go absolutely to town on them. Then tuning of the string changes ever so slightly the harder it is picked, so make sure you represent playing conditions when tuning.
paragraphs.ca: El traste 7 en lloc de la corda a l'aire. Descobriràs que la guitarra sona una mica més bé. A més, quan afinis les cordes, assegura't de fer-hi pua tan fort com hi tocaràs. De vegades, quan s'afina, els guitarristes acaricien la corda amb la pua. Després, a l'hora de tocar, hi van amb tota l'energia. L'afinació de la corda canvia lleugerament com més fort hi fas pua, així que assegura't de reproduir les condicions de tocada quan afinïs.

paragraphs.en: Doubling rhythm parts For almost every rock and metal song that you have ever listened to, the rhythm guitar has been doubled.
paragraphs.ca: Duplicar les parts rítmiques. Gairebé totes les cançons de rock i metal que hagis escoltat mai tenen la guitarra rítmica duplicada.

paragraphs.en: This means it was recorded twice. One recording is panned slightly left, and the other recording is panned to the right.
paragraphs.ca: Això vol dir que es va enregistrar dues vegades. Un enregistrament està desplaçat lleugerament a l'esquerra i l'altre està desplaçat a la dreta.

paragraphs.en: This creates a wider and thicker sound. When doing this, you need to make sure that both rhythm parts are precisely in time.
paragraphs.ca: Això crea un so més ampli i més gruixut. Quan ho facis, has d'assegurar-te que les dues parts rítmiques estiguin exactament ben quadrades en el temps.

paragraphs.en: An easy way to check the timing is to listen back to the recording using headphones. pan one recording to the left and one to the right.
paragraphs.ca: Una manera fàcil de comprovar el temps és escoltar l'enregistrament amb auriculars, desplaçant un enregistrament a l'esquerra i l'altre a la dreta.

paragraphs.en: If the rhythm part is in time, you will hear the recording in the centre of the stereo field. If the recording is out of time, you will hear it bounce back and forth, left to right.
paragraphs.ca: Si la part rítmica està ben quadrada, sentiràs l'enregistrament al centre del camp estèreo. Si l'enregistrament està desquadrat, el sentiràs rebotar d'un costat a l'altre, d'esquerra a dreta.

paragraphs.en: Give yourself extra time. Things such as recording almost always take more time than you think they will. If you're going to a studio, you will want a budget for this.
paragraphs.ca: Dóna't temps extra. Coses com enregistrar gairebé sempre triguen més del que penses. Si vas a un estudi, voldràs un pressupost per a això.

paragraphs.en: Some studios may be open to an arrangement where you book five days and have the option to do two additional days at the end, or something to that effect.
paragraphs.ca: Alguns estudis poden estar oberts a un acord en què reserves cinc dies i tens l'opció de fer dos dies addicionals al final, o alguna cosa semblant.

paragraphs.en: Don't ask. Don't get. However much time you give yourself, put a few extra days on the end, you'll probably need it. If going to a studio, you can also ask the engineer for their opinion on how much time you should need.
paragraphs.ca: Qui no demana, no obté. Sigui quin sigui el temps que et donis, afegeix-hi uns quants dies extra al final; probablement els necessitaràs. Si vas a un estudi, també pots demanar a l'enginyer la seva opinió sobre quant de temps hauries de necessitar.

paragraphs.en: Why use a studio? There are three main benefits to using a recording studio. 1. The engineer 2. The gear 3. The focus You get an engineer to operate the computer and set up the recording equipment.
paragraphs.ca: Per què fer servir un estudi? Hi ha tres beneficis principals d'utilitzar un estudi d'enregistrament. 1. L'enginyer 2. L'equip 3. La concentració. Tens un enginyer per fer anar l'ordinador i muntar l'equip d'enregistrament.

paragraphs.en: They'll help you get a good tone from your amp and problem, solve any problems that will come up. They can also give you a second opinion on any decisions that have to be made while recording.
paragraphs.ca: T'ajudarà a aconseguir un bon so del teu amplificador i resoldrà qualsevol problema que sorgeixi. També et pot donar una segona opinió sobre qualsevol decisió que s'hagi de prendre durant l'enregistrament.

paragraphs.en: An experienced engineer will have a lot of well experience. So while you don't have to do what they say, they can have valuable input.
paragraphs.ca: Un enginyer amb experiència tindrà molta experiència acumulada. Així que, tot i que no cal que facis el que diu, pot tenir aportacions valuoses.

paragraphs.en: I always try to say something along the lines of I'll welcome their ideas but may decide differently. All this allows you to focus on the guitar playing and let someone else deal with everything else.
paragraphs.ca: Jo sempre intento dir alguna cosa com: «Rebré les seves idees amb ganes, però potser decidiré diferent». Tot això et permet concentrar-te en la manera de tocar la guitarra i deixar que algú altre s'ocupi de tota la resta.

paragraphs.en: Studios also have a ton of gear. Nice amps are expensive and a studio will usually have a few amps that you can choose from.
paragraphs.ca: Els estudis també tenen una pila d'equip. Els bons amplificadors són cars i un estudi normalment en tindrà uns quants entre els quals pots triar.

paragraphs.en: This can help you get the best sound possible for your recording. If you want session players, a studio will probably know people that can help you out.
paragraphs.ca: Això et pot ajudar a aconseguir el millor so possible per al teu enregistrament. Si vols músics de sessió, un estudi probablement coneixerà gent que t'ho pot solucionar.

paragraphs.en: I found the main vocalist for impetuous desire through the recording studio I used to record the album. If you want a commercial quality recording, then go to a commercial studio.
paragraphs.ca: Vaig trobar la vocalista principal d'Impetuous Desire a través de l'estudi d'enregistrament que vaig fer servir per enregistrar l'àlbum. Si vols un enregistrament de qualitat comercial, ves a un estudi comercial.

paragraphs.en: Look at some albums you like. They usually list the recording studio in the liner notes. Look the studio up and ask for a quote.
paragraphs.ca: Mira alguns àlbums que t'agradin. Normalment hi consta l'estudi d'enregistrament a les notes del llibret. Busca l'estudi i demana un pressupost.

paragraphs.en: The obvious downside to using a studio is the cost. Studios can range from $180 per day to over $400 per day. However, that's the price of getting a professional sound.
paragraphs.ca: L'inconvenient evident d'utilitzar un estudi és el cost. Els estudis poden anar de 180 dòlars al dia fins a més de 400 dòlars al dia. Tanmateix, aquest és el preu d'aconseguir un so professional.

paragraphs.en: The last main benefit is the psychological benefit. Often, our emotional states are partially tied to the location we are in.
paragraphs.ca: L'últim benefici principal és el benefici psicològic. Sovint, els nostres estats emocionals estan parcialment lligats al lloc on som.

paragraphs.en: Going to a studio gives you a focused, distraction-free environment where you can fully apply yourself to the task at hand and also have an emotionally blank slate.
paragraphs.ca: Anar a un estudi et dóna un entorn concentrat i sense distraccions on pots aplicar-te plenament a la tasca que tens entre mans i també tenir la ment emocionalment en blanc.

paragraphs.en: Something as simple as having someone else operate the door frees up your mind to focus on your playing. Having someone there to give you instant feedback is also very helpful.
paragraphs.ca: Una cosa tan simple com que algú altre s'ocupi de la porta allibera la teva ment perquè es concentri en la teva manera de tocar. Tenir algú allà per donar-te retroalimentació instantània també és molt útil.

paragraphs.en: Personally, working with great professionals in a studio is something I love doing. I'd recommend you try it at least once.
paragraphs.ca: Personalment, treballar amb grans professionals en un estudi és una cosa que m'encanta fer. Et recomano que ho provis com a mínim una vegada.

paragraphs.en: Two methods of recording. There are two ways you can record a band, live or individually. With live recording, the whole band is recorded live, sometimes without the singer.
paragraphs.ca: Dues maneres d'enregistrar. Hi ha dues maneres d'enregistrar un grup: en directe o individualment. Amb l'enregistrament en directe, tot el grup s'enregistra en directe, de vegades sense el cantant.

paragraphs.en: Each instrument is mic'd up and there are often sound isolation panels between amplifiers and the drummer. Solos are often added afterwards.
paragraphs.ca: Cada instrument està microfonejat i sovint hi ha panells d'aïllament acústic entre els amplificadors i el bateria. Els solos sovint s'afegeixen després.

paragraphs.en: The benefit of recording this way is that you will get a more natural sound. Often the vocalist will record their parts separately.
paragraphs.ca: El benefici d'enregistrar així és que obtindràs un so més natural. Sovint la vocalista enregistra les seves parts per separat.

paragraphs.en: Apart from anything else, this helps save their voice. A singer can't sing for the same amount of time that a guitarist can play.
paragraphs.ca: Entre altres coses, això ajuda a estalviar la veu. Un cantant no pot cantar durant el mateix temps que un guitarrista pot tocar.

paragraphs.en: Usually, singers are limited to being able to sing for a couple of hours a day before their voice gets tired. By recording separately, the singer doesn't have to do the same parts over and over again when someone else in the band makes a mistake.
paragraphs.ca: Normalment, els cantants estan limitats a poder cantar un parell d'hores al dia abans que la seva veu es cansi. Enregistrant per separat, el cantant no ha de repetir les mateixes parts una vegada i una altra quan algú altre del grup comet un error.

paragraphs.en: A downside to recording this way is that there will be bleed in every instrument. Every instrument's microphone will pick up a bit of every other instrument.
paragraphs.ca: Un inconvenient d'enregistrar així és que hi haurà filtració a tots els instruments. El micròfon de cada instrument captarà una mica de tots els altres.

paragraphs.en: Your band has to be very well rehearsed to do this. The second method of recording is individual tracking. This is where every part is recorded one at a time and layered on top of each other.
paragraphs.ca: El teu grup ha d'estar molt ben assajat per fer això. La segona manera d'enregistrar és la gravació individual de pistes. És quan cada part s'enregistra d'una en una i es va superposant una sobre l'altra.

paragraphs.en: The benefits of recording this way are that you can get a pure signal for each instrument and there won't be any problems with bleed.
paragraphs.ca: Els beneficis d'enregistrar així són que pots obtenir un senyal pur per a cada instrument i no hi haurà cap problema de filtració.

paragraphs.en: You can also easily add recordings from other studios if the musicians you are using are spread out across the world.
paragraphs.ca: També pots afegir fàcilment enregistraments d'altres estudis si els músics que fas servir estan repartits pel món.

paragraphs.en: Control room and live room Studios are usually split into two rooms, the control room and the live room. The control room is where you and the engineer spend most of your time.
paragraphs.ca: Sala de control i sala en directe. Els estudis normalment es divideixen en dues sales: la sala de control i la sala en directe. La sala de control és on tu i l'enginyer passeu la major part del temps.

paragraphs.en: It has the mixing desk, monitors, computer, etc. The live room is where the noise is made. This is where your amplifiers will be, the drummer, the singer, etc.
paragraphs.ca: Hi ha la taula de mescles, els monitors, l'ordinador, etc. La sala en directe és on es fa el soroll. És on seran els teus amplificadors, el bateria, el cantant, etc.

paragraphs.en: When it comes to recording guitars, if you're recording individually, Usually, you'll want the guitar head and effects in the control room and the speaker cabinet in the live room.
paragraphs.ca: A l'hora d'enregistrar guitarres, si enregistres individualment, normalment voldràs el capçal de la guitarra i els efectes a la sala de control, i el bafle d'altaveus a la sala en directe.

paragraphs.en: Studios will have cables going through the wall that you can use to send the signal from your head to the cab. This will allow you to twiddle the amplifier settings and effects and perform without destroying your ears from your amplifier going full whack.
paragraphs.ca: Els estudis tindran cables que travessen la paret i que pots fer servir per enviar el senyal del capçal al bafle. Això et permetrà remenar la configuració de l'amplificador i els efectes i tocar sense destrossar-te les orelles amb l'amplificador a tot volum.

paragraphs.en: This also allows you to push a valve amplifier. Valves tend to sound best when they are turned up loud. The recording process.
paragraphs.ca: Això també et permet forçar un amplificador de vàlvules. Les vàlvules solen sonar millor quan estan pujades ben fort. El procés d'enregistrament.

paragraphs.en: There are a few steps to the recording process, so let's cover them one at a time. Composition. This is when you are composing your music.
paragraphs.ca: Hi ha uns quants passos en el procés d'enregistrament, així que tractem-los un per un. Composició. És quan compons la teva música.

paragraphs.en: You're figuring out what notes to use, the structure for the song, what the lyrics will be if you're going to have lyrics, the instrumentation, etc.
paragraphs.ca: Estàs esbrinant quines notes fer servir, l'estructura de la cançó, com seran les lletres si hi haurà lletres, la instrumentació, etc.

paragraphs.en: Once you have your notes on a page or computer file, you are ready for the next step.
paragraphs.ca: Un cop tens les notes en un full o en un fitxer d'ordinador, estàs a punt per al pas següent.

paragraphs.en: Demos. This is creating a rough recording of your song, using whatever you have available at home. This is sometimes done in tandem with the composition stage.
paragraphs.ca: Maquetes. Es tracta de crear un enregistrament aproximat de la teva cançó, fent servir el que tinguis disponible a casa. De vegades es fa alhora que l'etapa de composició.

paragraphs.en: If you are writing riffs, etc. using your guitar, you will probably be recording them as you go. Things don't need to be perfect at this stage, you are just getting everything recorded, so you can get a rough idea of what your song will sound like.
paragraphs.ca: Si escrius riffs, etc., amb la teva guitarra, probablement els aniràs enregistrant a mesura que avances. Les coses no cal que siguin perfectes en aquesta etapa; només ho enregistres tot per fer-te una idea aproximada de com sonarà la teva cançó.

paragraphs.en: Tracking This is when you start working on the final recording. You go through each instrument one at a time and take care to get a great recording for each part.
paragraphs.ca: Gravació de pistes. És quan comences a treballar en l'enregistrament final. Passes per cada instrument d'un en un i tens cura d'aconseguir un gran enregistrament per a cada part.

paragraphs.en: One effective method is to record in sections. Record the rhythm guitar for the verse, then the chorus, etc. If you can record the song in one go, do that.
paragraphs.ca: Un mètode efectiu és enregistrar per seccions. Enregistra la guitarra rítmica del vers, després la tornada, etc. Si pots enregistrar la cançó d'una tirada, fes-ho.

paragraphs.en: You can record each section two or three times, then use the comping tool to select the best bits from each take. Your engineer may do some editing at this level as you go.
paragraphs.ca: Pots enregistrar cada secció dues o tres vegades i després fer servir l'eina de comping per seleccionar els millors trossos de cada presa. El teu enginyer pot fer alguna edició en aquesta fase a mesura que avances.

paragraphs.en: Mixing Once everything has been recorded, it is time for mixing. Mixing is the art of making the music that you have recorded fit together.
paragraphs.ca: Mescla. Un cop tot està enregistrat, és hora de mesclar. La mescla és l'art de fer que la música que has enregistrat encaixi.

paragraphs.en: This involves things like 1. Adding effects 2. EQing instruments 3. Setting the stereo balance 4. Setting levels 5. Adding any volume automation and fades This stage can take several days and cost as much as the recording.
paragraphs.ca: Això implica coses com 1. Afegir efectes 2. Equalitzar els instruments 3. Ajustar l'equilibri estèreo 4. Ajustar els nivells 5. Afegir qualsevol automatització de volum i foses. Aquesta etapa pot trigar diversos dies i costar tant com l'enregistrament.

paragraphs.en: A single song can take a few hours to a day or two to mix. An album can take a week or two to mix.
paragraphs.ca: Una sola cançó pot trigar unes hores o un parell de dies a mesclar-se. Un àlbum pot trigar una setmana o dues a mesclar-se.

paragraphs.en: Mastering This is the final stage in the audio creation of your music and involves fine-tuning the EQ and effects at a song level.
paragraphs.ca: Masterització. Aquesta és l'última etapa en la creació d'àudio de la teva música i consisteix a ajustar finament l'equalització i els efectes a nivell de cançó.

paragraphs.en: The mastering engineer will take a stereo mix of your song, so they will have two channels, left and right, and create fine adjustments with EQ, compression, and other effects.
paragraphs.ca: L'enginyer de masterització agafarà una mescla estèreo de la teva cançó, de manera que tindrà dos canals, esquerre i dret, i farà ajustos fins amb equalització, compressió i altres efectes.

paragraphs.en: Mastering requirements will vary depending on the medium in which the song will be consumed. For example, vinyl, radio and mp3 all have slightly different mastering requirements.
paragraphs.ca: Els requisits de masterització varien segons el mitjà en què es consumirà la cançó. Per exemple, el vinil, la ràdio i l'mp3 tenen tots requisits de masterització una mica diferents.

paragraphs.en: Marketing How are you going to promote the song once it is done? Are you going to promote it at all? This can be anything from making a video of you playing the song at home and putting it on YouTube to concerts or paid ads online.
paragraphs.ca: Màrqueting. Com promocionaràs la cançó un cop estigui feta? La promocionaràs d'alguna manera? Això pot ser qualsevol cosa, des de fer un vídeo tocant la cançó a casa i penjar-lo a YouTube fins a concerts o anuncis pagats en línia.

paragraphs.en: Whatever your project, I would recommend at least making a play-along video at home If you went to a studio, you can make a play-along video in the studio Or take a few cameras and make a studio music video This is something I didn't do when recording Impetuous Desire, which was a huge mistake Release Everything is finally finished, and it's time to release your song Congratulations, this is a huge achievement I guess it's time to get started on the next one.
paragraphs.ca: Sigui quin sigui el teu projecte, et recomanaria com a mínim fer un vídeo de play-along a casa. Si vas anar a un estudi, pots fer un vídeo de play-along a l'estudi. O agafar unes quantes càmeres i fer un videoclip d'estudi. Això és una cosa que no vaig fer quan vaig enregistrar Impetuous Desire, cosa que va ser un gran error. Publicació. Finalment tot està acabat, i és hora de publicar la teva cançó. Enhorabona, és una fita enorme. Suposo que és hora de començar la següent.

paragraphs.en: Preparing for a studio session. When preparing for a studio recording session, you want to plan out the song for the engineer.
paragraphs.ca: Preparar una sessió d'estudi. Quan et prepares per a una sessió d'enregistrament en un estudi, voldràs planificar la cançó per a l'enginyer.

paragraphs.en: The engineer will want to set up the project on their DAW. This means entering the time signature and time signature changes.
paragraphs.ca: L'enginyer voldrà muntar el projecte al seu DAW. Això vol dir introduir el compàs i els canvis de compàs.

paragraphs.en: They may want to add project markers to show the song sections. Remember, this person won't know your songs as you do. You can prepare all of this information beforehand to make their job as easy as possible.
paragraphs.ca: Potser voldrà afegir marcadors de projecte per mostrar les seccions de la cançó. Recorda que aquesta persona no coneixerà les teves cançons com les coneixes tu. Pots preparar tota aquesta informació per endavant per facilitar-li la feina tant com sigui possible.

paragraphs.en: Remember, the easier the engineer's job is, the more brainpower they can put into helping you record as well as possible, rather than putting their brainpower into getting lost between verses and choruses.
paragraphs.ca: Recorda: com més fàcil sigui la feina de l'enginyer, més capacitat mental podrà posar a ajudar-te a enregistrar el millor possible, en lloc de posar-la a perdre's entre versos i tornades.

paragraphs.en: You will want to make a list of 1. Song name 2. Tempo 3. Time signature 4. Sections and lengths in bars 5. Any changes in bars in time signature or tempo and the bar at which that happens. As an example, here is a song sheet I created for recording impetuous desire. I made one of these for every song. Song, the path. Tempo, 140 BPM. Time, signature 4-4. Structure, intro, 8 bars, verse 1, 16 bars.
paragraphs.ca: Voldràs fer una llista de 1. Nom de la cançó 2. Tempo 3. Compàs 4. Seccions i durades en compassos 5. Qualsevol canvi de compàs o de tempo i el compàs on es produeix. Com a exemple, aquí tens un full de cançó que vaig crear per enregistrar Impetuous Desire. En vaig fer un per a cada cançó. Cançó: The Path. Tempo: 140 BPM. Compàs: 4-4. Estructura: intro, 8 compassos, vers 1, 16 compassos.

paragraphs.en: Chorus 8 bars Re-intro 8 bars Verse 2 16 bars Chorus 8 bars Re-intro 8 bars Break 1 bar Bridge 1 24 bars Bridge 2 8 bars Re-intro solo 1 8 bars Outro solo 2 12 bars We spent a few minutes at the start of the session putting this info into Cubase and then got busy recording.
paragraphs.ca: Tornada 8 compassos. Reintro 8 compassos. Vers 2 16 compassos. Tornada 8 compassos. Reintro 8 compassos. Break 1 compàs. Pont 1 24 compassos. Pont 2 8 compassos. Reintro solo 1 8 compassos. Outro solo 2 12 compassos. Vam passar uns quants minuts al principi de la sessió introduint aquesta informació a Cubase i després ens vam posar a enregistrar.

paragraphs.en: You may not need all of this information, but it's always better to have this information to hand and not need it than need it and not have it.
paragraphs.ca: Potser no necessitaràs tota aquesta informació, però sempre és millor tenir-la a mà i no necessitar-la que necessitar-la i no tenir-la.

paragraphs.en: You will also want to make sure that your equipment is ready. At the least, this means getting new strings on your guitar and getting it set up would be better.
paragraphs.ca: També voldràs assegurar-te que el teu equip estigui a punt. Com a mínim, això vol dir posar cordes noves a la guitarra, i encara millor, posar-la a punt.

paragraphs.en: Get new batteries for your pedals and if your amp has any problems, get that scene to before you go to the studio. Take spares of everything. You don't want to be halfway through a recording session and have a string break.
paragraphs.ca: Posa piles noves als pedals i, si el teu amplificador té algun problema, fes-lo reparar abans d'anar a l'estudi. Porta recanvis de tot. No vols trobar-te a mitja sessió d'enregistrament amb una corda trencada

paragraphs.en: meaning you have to stop to go buy a new string. You'll also want new picks. New picks will have a slightly sharper edge than a used pick, giving you better contact with the string.
paragraphs.ca: que et faci haver d'aturar-ho tot per anar a comprar una corda nova. També voldràs pues noves. Les pues noves tenen la punta una mica més afilada que una pua usada, cosa que et dóna un millor contacte amb la corda.

paragraphs.en: In addition to preparing the song sheets, you'll want to practice recording yourself at home. Before you go to a recording studio, simulate the experience at home and practice recording your songs.
paragraphs.ca: A més de preparar els fulls de cançó, voldràs practicar enregistrar-te a casa. Abans d'anar a un estudi d'enregistrament, simula l'experiència a casa i practica enregistrant les teves cançons.

paragraphs.en: Record your album, then delete it, or copy and paste the DAW session and do it again. This way, when you get to the recording studio, you'll be confident in your ability to perform.
paragraphs.ca: Enregistra el teu àlbum, després esborra'l, o copia i enganxa la sessió del DAW i torna-ho a fer. D'aquesta manera, quan arribis a l'estudi d'enregistrament, tindràs confiança en la teva capacitat d'interpretar.

paragraphs.en: Another trick you may find useful is to practice the songs you're going to play 5% to 10% faster than you want to record them.

chapters.title: Section 8. Techniques for being more creative with specific musical ideas

segments.text: Section 8. Techniques for being more creative with specific musical ideas.
We have covered a lot of ground on practice, study and general approaches to improving your playing.
Let's look at some specific techniques you can use to be more creative.
One of the biggest roadblocks to creativity that people face is the blank page.
Staring at a blank piece of paper and thinking, well, what do I do now?
The first thing to do in this situation is to give yourself a set of limitations.
Decide on the 1. Form, 2. Key, 3. Harmony and harmonic progressions, 4. Type of melody, fast,
lyrical, ornamented, etc. Once you have those constraints, the music usually writes itself.
All you have to do is take the theory you have learned from studying and apply it to solving
the problem that you have outlined for yourself. Also, you don't have to stick to these constraints.
If you use these constraints to get started, but find the music going somewhere different,
go with it and see where the music takes you.
A good way to unlock a new source of creativity is to take a different approach to the order
in which you compose parts for instruments.
For example, guitar players tend to compose the guitar part first, and everything else
in the song is structured around the guitar part.
What if you tried writing a bass riff first, or lyrics, or a vocal melody, or a drum pattern?
You will find that by composing for different instruments,
your mind will be forced to work a bit differently from usual,
and as a result, you will come up with new and interesting ideas.
Here are a few ideas on specific areas of composition
that you can use to help you write more ideas.
Hopefully, these also show why knowing a little theory can be a powerful thing.
melody when it comes to writing melodies there are a few approaches that we can
take
Before deciding on an approach, it's worth thinking about the type of melody that you want to compose. Do you want to compose a...
1. Song melody. 2. Motivic melody. 3. Chant melody. 4. Virtuosic melody. Arpeggiating a chord progression.
One approach to composing music is to start with a theoretical model, which gets expanded upon before realizing the music.
Let's say that we had constructed the following model.
Figure 12, notated chords, and we wanted some ideas on how to arpeggiate it.
Sometimes a student will get stuck at this stage.
What note in the melody do I start with?
Where do I go from there?
The terror of the blank page has struck again.
However, if we create a graphical representation of what we are dealing with,
we can quickly, in seconds, create dozens of variations.
Each chord in the above model has a top note, middle note, and bass note.
We could represent this on the following diagram.
I call this diagram an arpeggiation map.
Figure 13, Melody Template.
We can then simply draw a line to represent how we want to move between the bass, middle, and top notes.
Figure 14, Melody Sketch, which would give us the following melody.
Figure 15, Notated Melody.
If you are unsure how we went from the diagram to the notated arpeggiation,
match up the notes in the chord, top stave, with the red lines in the arpeggiation map.
Drawing lines on an arpeggiation map is pretty easy.
You could probably make a dozen or so of those in under two minutes.
You can then translate those into all sorts of arpeggiations of your model.
You can then add non-harmonic tones or edit the rhythm as you see fit.
Non-harmonic tone and rhythm first approach to melody
An alternative approach to composing melodic ideas
is to focus instead on the rhythm and type of non-harmonic tones
that you want to use in the melody.
Let's assume that we want to write a melody that is one bar long.
Choose a time signature, then write out rhythms that fill up a bar.
Let's use 4-4.
Here is an example of four rhythms we could use.
Figure 16, Rhythms
Let's then choose four different ways we can combine pairs of non-harmonic tones
1. Passing tones and neighbor tones
2. Reaching tones and neighbor tones
3. Reaching tones and escape tones
4. Passing tones and reaching tones
Let's assume that we are playing over an AM harmony
and then we can then match up the pairs of non-harmonic tones with different rhythms as follows
Figure 17, Melody with Rhythms
There are a couple of things to note here.
These examples are just one possible example.
We could have found dozens of ways to combine these rhythms and non-harmonic tones.
Example 3 only contains a reaching tone.
There were not enough notes to add an escape tone.
If things don't work out exactly, that's okay.
Earlier in the book, we talked about two ideas.
One, the importance of studying theory.
2. How creativity can be seen as a way of combining theoretical ideas.
Hopefully, these examples are starting to illustrate how easy it can be to be creative
when you have studied the theory in depth and when then start creating scenarios in which to apply it.
Vocal approach to melody writing.
A great way to approach melody writing, especially for instrumental music,
is to use your voice to compose the melody.
It's easy to get very self-conscious when using your voice,
so try and find somewhere where you are by yourself to try this out, or hum.
It's easier to hum a pitch correctly than it is to sing it.
Take a simple chord progression, loop it,
and then use your voice to improvise a melody over the chords.
I approached the song Longing on impetuous desire this way.
I wrote a simple chord progression on guitar, I think it was just two chords,
then looped them and hummed random notes until I found the note I wanted.
That was the first note on the cello.
I then restarted the loop, hummed the first note,
and then hummed to other notes until I found the next note that fitted.
I now had two notes, and so on and so on, until I had the entire melody.
You can apply this to guitar melodies,
using this method to compose the fundamental notes of the melody.
You can then, if you want, make the melody more complex by changing how those notes are ornamented,
adding arpeggios and scale ideas around those fundamental pitches.
This is a great way to get a highly melodic melody.
Warning on melody writing.
The first time guitar players approach writing melodies, they, more often than not, add too many notes.
They end up vomiting notes on the page with straight 16th notes everywhere.
This often comes from insecurity around the perceived complexity of the idea.
Remember, melodies do not need to be complex to be enjoyable.
Sure, write a complex melody if it serves the music, but don't add notes for the sake of it.
If you find you always write melodies in straight sixteenths or something similar,
try challenging yourself by restricting yourself to different types of rhythms.
The non-harmonic tone and rhythm first approach that is outlined above would be a great exercise for you
Using your voice to improvise a melody would also be a great exercise
As the voice cannot sing as fast as we can play on guitar
Writing chord progressions and strumming patterns
Free writing chord progressions for a song
We're writing a song and songs have a structure
So to get started, let's make up a simple structure
Verse, chorus, verse, chorus, bridge, chorus.
Let's start by restricting ourselves to a particular key, say E minor.
Let's first look at the chords in E minor.
E minor, F sharp diminished, G, A minor, B minor, C and D.
We'll ignore possible chromatic chords, modal mixture and other minor chords,
restricting ourselves to the natural minor scale outlined above.
To make things easier for ourselves, let's also ignore the F-sharp diminished chord, which is a bit harder to use.
Ignoring the F-sharp diminished leaves us with six chords, E minor, G, A minor, B minor, C and D.
Now let's take four of these chords at random.
Pick four different chords to what I choose so that you can see this method works for yourself.
First progression, E minor, C, G, A minor.
Let's repeat that process to write a second chord progression.
Second progression.
C, B minor, E minor, C.
Finally, let's write a third chord progression that is only two chords long,
but will have each chord last two bars.
Third progression.
A minor, A minor, D, D.
Figure 18.
Rhythms for chords.
Next, we need some rhythms that we can use with these chord progressions.
Let's use a mixture of eighth notes and quarter notes
We'll use chord progression 1 and rhythm 1 as a verse
Chord progression 2 and rhythm 2 as a chorus
And chord progression 3 and rhythm 3 as a bridge
And hey presto, we now have a song
Figure 19, song example
Sure, it might not be the greatest song in the world
But it's a start
And it wasn't exactly difficult to write
And most importantly, it sounds like a song
Once you have a basic outline as we have above, you can then start picking at it,
deciding what you like, what you don't like, and editing it into a song that you do like.
Using functional harmony to write chord progressions
The Common Practice Period, CPP, is an era of music that most people know as classical music.
It was when great composers, such as Mozart and Beethoven, were alive.
One of the conventions that was followed for writing harmonic progressions, what guitar
players often understand as chord progressions, is called functional harmony. This is a method for
deciding what chord comes next. To give a very brief overview, there is a lot, lot more to
functional harmony which warrants an entire course. We use numerals to label the chords from the major
scale. C major, C, D minor, E minor, F, G, A minor, B diminished. Numeral 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7.
C major is the I chord. D minor is the II chord. E minor is the III chord. F is the IV chord. G
is the V chord. A minor is the VI chord. B diminished is the VII chord. Note 1. With this
audiobook version, the numerals are a bit lost and make more sense on the page. Note 2. Numerals
give us a way to analyze chord progressions by looking at the relationship of a chord to its
scale rather than the chord by itself. For example, using numerals, we can think of D minor as being
the second chord in a C major scale rather than thinking of it as the pitches D, F, and A. The
The chord numerals are then organized into tonic, subdominant and dominant.
Table 1, chord categories.
Generally speaking, we move from left to right through the table.
We can skip chords when moving right.
We can only move left when moving from dominant to tonic.
For example, first progression.
Second progression.
Third progression. One, six, four, five. If you take your guitar and try playing these
progressions, you should find they have quite a structured slash logical slash classical sound to
them, especially if you pay attention to the voice leading. Are you starting to see the benefits of
in-depth study now? When you understand functional harmony, voice leading, and form, composing can
almost be boiled down to following some rules, creating some progressions, and then filling in
the gaps with some notes. Now, there is a lot, lot more to functional harmony than this. But as I
mentioned before, that would be an entire course and outside the scope of this book. We could use
functional harmony combined with the rhythm and structure ideas from the previous example
to write a song. First progression 1, 6, 4, 2, 7, 5, 1. C major, C, A minor, F, D minor, B diminished,
G, C. Second progression 1, 2, 5, 1. C major, C, D minor, G, C. Third progression 1, 6, 4, 5.
C major, C, A minor, F, G, which would give us the following song.
Figure 20, song using functional harmony.
Again, from here we can start editing to get it more the way we want it,
or adding to the structure, other instruments, etc.
Improvised ideas when writing.
Usually, most guitarists approach songwriting by improvising ideas on their guitar.
Why not put your improvisational skills to use in a different medium?
You could try starting with a bass guitar and improvising a bass idea,
then arrange the guitar and drums around your bass idea.
You could try starting by writing a cool drum pattern that you then write guitar and bass over.
Maybe you start with a vocal melody or work with a singer and then compose around the vocals.
Putting your improvisation skills to work with different instruments, even if you aren't very
good at them, will quickly give you new ideas that you work with for your songwriting.
I would strongly recommend buying a bass guitar, even if it's a cheap one. Mine was £100. They
are great for coming up with ideas, and also for making demos of your musical ideas.
Principles behind the above creativity ideas
The above ideas are great, but what is important is that you understand the principle behind the
ideas, so that you can not only use these creativity tools effectively, but create your own.
We are taking a specific element of music, whether it's chord tone melodies, chord progressions,
rhythm in melody, etc., thinking of several variations of that aspect of music,
then taking those variations and fleshing them out into complete ideas.
You can also see how important it is to have a good grasp of music theory,
and how understanding music theory can immensely aid creativity.

paragraphs.en: Improvised ideas when writing. Usually, most guitarists approach songwriting by improvising ideas on their guitar. Why not put your improvisational skills to use in a different medium?
paragraphs.ca: Idees improvisades a l'hora d'escriure. Normalment, la majoria de guitarristes enfoquen la composició de cançons improvisant idees amb la guitarra. Per què no posar les teves habilitats d'improvisació al servei d'un altre mitjà?

paragraphs.en: You could try starting with a bass guitar and improvising a bass idea, then arrange the guitar and drums around your bass idea.
paragraphs.ca: Podries provar de començar amb un baix elèctric i improvisar una idea de baix, i després arreglar la guitarra i la bateria al voltant de la teva idea de baix.

paragraphs.en: You could try starting by writing a cool drum pattern that you then write guitar and bass over. Maybe you start with a vocal melody or work with a singer and then compose around the vocals.
paragraphs.ca: Podries provar de començar escrivint un patró de bateria xulo sobre el qual després escriure guitarra i baix. Potser comences amb una melodia vocal o treballes amb un cantant i després compondre al voltant de la veu.

paragraphs.en: Putting your improvisation skills to work with different instruments, even if you aren't very good at them, will quickly give you new ideas that you work with for your songwriting.
paragraphs.ca: Posa les teves habilitats d'improvisació a treballar amb instruments diferents, encara que no siguis gaire bo amb ells: de seguida et donaran idees noves amb què treballar per a les teves cançons.

paragraphs.en: I would strongly recommend buying a bass guitar, even if it's a cheap one. Mine was £100. They are great for coming up with ideas, and also for making demos of your musical ideas.
paragraphs.ca: Et recomanaria fermament comprar un baix elèctric, encara que sigui barat. El meu va costar 100 lliures. Van molt bé per treure idees i també per fer maquetes de les teves idees musicals.

paragraphs.en: Principles behind the above creativity ideas The above ideas are great, but what is important is that you understand the principle behind the ideas, so that you can not only use these creativity tools effectively, but create your own.
paragraphs.ca: Els principis darrere de les idees de creativitat anteriors. Les idees anteriors són genials, però l'important és que entenguis el principi que hi ha darrere de les idees, perquè no només puguis fer servir aquestes eines de creativitat amb eficàcia, sinó també crear les teves pròpies.

paragraphs.en: We are taking a specific element of music, whether it's chord tone melodies, chord progressions, rhythm in melody, etc., thinking of several variations of that aspect of music, then taking those variations and fleshing them out into complete ideas.
paragraphs.ca: Agafem un element concret de la música, sigui melodies de notes d'acord, progressions d'acords, ritme en la melodia, etc., pensem en diverses variacions d'aquest aspecte de la música i després agafem aquestes variacions i les desenvolupem fins a convertir-les en idees completes.

paragraphs.en: You can also see how important it is to have a good grasp of music theory, and how understanding music theory can immensely aid creativity.
paragraphs.ca: També pots veure com d'important és dominar bé la teoria musical i com entendre-la pot ajudar enormement la creativitat.

chapters.title: Section 9. Final thoughts on creativity

segments.text: Section 9. Final thoughts on creativity.
Can anyone learn anything?
We've spent an entire book discussing how you can become more creative.
But are there any limits on the levels you can reach,
or on the levels of creative achievement that people can reach in general?
The answer is, sort of.
This has a bit to do with IQ.
One thing that IQ affects is the speed at which someone can learn and understand complex information.
To put it another way, someone with a high IQ can learn complex things quickly.
Someone with a low IQ will take a long time to learn complex things.
I believe anyone with an average or even below average IQ can become an expert at something over the course of their life.
Only people with a high IQ will be able to become experts in multiple fields over the course of their life.
This is due to the practical limit of how long we live.
The rate at which we learn, the time we spend learning, and the length of our lives determine the number of fields in which we can become an expert.
And we only have so much time.
It's also worth noting that IQ can be increased.
learning is simply recognizing how concepts fit together.
If you can train your mind to think more conceptually
you can increase your IQ.
If you've managed to read this far in the book
you have enough intelligence to become an expert level guitarist composer.

When considering this, it is also important to factor in time. If you do take a long time to learn something, but you increase the time you spend each day on it, then you will learn as fast, or even faster, than someone who is theoretically more intelligent.
The old idiom of hard work beats talent when talent doesn't work hard has some truth to it.
The first four hours of your day define your life. I have a pet theory I've been considering
over the last couple of years. The first four hours of your day define your life. The first
four hours of your day are your best time of day. Your brain is alert and you can focus for
extended periods. The most effective way to get better at guitar and writing music is to wake up
and spend your morning working on it. Now doing four hours might be difficult if you have a job,
But if you can, go to bed earlier and wake up earlier, so you can put an hour or two into music.
You will see that you improve quickly.
I wanted to write this book, so the first one to two hours of my day for the last few months have been put into writing this book,
followed by a couple of hours of guitar practice.
If the guitar and music are something you want to work on full-time,
you will have to figure out a way to either make more money with less time or make money from playing the guitar.
Progress is not accidental. Hopefully, now you are starting to see that.
1. Progress is not accidental.
2. Great guitarists are not born, they are made.
Every great guitarist has a story about the hours and hours of practice time they put into their instrument.
If you replicate that, you will replicate the results.
Practice doesn't magically happen. It has to be planned, scheduled and prioritized in your life.
Creativity as a path to happiness
Is it possible to be too happy?
What do we mean when we talk about happiness?
We're not talking about some drug-like state of deliriousness,
but more a state of satisfaction or contentedness
that runs through our lives like a backing track.
Human beings survive via production.
This is an unavoidable fact of life.
When you can spend your productive time, or at least some of it,
creating something you love, you will gain a piece of happiness. A fundamental part of being human
is problem-solving. Some writers have described man as a teleological being. This means goal-orientated.
Setting yourself a challenge and then overcoming it is a fundamental part of being human,
and when we act in accordance with our nature, we tend to feel good. Composing, recording,
and releasing a piece of music takes a lot of work. Composing a piece of music is an incredible
feat of problem solving. It involves pushing your mind to see what it's capable of and then
concretizing a range of concepts so you can create a physical representation of what your mind can do.
By physical, we mean existing in a format that others can perceive.
As such, I believe that taking guitar seriously and creating music can be a great way to be happier.
I certainly find that I'm at my happiest when creating and recording music.

paragraphs.en: I certainly find that I'm at my happiest when creating and recording music.
paragraphs.ca: Jo, certament, trobo que estic més feliç quan creo i gravo música.
